```tsx
        {plan.features.map((feature) => (
          <li key={feature} style={{ display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
            <Check style={{ width: 16, height: 16, color: "var(--color-text-success-soft)" }} />
            {feature}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </Card.Content>
    <Card.Footer style={{ marginTop: "auto", paddingTop: 4 }}>
      <Button
        color={plan.highlighted ? "primary" : "secondary"}
        variant={plan.highlighted ? "solid" : "outline"}
        block
      >
        Choose {plan.name}
      </Button>
    </Card.Footer>
  </Card>
))}
</div>
```

## Checkbox
Checkbox for binary on/off selection with solid, pill, and ghost variants, an indeterminate state, and rich labels with inline descriptions.
Import: import { Checkbox } from "@plexui/ui/components/Checkbox"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/checkbox
Props:
  - variant ("solid" | "ghost") default: "solid" — Visual style: solid (filled background) or ghost (checkmark only)
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded indicator corners
  - checked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Controlled state
  - defaultChecked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Initial state (uncontrolled)
  - onCheckedChange ((next: boolean) => void) — Called with the next state when it changes
  - label (ReactNode) — Accessible label. Accepts ReactNode for rich content
  - description (ReactNode) — Second line below the label, linked via aria-describedby. Renders only with a label
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent interaction
  - required (boolean) — Required for form submission
  - name (string) — Form field name
  - value (string) default: "on" — Value when submitted
  - orientation ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Checkbox position relative to the label
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the wrapper node
  - id (string) — The id of the checkbox element (generated when omitted)
  - onFocus ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the checkbox gains focus
  - onBlur ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the checkbox loses focus

### Overview
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox label="Same as billing address" />
<Checkbox label="Subscribe to newsletter" defaultChecked />
</div>
```

### With Radio Group
Place Checkbox alongside RadioGroup controls to verify that indicator sizes, label baselines, and spacing align consistently in both horizontal and vertical layouts. This check is desktop only: on a phone both live in rows, where the radio is a checkmark and the checkbox a circle at the end of the row.
```tsx
const channels = [
{ value: "email", label: "Email", description: "Messages delivered to your inbox." },
{ value: "sms", label: "SMS", description: "Text messages to your phone number." },
{ value: "push", label: "Push", description: "Real-time alerts on your device." },
]
const topics = [
{ label: "Product updates", description: "New features and improvements.", checked: true },
{ label: "Security alerts", description: "Account activity and login notifications.", checked: true },
{ label: "Community", description: "Events, meetups, and discussions.", checked: false },
]

<div className="flex flex-col gap-6 w-full max-w-md">
<Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
  {() => (
    <RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="email" aria-label="Notification channel">
      {channels.map((channel) => (
        <RadioGroup.Item key={channel.value} value={channel.value}>
          <div className="flex flex-col">
            <span className="font-medium">{channel.label}</span>
            <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">{channel.description}</span>
          </div>
        </RadioGroup.Item>
      ))}
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field label="Topics" description="Select the topics you want to follow.">
  {() => (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
      {topics.map((topic) => (
        <Checkbox
          key={topic.label}
          defaultChecked={topic.checked}
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">{topic.label}</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">{topic.description}</span>
            </div>
          }
        />
      ))}
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Descriptions
Combine Field-level label and description with item-level descriptions for options that need additional context. Use a plain label without descriptions when the options are self-explanatory. On a phone the group title, its description and row descriptions do this, as Group with description and Grouped sections show, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
const [settings, setSettings] = useState({
projects: true,
members: true,
csv: true,
json: false,
pdf: false,
})
const toggle = (key: keyof typeof settings) => () =>
setSettings((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: !prev[key] }))

<div className="flex flex-col max-w-sm w-full divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Export contents" description="Choose what the archive includes.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">Projects</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Files, comments, and version history.</span>
            </div>
          }
          checked={settings.projects}
          onCheckedChange={toggle("projects")}
        />
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">Members</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Names, roles, and email addresses.</span>
            </div>
          }
          checked={settings.members}
          onCheckedChange={toggle("members")}
        />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="File formats">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <Checkbox label="CSV" checked={settings.csv} onCheckedChange={toggle("csv")} />
        <Checkbox label="JSON" checked={settings.json} onCheckedChange={toggle("json")} />
        <Checkbox label="PDF" checked={settings.pdf} onCheckedChange={toggle("pdf")} />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

### Variants
The checkbox supports three visual styles: solid (default) with a filled background and standard radius, solid pill with fully rounded corners, and ghost, which renders only the checkmark without a border or background fill. Toggle disabled without resetting checked or indeterminate states. On a phone with touch.css a solid checkbox is the 22px selection circle of iOS with or without pill, so the phone view leaves out the solid pill group. A ghost checkbox is the checkmark of an iOS list row.
```tsx
const [disabled, setDisabled] = useState(false)

<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-x-12 gap-y-6">
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">solid</span>
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Unchecked" />
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Checked" defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Indeterminate" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">solid pill</span>
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Unchecked" pill />
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Checked" pill defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Indeterminate" pill checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start">
  <span className="text-xs text-secondary font-mono mb-1">ghost</span>
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Unchecked" variant="ghost" />
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Checked" variant="ghost" defaultChecked />
  <Checkbox disabled={disabled} label="Indeterminate" variant="ghost" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Pill
Set pill to render the checkbox indicator with fully rounded corners (border-radius: full) instead of the default square radius. On a phone with touch.css every checkbox indicator is round, the 22px selection circle of iOS, so pill makes no difference there: the phone view leaves out the pill control in the overview, and this example, which would repeat the solid group of Variants, is desktop only.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox label="Unchecked" pill />
<Checkbox label="Checked" pill defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Indeterminate" pill checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
```

### Ghost
Use variant="ghost" to render the checkbox without a border or background. The checkmark uses the text color instead of white, making it suitable for subtle inline selections or task lists. On a phone this would repeat the ghost group of Variants, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox label="Unchecked" variant="ghost" />
<Checkbox label="Checked" variant="ghost" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Indeterminate" variant="ghost" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
```

### With description
Use description for a second line under the label. It sits outside the label, so the checkbox keeps the label as its name and gets the description through aria-describedby. The description renders only next to a label.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4 max-w-sm">
<Checkbox
  label="Share usage data"
  description="Help improve the product with anonymous usage reports."
  defaultChecked
/>
<Checkbox
  label="Enable notifications"
  description="You can enable or disable notifications at any time from settings."
/>
</div>
```

### Indeterminate
Use checked="indeterminate" to indicate a partially selected state. This is typically used for "select all" controls where only some child items are checked. Here checked starts as "indeterminate" and each click moves it to the next state.
```tsx
const [checked, setChecked] = useState<boolean | "indeterminate">("indeterminate");

<Checkbox
checked={checked}
onCheckedChange={() =>
  setChecked(c => c === "indeterminate" ? true : c ? false : "indeterminate")
}
label="Select all"
/>
```

### Label orientation
By default the checkbox renders to the left of the label. Set orientation="right" to place the checkbox after the label.
```tsx
<Checkbox label="Remember this device" orientation="right" />
```

### Without label
When no label is provided, the checkbox renders as a standalone control, so pass aria-label to give it an accessible name. All three visual states are shown: unchecked, checked, and indeterminate.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-4">
<Checkbox aria-label="Accept terms" />
<Checkbox aria-label="Subscribe" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox aria-label="Select all" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
```

### Group with select all
Combine a parent checkbox with child checkboxes to create a "select all" pattern. The parent shows an indeterminate state when only some children are checked. Each child is controlled by its item in items.
```tsx
const [items, setItems] = useState([
{ id: "read", label: "Read", checked: true },
{ id: "write", label: "Write", checked: false },
{ id: "execute", label: "Execute", checked: false },
])

const allChecked = items.every((i) => i.checked)
const noneChecked = items.every((i) => !i.checked)
const parentChecked = allChecked ? true : noneChecked ? false : "indeterminate"

<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox
  label="Permissions"
  checked={parentChecked}
  onCheckedChange={() => {
    const next = !allChecked
    setItems((prev) => prev.map((i) => ({ ...i, checked: next })))
  }}
/>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 pl-6">
  {items.map((item) => (
    <Checkbox
      key={item.id}
      label={item.label}
      checked={item.checked}
      onCheckedChange={(next) => {
        setItems((prev) => prev.map((i) => (i.id === item.id ? { ...i, checked: Boolean(next) } : i)))
      }}
    />
  ))}
</div>
</div>
```

### Group with description
Wrap a group of checkboxes in a Field for a shared label and description. This is a common pattern for preference lists and settings panels. On a phone the group is a FieldGroup whose title and description name the list, with a row for each option.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Field label="Download over cellular" description="Choose what can use mobile data.">
{() => (
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
    <Checkbox label="Photos" defaultChecked />
    <Checkbox label="Videos" />
    <Checkbox label="Music" />
    <Checkbox label="Podcasts" />
  </div>
)}
</Field>

// Phone
<FieldGroup title="Download over cellular" description="Choose what can use mobile data.">
<Field row label="Photos"><Checkbox defaultChecked /></Field>
<Field row label="Videos"><Checkbox /></Field>
<Field row label="Music"><Checkbox /></Field>
<Field row label="Podcasts"><Checkbox /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### With Field
Wrap checkboxes in a Field component for form layout with label, description, and error message support. A single control passed as the child gets aria-describedby and aria-invalid automatically; the render-prop form receives them as arguments, so spread them onto the control that should carry them. On a phone the options are rows of a FieldGroup and a FieldError in its footer shows the message; link it to the checkbox it is about with aria-describedby.
```tsx
const [agreed, setAgreed] = useState(false)
const errorId = useId()

// Desktop
<Field
label="Terms"
description="Please review and accept the terms before continuing."
errorMessage={showError ? "You must accept the terms to continue." : undefined}
>
{() => (
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
    <Checkbox
      label="I agree to the Terms of Service"
      checked={agreed}
      onCheckedChange={(next) => setAgreed(Boolean(next))}
    />
    <Checkbox label="I agree to the Privacy Policy" />
  </div>
)}
</Field>

// Phone
<FieldGroup
title="Terms"
description="Please review and accept the terms before continuing."
footer={showError ? <FieldError id={errorId}>You must accept the terms to continue.</FieldError> : undefined}
>
<Field row label="I agree to the Terms of Service">
  <Checkbox
    checked={agreed}
    onCheckedChange={(next) => setAgreed(Boolean(next))}
    aria-invalid={showError || undefined}
    aria-describedby={showError ? errorId : undefined}
  />
</Field>
<Field row label="I agree to the Privacy Policy"><Checkbox /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Grouped sections
Use dividers to separate checkbox groups into logical sections. Each section can be wrapped in a Field with its own label and description.
```tsx
const [settings, setSettings] = useState({
emailMarketing: true,
emailSecurity: true,
pushMessages: true,
pushMentions: true,
pushComments: false,
})
const toggle = (key: keyof typeof settings) => () =>
setSettings((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: !prev[key] }))

// BackButton is your app's navigation action.
<Page className="h-dvh [--page-content-padding-top:10px] [--page-content-padding-bottom:16px] [--page-footer-gutter:24px] [--page-footer-padding-bottom:max(24px,env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))]">
<Page.Header style={{ paddingTop: 'env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)' }}><Page.Bar><Page.Leading><BackButton /></Page.Leading><Page.Title>Notifications</Page.Title></Page.Bar></Page.Header>
<Page.Content>
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
    <FieldGroup title="Email notifications" description="Configure which emails you receive.">
      <Field row label="Marketing" description="Receive emails about new products and features."><Checkbox checked={settings.emailMarketing} onCheckedChange={toggle('emailMarketing')} /></Field>
      <Field row label="Security" description="Receive emails about account activity and security."><Checkbox checked={settings.emailSecurity} onCheckedChange={toggle('emailSecurity')} /></Field>
    </FieldGroup>
    <FieldGroup title="Push notifications" description="Configure which push notifications you receive.">
      <Field row label="Direct messages"><Checkbox checked={settings.pushMessages} onCheckedChange={toggle('pushMessages')} /></Field>
      <Field row label="Mentions"><Checkbox checked={settings.pushMentions} onCheckedChange={toggle('pushMentions')} /></Field>
      <Field row label="Comments"><Checkbox checked={settings.pushComments} onCheckedChange={toggle('pushComments')} /></Field>
    </FieldGroup>
  </div>
</Page.Content>
</Page>
```

## Code Block
Code block with syntax highlighting, a copy button, and collapsible long snippets with configurable expanded height limits.
Import: import { CodeBlock } from "@plexui/ui/components/CodeBlock"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/code-block
Props:
  - children (string) — Code content
  - language (string) — Prism language name
  - className (string) — Additional wrapper class
  CollapsibleCodeBlock:
    - children (string) — Code content
    - language (string) — Prism language name
    - defaultExpanded (boolean) default: false — Start expanded
    - collapsedHeight (number) default: 140 — Height when collapsed (px)
    - maxExpandedHeight (number) — Max height when expanded (px); taller code scrolls
    - copyable (boolean) default: true — Show copy button
    - className (string) — Additional wrapper class

### Overview
```tsx
<CodeBlock language="javascript">{codeSnippet}</CodeBlock>
```

### Collapsible
Use CollapsibleCodeBlock to display code in a compact view with gradient overlay and an expand action.
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx">{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Expanded by default
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx" defaultExpanded>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Custom collapsed height
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="typescript" collapsedHeight={60}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Max expanded height
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="typescript" defaultExpanded maxExpandedHeight={200}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Without copy button
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="python" defaultExpanded copyable={false}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Supported languages
A pragmatic set of Prism grammars are pre-registered out of the box.
```tsx
<CodeBlock language="javascript">{code}</CodeBlock>
```

## Color Picker
"The iOS 26 system color picker: Grid, Spectrum and Sliders, an Opacity slider and saved colors, and the color well that opens it in a popover or, on a phone, a sheet."
Import: import { ColorPicker, ColorWell } from "@plexui/ui/components/ColorPicker"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/color-picker
Props:
  - value (string) — The controlled color, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`
  - defaultValue (string) default: "#000000" — The color when it is initially rendered
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called with the next color: `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` when it is not opaque
  - supportsAlpha (boolean) default: true — Shows the Opacity slider
  - mode ("grid" | "spectrum" | "sliders") — The controlled way to choose a color
  - defaultMode ("grid" | "spectrum" | "sliders") default: "grid" — The way to choose a color when it is initially rendered
  - onModeChange ((mode) => void) — Called when another way is chosen
  - swatches (string[]) — The controlled saved colors
  - defaultSwatches (string[]) default: [] — The saved colors when it is initially rendered
  - onSwatchesChange ((swatches: string[]) => void) — Called after Add saves the current color or Delete removes one
  - aria-label (string) default: "Colors" — Accessible name of the picker
  ColorWell:
    - value (string | null) — The controlled color, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`; `null` shows the well with no color
    - defaultValue (string | null) default: null — The color when it is initially rendered
    - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called with the color the picker chose
    - size ("sm" | "lg") default: "sm" — 28px or 36px
    - title (string) default: "Colors" — The title of the picker
    - supportsEyedropper (boolean) default: true — Shows the eyedropper where the browser has the EyeDropper API
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevents opening the picker
    - name (string) — Submits the color with the owning form
    - aria-label (string) default: "Color" — Accessible name of the well
    - aria-labelledby (string) — The `id` of the visible label of the well

### Color well
The well shows the chosen color inside a rainbow ring, or the full rainbow when there is no color yet (null). It opens the picker in a popover from the well, and on a phone in a sheet. The eyedropper appears where the browser can pick a color from the screen. Both wells here share their saved colors. On a phone the rows sit in an iOS settings screen under its toolbar.
```tsx
const [tint, setTint] = useState('#af52de')
const [swatches, setSwatches] = useState(['#000000', '#007aff', '#34c759'])

<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Tint">
  <ColorWell aria-label="Tint" value={tint} onChange={setTint}
    swatches={swatches} onSwatchesChange={setSwatches} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Sizes and states
The kit's two sizes: sm 28px and lg 36px.
```tsx
<ColorWell aria-label="Small, no color" />
<ColorWell aria-label="Small" defaultValue="#af52de" />
<ColorWell aria-label="Large, no color" size="lg" />
<ColorWell aria-label="Large" size="lg" defaultValue="#af52de" />
<ColorWell aria-label="Disabled" defaultValue="#007aff" disabled />
```

### Picker
The picker on its own. Grid shows the kit's 120 colors; Spectrum runs the hues from top to bottom, from white through the full hue to black across; Sliders sets red, green and blue, or a hex color. Add saves the current color; Delete or Backspace, or Delete in a saved color's context menu, removes one. Saved colors fill pages of ten that scroll sideways.
```tsx
const [color, setColor] = useState('#be38f3')

<ColorPicker value={color} onChange={setColor} defaultSwatches={['#000000', '#007aff', '#34c759']} />
```

### Without opacity
With supportsAlpha off there is no Opacity slider, and every color is opaque.
```tsx
<ColorPicker defaultValue="#007aff" defaultMode="sliders" supportsAlpha={false} />
```

## Context Menu
"A menu of actions for an element: a secondary click opens it at the pointer, a touch and hold opens it beside the element over a dimmed page, as iOS 26 context menus do. Its items are the ones of Menu."
Import: import { ContextMenu } from "@plexui/ui/components/ContextMenu"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/context-menu
Props:
  - onOpen (() => void) — Called when the menu opens
  - onClose (() => void) — Called when the menu closes
  ContextMenu.Trigger:
    - children (ReactElement) — The element the menu is for; it receives the handlers
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — The element keeps the browser's own context menu

### Overview
Wrap the element in ContextMenu.Trigger: it keeps its own role and focus. On a touch screen, hold for half a second: the element stays clear above the dimmed, blurred page and the menu opens 16px below it, as in the iOS 27 kit, at the edge on the side of the touch. The press that opened the menu does not activate the element. On a phone the rows sit on the grouped background of an iOS list.
```tsx
<ContextMenu>
<ContextMenu.Trigger>
  <div tabIndex={0}>Groceries</div>
</ContextMenu.Trigger>
<ContextMenu.Content>
  <ContextMenu.Item onSelect={copy}><Copy /> Copy</ContextMenu.Item>
  <ContextMenu.Item onSelect={share}><Share /> Share</ContextMenu.Item>
  <ContextMenu.Item onSelect={pin}><Pin /> Pin</ContextMenu.Item>
  <ContextMenu.Separator />
  <ContextMenu.Item danger onSelect={remove}><RemoveTrash /> Delete</ContextMenu.Item>
</ContextMenu.Content>
</ContextMenu>
```

### Rounded elements
The element is cut out of the dimming with its own corners. An element without corners of its own gets the 30px corner of the kit's preview, at most half its height.
```tsx
<ContextMenu>
<ContextMenu.Trigger>
  <div tabIndex={0} role="img" aria-label="Photos" className="rounded-2xl">
    <Images />
  </div>
</ContextMenu.Trigger>
<ContextMenu.Content>...</ContextMenu.Content>
</ContextMenu>
```

## Copy Tooltip
A copy-to-clipboard tooltip that wraps any trigger element and confirms when the value has been copied.
Import: import { CopyTooltip } from "@plexui/ui/components/Tooltip"
Import: import { Button } from "@plexui/ui/components/Button"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/copy-tooltip
Props:
  - children (ReactNode) — Trigger element (for example Tooltip.TriggerDecorator)
  - copyValue (string) — Required. Content to copy to clipboard
  - openDelay (number) default: 150 — Tooltip open delay in milliseconds
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Preferred tooltip alignment against the trigger
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 — Offset from start/end alignment in pixels
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "top" — Preferred side of the trigger
  - sideOffset (number) default: 5 — Distance from trigger in pixels
  - onCopy ((copied: boolean) => void) — Called once the clipboard write settles, with whether it succeeded. The tooltip says Copied! only after a successful write

### Overview
Hovering the trigger shows Copy after openDelay, keyboard focus shows it at once; a click copies the value and the tooltip says Copied! On a phone a tap copies and shows Copied! at once, so the delay applies to a pointer only.
```tsx
<CopyTooltip copyValue="sess_12345abcdefg">
<Button color="secondary" variant="ghost" size="xl" aria-label="Copy session ID">
  sess_12345abcdefg
</Button>
</CopyTooltip>
```

## Date Input
Masked text input for typing dates and times, with automatic formatting, min and max limits, and validation.
Import: import { DateInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/DateInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-input
Props:
  - value (DateTime | null) — Required. Selected date (Luxon DateTime)
  - onChange ((date: DateTime | null) => void) — Required. Called when a complete valid date is entered or the field is cleared
  - mode (MaskitoDateMode) default: "dd/mm/yyyy" — Date format mode: dd/mm/yyyy, mm/dd/yyyy, yyyy/mm/dd, etc.
  - separator (string) default: "." — Character between date parts
  - timeMode (MaskitoTimeMode) — Enable time input: HH:MM, HH:MM:SS, etc.
  - dateTimeSeparator (string) default: ", " — Separator between date and time parts
  - timeStep (number) default: 0 — Arrow-key increment step for time segments
  - min (DateTime) — Earliest allowed date
  - max (DateTime) — Latest allowed date
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button when input has a value
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Input size (3xs to 3xl)
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded corners
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable input
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark as invalid
  - placeholder (string) — Generated from the format if not set

### Overview
Pass a Luxon DateTime (or null) as value with onChange. onChange fires once a complete, valid date is typed, and with null when the field is emptied or cleared. Leaving the field with a partly typed date shows the value again.
```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { DateTime } from 'luxon';
import { DateInput } from '@plexui/ui/components/DateInput';

// Desktop
export default function DateInputExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(null);
  const [disabled] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="w-[200px]">
      <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} size="md" variant="outline"
        clearable disabled={disabled} />
    </div>
  );
}

// Phone: the date is the value of a row.
<FieldGroup>
  <Field row label="Date">
    <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable disabled={disabled} />
  </Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### With time
Pass timeMode="HH:MM" to enable date + time input in one field.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[260px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} timeMode="HH:MM" clearable />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Starts">
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} timeMode="HH:MM" clearable />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### With seconds
Use timeMode="HH:MM:SS" for second-level precision.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[300px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} timeMode="HH:MM:SS" clearable />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Logged">
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} timeMode="HH:MM:SS" clearable />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Limits
Use min and max to restrict the date range. The mask prevents entering values outside the allowed range. today is DateTime.local().
```tsx
const today = DateTime.local()
const [date, setDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(today)

// Desktop
<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput
  value={date}
  onChange={setDate}
  min={today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf("day")}
  max={today.plus({ days: 30 }).endOf("day")}
  clearable
/>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <DateInput
    value={date}
    onChange={setDate}
    min={today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf("day")}
    max={today.plus({ days: 30 }).endOf("day")}
    clearable
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### US format
Set mode="mm/dd/yyyy" and separator="/" for US-style date formatting.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" clearable />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" clearable />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### ISO format
Set mode="yyyy/mm/dd" and separator="-" for ISO 8601 formatting.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="yyyy/mm/dd" separator="-" clearable />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="yyyy/mm/dd" separator="-" clearable />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### With Field
Wrap with Field to add a label, description, and automatic accessibility attributes.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[200px]">
<Field label="Date of birth" description="Enter your date of birth">
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
</Field>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date of birth" description="Enter your date of birth">
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Validation
Pass errorMessage to Field to display a validation error.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[200px]">
<Field label="Date of birth" errorMessage={!date ? "Date is required" : undefined}>
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
</Field>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date of birth" errorMessage={!date ? "Date is required" : undefined}>
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

## Date Picker
Date picker with an interactive calendar, time picker, year and month dropdowns, min/max limits, and date-of-birth presets.
Import: import { DatePicker } from "@plexui/ui/components/DatePicker"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-picker
Props:
  - value (DateTime | null) — Required. Selected date (luxon)
  - onChange ((date: DateTime | null) => void) — Required. Called when the date changes
  - id (string) — Id of the trigger, for forms and labels
  - min (DateTime) — Earliest selectable date (inclusive)
  - max (DateTime) — Latest selectable date (inclusive). Must not be before min
  - captionLayout ("buttons" | "dropdown") default: "buttons" — Calendar header mode. Use dropdown for date of birth
  - showTime (boolean) default: false — Show time input below calendar
  - yearRange ([number, number]) default: last 120 years — Min/max years for dropdown caption
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Trigger size (3xs to 3xl)
  - variant ("outline" | "soft" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Trigger style
  - pill (boolean) default: true — Rounded trigger
  - block (boolean) default: false — Full-width trigger
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button
  - triggerShowIcon (boolean) default: true — Show calendar icon
  - triggerDateFormat (string) default: "MM/dd/yy" — Date format in trigger. Auto-includes time when showTime is enabled and triggerTimeFormat is not set
  - triggerTimeFormat (string) — With showTime, the time format after the date in the trigger. The date and the time become two parts; in a phone row, two capsules
  - triggerClassName (string) — Class applied to the trigger
  - dropdownIconType ("dropdown" | "chevronDown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Icon at the end of the trigger
  - placeholder (string) default: "Select date..." — Trigger placeholder
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable picker
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred side of the calendar popover. On phones, left and right prefer bottom so all seven day targets fit. Top and bottom keep their preference; collisions can still flip placement.
  - sideOffset (number) default: 8 — Distance from the trigger in pixels
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Alignment against the trigger
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 (center), -5 (start, end) — Offset from start/end alignment in pixels

### Overview
Pass the date (a luxon DateTime, or null) as value and update it in onChange.
```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { DateTime } from 'luxon';
import { DatePicker } from '@plexui/ui/components/DatePicker';

// Desktop
export default function DatePickerExample() {
  const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(null);
  const [disabled] = useState(false);

  return (
    <DatePicker
      id="date-picker-base"
      triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy"
      size="lg"
      pill
      clearable
      disabled={disabled}
      value={selectedDate}
      onChange={setSelectedDate}
    />
  );
}

// Phone: the date is the value of a row, in the compact date that opens the calendar.
<FieldGroup>
  <Field row label="Date">
    <DatePicker
      id="date-picker-base"
      triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
      triggerShowIcon={false}
      placeholder="Select date"
      disabled={disabled}
      value={selectedDate}
      onChange={setSelectedDate}
    />
  </Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Limits
Use min and max to limit selectable dates to a specific timeframe. Equal bounds leave one selectable day.
```tsx
const today = DateTime.local()
const minDate = today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf("day")
const maxDate = today.plus({ days: 30 }).endOf("day")
const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(today)

// Desktop
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-limits"
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy"
size="lg"
pill
triggerShowIcon
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
min={minDate}
max={maxDate}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <DatePicker
    id="date-picker-limits"
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    value={selectedDate}
    onChange={setSelectedDate}
    min={minDate}
    max={maxDate}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Date of birth
Set captionLayout="dropdown" to add month and year dropdowns inline with the arrow navigation. Ideal for selecting a date of birth where navigating month-by-month would be impractical.
```tsx
// Desktop
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-dob"
triggerDateFormat="MMMM d, yyyy"
size="lg"
pill
clearable
placeholder="Select your birthday"
captionLayout="dropdown"
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
max={DateTime.local()}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Birthday">
  <DatePicker
    id="date-picker-dob"
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    placeholder="Select date"
    captionLayout="dropdown"
    value={selectedDate}
    onChange={setSelectedDate}
    max={DateTime.local()}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Time picker
Enable showTime to add hour and minute inputs below the calendar. The popover stays open after selecting a date so the user can adjust the time. Use arrow keys to increment or decrement values. With triggerTimeFormat the trigger shows the date and the time as two parts: on Phone, in a row, they are two capsules, as iOS shows a date and a time.
```tsx
// Desktop
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-time"
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy HH:mm"
size="lg"
pill
clearable
placeholder="Select date & time"
showTime
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Starts">
  <DatePicker
    id="date-picker-time"
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
    triggerTimeFormat="HH:mm"
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    placeholder="Select date"
    showTime
    value={selectedDate}
    onChange={setSelectedDate}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Dropdown + time
Combine captionLayout="dropdown" with showTime for quick month/year jumps and time selection in a single picker, useful for scheduling events at a specific date and time.
```tsx
// Desktop
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-datetime-dropdown"
triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy HH:mm"
size="lg"
pill
clearable
placeholder="Schedule event"
captionLayout="dropdown"
showTime
yearRange={[2020, 2030]}
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Event">
  <DatePicker
    id="date-picker-datetime-dropdown"
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
    triggerTimeFormat="HH:mm"
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    placeholder="Select date"
    captionLayout="dropdown"
    showTime
    yearRange={[2020, 2030]}
    value={selectedDate}
    onChange={setSelectedDate}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Two fields
Compose DatePicker and Input side by side for maximum flexibility in form layouts. Each field operates independently while sharing the same DateTime value. Here handleTimeInput masks the typed time as HH:MM and moves the date to a complete typed time, and a newly picked date takes the typed time.
```tsx
const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(null)
const [time, setTime] = useState("10:30")

// Mask the typed time as HH:MM; a complete time moves the picked date's time
const handleTimeInput = (event: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
const raw = event.target.value.replace(/[^\d:]/g, "")
const digits = raw.replace(/:/g, "")
let formatted = digits
if (digits.length >= 3) {
  formatted = digits.slice(0, 2) + ":" + digits.slice(2, 4)
} else if (digits.length === 2 && !raw.includes(":")) {
  formatted = digits + ":"
}
setTime(formatted.slice(0, 5))

const parts = formatted.split(":")
if (parts.length === 2 && parts[1].length === 2 && selectedDate) {
  const hour = Math.min(23, Number(parts[0]) || 0)
  const minute = Math.min(59, Number(parts[1]) || 0)
  setSelectedDate(selectedDate.set({ hour, minute }))
}
}

// A picked date takes the typed time
const onDateChange = (next: DateTime | null) => {
if (next && time) {
  const [hour, minute] = time.split(":").map(Number)
  setSelectedDate(next.set({ hour: hour || 0, minute: minute || 0 }))
} else {
  setSelectedDate(next)
}
}

// Desktop
<div style={{ display: "flex", gap: "8px", alignItems: "center" }}>
<DatePicker
  id="date-picker-two-field-date"
  triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
  size="lg"
  pill
  captionLayout="dropdown"
  triggerShowIcon={false}
  dropdownIconType="none"
  placeholder="Select date"
  value={selectedDate}
  onChange={onDateChange}
/>
<Input
  id="date-picker-two-field-time"
  size="lg"
  pill
  value={time}
  onChange={handleTimeInput}
  placeholder="HH:MM"
  maxLength={5}
  style={{ width: "72px" }}
/>
</div>

// Phone: two rows, the compact date and the time typed at the row's end
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <DatePicker
    id="date-picker-two-field-date"
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
    captionLayout="dropdown"
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    placeholder="Select date"
    value={selectedDate}
    onChange={onDateChange}
  />
</Field>
<Field row label="Time">
  <Input
    id="date-picker-two-field-time"
    value={time}
    onChange={handleTimeInput}
    placeholder="HH:MM"
    maxLength={5}
    inputMode="numeric"
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Date input
For typing a date directly instead of picking it, use DateInput, a masked input that auto-formats as you type.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[200px]">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" aria-label="Date" />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### DateTime input
Pass timeMode="HH:MM" to DateInput to type the date and time in one field.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[260px]">
<DateInput
  value={dateTime}
  onChange={setDateTime}
  mode="mm/dd/yyyy"
  separator="/"
  timeMode="HH:MM"
  aria-label="Date and time"
/>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Starts">
  <DateInput value={dateTime} onChange={setDateTime} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" timeMode="HH:MM" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Without Icon
Remove the calendar icon from the trigger by setting triggerShowIcon to false. In a phone row the date never shows the icon, as the compact date of iOS does not, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
// Desktop
<DatePicker
id="date-picker-no-icon"
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy"
size="lg"
triggerShowIcon={false}
placeholder="Choose a date"
value={selectedDate}
onChange={setSelectedDate}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <DatePicker
    id="date-picker-no-icon"
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy"
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    placeholder="Choose a date"
    value={selectedDate}
    onChange={setSelectedDate}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

## Date Range Picker
Date range picker with an interactive calendar, min/max limits, preset shortcuts, and a month stepper for selecting start and end dates.
Import: import { DateRangePicker } from "@plexui/ui/components/DateRangePicker"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-range-picker
Props:
  - value (DateRange | null) — Required. Selected range ([start, end], inclusive)
  - onChange ((next: DateRange | null, shortcut?: DateRangeShortcut) => void) — Required. Called when the range changes
  - min (DateTime) — Earliest selectable date (inclusive)
  - max (DateTime) — Latest selectable date (inclusive). Must not be before min
  - maxRangeDays (number) — Max length of range in days (inclusive)
  - weekStartsOn (0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6) default: 0 — The day each week starts on, from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday)
  - shortcuts (DateRangeShortcut[]) — Quick selection shortcuts ({ label, getDateRange }), shown next to the calendar from the md breakpoint up
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred side of the calendar popover. On phones, left and right prefer bottom so all seven day targets fit. Top and bottom keep their preference; collisions can still flip placement.
  - sideOffset (number) default: 8 — Distance from trigger in pixels
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Preferred popover alignment
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 (center), -5 (start, end) — Offset from start/end alignment in pixels
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable picker interactions
  - placeholder (string) default: "Select date range..." — Placeholder in trigger when value is empty
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Trigger style variant
  - pill (boolean) default: true — Rounded trigger shape
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Trigger size scale
  - dropdownIconType ("chevronDown" | "dropdown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Icon shown at trigger end
  - triggerClassName (string) — Custom class for trigger
  - triggerShowIcon (boolean) default: true — Show calendar icon at trigger start
  - triggerStepperUnit ("month") — Enable month stepper mode in trigger
  - triggerDateFormat (string) default: "MM/dd/yy" — Date formatting in trigger text
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button in trigger
  - block (boolean) default: false — Stretch trigger to full available width

### Overview
Pass the range ([start, end] luxon DateTimes, or null) as value and update it in onChange.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>(null)
const [disabled] = useState(false)

// Desktop
<div style={{ width: "fit-content" }}>
<DateRangePicker
  size="lg"
  pill
  clearable
  disabled={disabled}
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
/>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Dates">
  <DateRangePicker
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d"
    placeholder="None"
    disabled={disabled}
    value={value}
    onChange={setValue}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Limits
Use min and max to limit the selectable range. Use maxRangeDays to limit the range length. Here minDate is 30 days ago (start of day) and maxDate is the end of today.
```tsx
const today = DateTime.local()
const minDate = today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf("day")
const maxDate = today.endOf("day")
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>([
DateTime.max(minDate, today.startOf("month")),
DateTime.min(maxDate, today.endOf("month")),
])

// Desktop
<div style={{ width: "fit-content" }}>
<DateRangePicker
  size="lg"
  pill
  triggerShowIcon
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  min={minDate}
  max={maxDate}
/>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Dates">
  <DateRangePicker
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d"
    placeholder="None"
    value={value}
    onChange={setValue}
    min={minDate}
    max={maxDate}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Shortcuts
Use the shortcuts array to provide quick date range options. When a shortcut is selected, its label is shown in the trigger and onChange receives that shortcut as its second argument. Each shortcut has a label and a getDateRange() function. A shortcut whose range falls outside min and max, or is longer than maxRangeDays, is disabled. The calendar doesn't show shortcuts below the md breakpoint. On a phone, offer them in a row of their own, as iOS settings offer presets: here a Period row with a Select of the shortcut labels above the Dates row. When the dates match no shortcut, the Period row reads Custom.
```tsx
const dayShortcuts: DateRangeShortcut[] = [
{
  label: "Today",
  getDateRange: () => {
    const today = DateTime.local()
    return [today.startOf("day"), today.endOf("day")]
  },
},
{
  label: "Yesterday",
  getDateRange: () => {
    const yesterday = DateTime.local().minus({ days: 1 })
    return [yesterday.startOf("day"), yesterday.endOf("day")]
  },
},
{
  label: "Last 7 days",
  getDateRange: () => {
    const today = DateTime.local().endOf("day")
    return [today.minus({ days: 6 }).startOf("day"), today]
  },
},
{
  label: "Last 30 days",
  getDateRange: () => {
    const today = DateTime.local().endOf("day")
    return [today.minus({ days: 29 }).startOf("day"), today]
  },
},
]
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>(null)

// Desktop
<div style={{ width: "fit-content" }}>
<DateRangePicker
  size="lg"
  pill
  clearable
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  shortcuts={dayShortcuts}
/>
</div>

// Phone: the shortcuts are a pop-up in a row of their own, which reads Custom for any other range
const periodOptions = dayShortcuts.map(({ label }) => ({ value: label, label }))
const period = value
? dayShortcuts.find(({ getDateRange }) => {
    const [start, end] = getDateRange()
    return value[0].hasSame(start, "day") && value[1].hasSame(end, "day")
  })?.label ?? ""
: ""

<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Period">
  <Select
    value={period}
    options={periodOptions}
    onChange={({ value: label }) => {
      const shortcut = dayShortcuts.find((item) => item.label === label)
      if (shortcut) setValue(shortcut.getDateRange())
    }}
    placeholder={value ? "Custom" : "None"}
    block={false}
    align="end"
  />
</Field>
<Field row label="Dates">
  <DateRangePicker
    triggerShowIcon={false}
    triggerDateFormat="MMM d"
    placeholder="None"
    value={value}
    onChange={setValue}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Month stepper
Enable a stepper in the trigger with triggerStepperUnit="month". When the selected range matches the unit, the trigger shows the stepper.
```tsx
const today = DateTime.local()
const maxDate = today.endOf("day")
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>([today.startOf("month"), today])

// Desktop
<div style={{ width: "fit-content" }}>
<DateRangePicker
  size="lg"
  clearable
  pill
  triggerStepperUnit="month"
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  max={maxDate}
/>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Month">
  <DateRangePicker
    triggerStepperUnit="month"
    value={value}
    onChange={setValue}
    max={maxDate}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

## Dialog
Modal dialog for confirmations, forms, and destructive alerts, with a focus trap, escape handling, and an overlay scrim.
Import: import { Dialog } from "@plexui/ui/components/Dialog"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/dialog
Props:
  - open (boolean) — Controlled open state; uncontrolled when omitted
  - onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void) — Called when the dialog opens or closes
  Dialog.Content:
    - surface ("plain" | "grouped") default: "plain" — Mobile panel and field-group palette. Dark dialogs use elevated surface levels; desktop colors stay unchanged
    - width (number | string) default: 480 — Panel width. Mobile alert uses its compact width; a bottom sheet fills the viewport width
    - showClose (boolean) default: true — Show the built-in close button. Mobile sheet places it at the leading edge; mobile alert hides it
    - pill (boolean) default: false — Rounder panel and a round close button, for dialogs beside pill controls
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class on the panel
    - placement ("center" | "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" | "fullscreen") default: "center" — Where the panel sits: centered, near the top, a bottom sheet, a side panel, or the whole screen
    - mobileVariant ("alert" | "sheet") — Mobile appearance at 767px and below. Alert is compact and centered; sheet defaults to the bottom. Omit for the standard appearance
    - mobilePlacement ("center" | "bottom" | "fullscreen") — Placement at 767px and below. Defaults to bottom for sheet, otherwise placement. Alert stays centered
    - onOpenAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called when focus moves into the dialog on open; call event.preventDefault() to place it yourself, for example on the panel instead of the first field
    - onCloseAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called when focus returns on close; call event.preventDefault() to keep it elsewhere
    - onEscapeKeyDown ((event: KeyboardEvent) => void) — Called on Escape before the dialog closes; call event.preventDefault() to keep it open
    - onInteractOutside ((event: DialogInteractOutsideEvent) => void) — Called on a press or a focus outside the dialog before it closes; call event.preventDefault() to keep it open. event.detail.originalEvent is the browser's event
    - zIndex (number) default: 50 — Stack order of the overlay and the dialog, for a page whose own layers sit above 50
    - rootProps (DialogLayerProps) — className, style and data attributes for the fixed layer that holds the panel. Data attributes on Dialog.Content land there too
    - overlayProps (DialogLayerProps) — className, style and data attributes for the overlay
    - layout ("auto" | "phone") default: "auto" — phone lays the dialog out as on a phone at any window width, with the dialogs it opens. Inside a PhoneLayout it always is
  Dialog.Footer:
    - background ("soft" | "hard" | "glass" | "solid") default: "soft" — How the phone Sheet's bar meets the body scrolled under it, as on a Toolbar. Also available on the header; desktop and Alert surfaces are unchanged
    - mobileLayout ("inline" | "stacked") — Action layout at 767px and below. Defaults to inline for alert, stacked otherwise. Inline actions wrap when they do not fit
  Dialog.Steps:
    - step (string | number) — The step on screen. A new value brings its content in
    - direction ("forward" | "back") default: "forward" — forward brings the new step in from the trailing edge over the one before; back returns to a step before it
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class on the steps

### Overview
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
const heading = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline">Open dialog</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="alert" onOpenAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); heading.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }}>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <div ref={heading} tabIndex={-1} className="outline-none"><Dialog.Title>Unsaved changes</Dialog.Title></div>
    <Dialog.Description>You have unsaved changes that will be lost if you close this page. Do you want to save before leaving?</Dialog.Description>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Dialog.Close>
      <Button color="primary" variant="soft">Cancel</Button>
    </Dialog.Close>
    <Button color="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Save</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

### Destructive confirmation
Use color="danger" on the action button for destructive operations.
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
const heading = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="danger" variant="outline">Delete</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="alert" onOpenAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); heading.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }}>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <div ref={heading} tabIndex={-1} className="outline-none"><Dialog.Title>Delete assistant?</Dialog.Title></div>
    <Dialog.Description>
      This change will affect all API integrations using{" "}
      <span className="md:font-medium md:text-[var(--color-text)]">asst_NAM5K9a7loKZay9W8gtQVQ3H</span>.
      It cannot be undone.
    </Dialog.Description>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Dialog.Close>
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Cancel</Button>
    </Dialog.Close>
    <Button color="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Delete</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

### Text field
An alert can ask for one short value. The field fills the alert like its actions, a 52px capsule on a phone, and its text is selected when the alert opens. Create is unavailable while the field is empty.
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
const [name, setName] = useState("New folder")
const field = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={(next) => { setOpen(next); if (next) setName("New folder"); }}>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline">New folder</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="alert" onOpenAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); field.current?.select(); }}>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <Dialog.Title>New folder</Dialog.Title>
    <Dialog.Description>Enter a name for this folder.</Dialog.Description>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Body>
    <Input ref={field} aria-label="Folder name" variant="soft" size="3xl" pill value={name} onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)} onClear={() => setName("")} />
  </Dialog.Body>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Dialog.Close>
      <Button color="primary" variant="soft">Cancel</Button>
    </Dialog.Close>
    <Button color="primary" disabled={!name.trim()} onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Create</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

### Metadata details
Use a definition list for labels and values. CopyTooltip wraps a real ghost Button, so the value supports pointer and keyboard copying. The visible value truncates in the middle while the full value is copied. Focus starts at the heading, then Tab reaches the controls.
```tsx
'use client';

import { useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Badge } from '@plexui/ui/components/Badge';
import { Button } from '@plexui/ui/components/Button';
import { Dialog } from '@plexui/ui/components/Dialog';
import { CopyTooltip } from '@plexui/ui/components/Tooltip';
import { useBreakpoint } from '@plexui/ui/hooks/useBreakpoints';

const detailsStyles = `/* Read-only metadata uses native Body and Footnote roles on phones. */
@media (max-width: 767px) {
  .details-content [data-detail-list] {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: 0;
    font-size: 17px;
    line-height: 22px;
  }

  .details-content [data-detail-row] {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
    row-gap: 4px;
    margin: 0;
    padding-block-end: 20px;
  }

  /* A copy target includes its own space below the text; targets never overlap. */
  .details-content [data-detail-row]:has([data-detail-copy]),
  .details-content [data-detail-row]:last-child {
    padding-block-end: 0;
  }

  .details-content [data-detail-row] > dt {
    font-size: 13px;
    font-weight: 400;
    line-height: 18px;
  }

  .details-content [data-detail-row] > dd {
    grid-column: auto;
    color: var(--color-text);
  }

  .details-content [data-detail-copy] {
    --button-radius: 8px;
    --button-gutter: 0px;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: flex-start;
    height: 44px;
    min-width: 0;
    max-width: 100%;
    margin: 0;
    padding: 0;
    color: var(--color-text);
    vertical-align: top;
  }

  .details-content [data-detail-copy] > span {
    align-items: flex-start;
    height: 22px;
  }

  .details-content [data-detail-copy]::before,
  .details-content [data-detail-copy]::after {
    inset-block-end: 22px;
  }

  .details-content [data-detail-value] {
    font-size: 17px;
    font-weight: 400;
    line-height: 22px;
  }
}
`;

const CLIENT_ID = 'client_76fb07f7-78e2-4656-abdf-e77b5d7b1ed1';

function CopyValue({ value, label }: { value: string; label: string }) {
  const wide = useBreakpoint('md');
  return (
    <CopyTooltip copyValue={value} sideOffset={wide ? 5 : 24} align={wide ? 'center' : 'start'}>
      <Button data-detail-copy color="secondary" variant="ghost" size="sm" opticallyAlign="start" className="-my-1 max-w-full" aria-label={label}>
        <span data-detail-value className="flex min-w-0 font-mono text-xs">
          <span className="truncate">{value.slice(0, -6)}</span>
          <span className="shrink-0">{value.slice(-6)}</span>
        </span>
      </Button>
    </CopyTooltip>
  );
}

function DetailRow({ label, children }: { label: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div data-detail-row className="grid grid-cols-1 items-start gap-x-4 gap-y-1 sm:grid-cols-4">
      <dt className="text-secondary">{label}</dt>
      <dd className="min-w-0 sm:col-span-3">{children}</dd>
    </div>
  );
}

export function DetailsDialogExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const heading = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-4 py-10">
      <style>{detailsStyles}</style>
      <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <Dialog.Trigger>
          <Button color="secondary" variant="outline">View details</Button>
        </Dialog.Trigger>
        <Dialog.Content mobileVariant="sheet" width={640} onOpenAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); heading.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }}>
          <Dialog.Header>
            <div ref={heading} tabIndex={-1} className="outline-none"><Dialog.Title>Application details</Dialog.Title></div>
            <Dialog.Description className="sr-only">Application metadata.</Dialog.Description>
          </Dialog.Header>
          <Dialog.Body>
            <div className="details-content py-2">
              <dl data-detail-list className="space-y-4 text-sm">
                <DetailRow label="Name">Plex application</DetailRow>
                <DetailRow label="Client ID"><CopyValue value={CLIENT_ID} label="Copy client ID" /></DetailRow>
                <DetailRow label="Status"><Badge color="success" size="sm">Active</Badge></DetailRow>
                <DetailRow label="Created">Nov 3, 2026</DetailRow>
                <DetailRow label="Last used">Nov 4, 2026</DetailRow>
              </dl>
            </div>
          </Dialog.Body>
        </Dialog.Content>
      </Dialog>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Scrolling body
Put long content in Dialog.Body: only the body scrolls, while the header and footer stay in view. Without it the whole panel scrolls. On a phone, background on Dialog.Header and Dialog.Footer sets how the Sheet's bars meet the body scrolled under them, as a Toolbar's do: by default glass on the header and soft on the footer, or hard or solid.
```tsx
const heading = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="sheet" onOpenAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); heading.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }}>
<Dialog.Header>
  <div ref={heading} tabIndex={-1} className="outline-none"><Dialog.Title>Terms of service</Dialog.Title></div>
</Dialog.Header>
<Dialog.Body>
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-4 text-sm text-secondary max-md:text-[length:var(--dialog-mobile-type-size)] max-md:leading-[var(--dialog-mobile-type-leading)]">
    {terms.map((term) => <p key={term}>{term}</p>)}
  </div>
</Dialog.Body>
<Dialog.Footer>
  <Dialog.Close><Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Decline</Button></Dialog.Close>
  <Button color="primary">Accept</Button>
</Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
```

### Placement
Use placement to move the panel: top for search and command lists, bottom for a sheet along the bottom edge, start and end for a full-height side panel, fullscreen for the whole screen. mobilePlacement applies at 767px and below, so a centered dialog can become a bottom sheet on phones: {''}.
```tsx
const heading = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="sheet" surface="grouped" onOpenAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); heading.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }} placement="end" width={360}>
<Dialog.Header>
  <div ref={heading} tabIndex={-1} className="outline-none"><Dialog.Title>Filters</Dialog.Title></div>
  {/* On a phone (phone = !useBreakpoint('md')) the note is the group's footer, so the description is only read out. */}
  <Dialog.Description className={phone ? 'sr-only' : undefined}>Narrow the list down.</Dialog.Description>
</Dialog.Header>
<Dialog.Body>
  <FieldGroup columns footer={phone ? 'Narrow the list down.' : undefined}>
    <Field row label="Status"><Input placeholder="Any status" /></Field>
    <Field row label="Owner"><Input placeholder="Anyone" /></Field>
    <Field row label="Created after"><Input placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" /></Field>
  </FieldGroup>
</Dialog.Body>
<Dialog.Footer>
  <Dialog.Close><Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Clear filters</Button></Dialog.Close>
  <Button color="primary">Done</Button>
</Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
```

### View options sheet

```tsx
import { ViewOptionsSheetDemo } from './ViewOptionsSheet';

export default function ViewPreferences() {
return <ViewOptionsSheetDemo />;
}
```

### Segmented composer header

```tsx
import { SegmentedComposer } from './SegmentedComposer';

export default function Example() {
return <SegmentedComposer surface="grouped" />;
}
```

### Setup choices
```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SetupChoicesSheet } from './SetupChoicesSheet';

export default function Example() {
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
return <SetupChoicesSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} layout="grouped" onAdd={(method) => console.log(method.id)} />;
}
```

### Steps
Put the steps of a flow in Dialog.Steps: a new step comes in from the trailing edge over the one before, which moves a third of the way out under it, as a push on iOS. direction="back" reverses it for a return to a step before. The new step starts at its top, the steps reach the panel's edges, and focus in the step that leaves moves to the one that comes in. With reduced motion the step changes at once.
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
const [step, setStep] = useState('email')
const [direction, setDirection] = useState('forward')
const go = (next, to) => { setDirection(to); setStep(next) }

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline">Sign in</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="sheet" width={420}>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <Dialog.Title>Sign in</Dialog.Title>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Body>
    <Dialog.Steps step={step} direction={direction}>
      {step === 'email' ? (
        <Field label="Email" description="We send a code to this address.">
          <Input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
        </Field>
      ) : (
        <Field label="Code" description="Enter the code we sent to your email.">
          <Input inputMode="numeric" autoComplete="one-time-code" placeholder="6-digit code" />
        </Field>
      )}
    </Dialog.Steps>
  </Dialog.Body>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    {step === 'code' && <Button color="primary" variant="soft" onClick={() => go('email', 'back')}>Back</Button>}
    {step === 'email'
      ? <Button color="primary" onClick={() => go('code', 'forward')}>Continue</Button>
      : <Button color="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Verify</Button>}
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

### Keep it open
Escape and a press or a focus outside ask onEscapeKeyDown and onInteractOutside first: event.preventDefault() keeps the dialog open, such as for a form with unsaved changes, or for a press on a developer panel over the page. The Close button and Dialog.Close still close it.
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
const [name, setName] = useState('Mia')
const dirty = name !== 'Mia'
const hold = (event) => { if (dirty) event.preventDefault() }

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline">Edit profile</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content width={420} onEscapeKeyDown={hold} onInteractOutside={hold}>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <Dialog.Title>Edit profile</Dialog.Title>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <Field label="Name">
    <Input value={name} onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)} />
  </Field>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Dialog.Close>
      <Button color="primary" variant="soft">Discard</Button>
    </Dialog.Close>
    <Button color="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Save</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

## Empty Message
Empty state for telling users there's nothing to show, with error, warning, no-results, and onboarding compositions.
Import: import { EmptyMessage } from "@plexui/ui/components/EmptyMessage"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/empty-message
Props:
  - fill ("static" | "absolute" | "none") default: "static" — How the container fills its parent: "static" takes full width and height, "absolute" covers a positioned parent (inset 0), "none" applies no sizing
  - size ("sm" | "md") default: "md" — sm is the compact message for a panel, a card section or an empty list
  - align ("center" | "start") default: "center" — start left-aligns the message, for an empty state under a section heading
  EmptyMessage.Icon:
    - color ("secondary" | "danger" | "warning") default: "secondary" — Semantic color
    - size ("sm" | "md") default: "md" — Icon badge size
  EmptyMessage.Title:
    - color ("secondary" | "danger" | "warning") default: "secondary" — Semantic color
  EmptyMessage.ActionRow:
    - className (string) — Additional classes for the action row container

### Composition
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon>
  <Explore />
</EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title>No projects yet</EmptyMessage.Title>
<EmptyMessage.Description>Create your first project to get started</EmptyMessage.Description>
<EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
  <Button color="primary" size="xl">
    <Plus className="mr-[-2px]" />
    New project
  </Button>
</EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### Error message
The color property enables you to display clearer intent with the message, such as showing an error state.
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon color="danger">
  <Mic />
</EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title color="danger">
  Enable microphone access in your browser's settings.
</EmptyMessage.Title>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### Warning message
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon color="warning">
  <Sparkle />
</EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title>o1-preview is in beta</EmptyMessage.Title>
<EmptyMessage.Description>
  System instructions and model configuration are not available yet. Responses may take
  longer.
</EmptyMessage.Description>
<EmptyMessage.ActionRow className="text-sm">
  <TextLink href="/">
    Learn more
    <ArrowUpRight />
  </TextLink>
</EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### No results
The components of EmptyMessage are both composable and optional. This example omits the EmptyMessage.Title component, using only an icon and description for a simpler message style.
```tsx
<div className="w-full">
<EmptyMessage fill="none">
  <EmptyMessage.Icon size="sm">
    <Search />
  </EmptyMessage.Icon>
  <EmptyMessage.Description>
    No icons found matching <span className="font-semibold">"pizza"</span>
  </EmptyMessage.Description>
</EmptyMessage>
</div>
```

### Compact
Use size="sm" for an empty panel, card section or list: a smaller title, tighter spacing and no minimum width. Pair it with fill="none" when the container sets the height.
```tsx
<Card>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Members</Card.Title>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <EmptyMessage size="sm" fill="none">
    <EmptyMessage.Icon size="sm"><Group /></EmptyMessage.Icon>
    <EmptyMessage.Title>No members yet</EmptyMessage.Title>
    <EmptyMessage.Description>Invite people to work on this project.</EmptyMessage.Description>
    <EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" size="sm">Invite</Button>
    </EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
  </EmptyMessage>
</Card.Content>
</Card>
```

### Left aligned
Use align="start" for an empty state that sits under a section heading instead of filling a surface: a single line such as "No tags added" reads with the heading above it.
```tsx
<Card>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Tags</Card.Title>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <EmptyMessage size="sm" align="start" fill="none">
    <EmptyMessage.Description>No tags added.</EmptyMessage.Description>
  </EmptyMessage>
</Card.Content>
</Card>
```

## Field
Form field wrapper with a label, helper text, an error message, and automatic accessibility linking to its control.
Import: import { Field } from "@plexui/ui/components/Field"
Import: import { FieldGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/FieldGroup"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/field
Props:
  - label (ReactNode) — Label text for the field
  - hideLabel (boolean) default: false — Hides the label from view; it still names the control. A description moves under the control. On a row the value or placeholder starts at the row's edge, so the row is vertical unless orientation says otherwise
  - description (ReactNode) — Helper text below the label; linked via aria-describedby
  - errorMessage (ReactNode) — Error message below the control; auto-sets aria-invalid on child
  - labelAction (ReactNode) — Content at the end of the label row, such as a link that acts on the field
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: child's size, else "md" — Label font size; defaults to the child control's size
  - required (boolean) default: false — Shows a required asterisk after the label (visual only)
  - orientation ("vertical" | "horizontal") default: "horizontal" on a row with a visible label, else "vertical" — Layout direction of label and control
  - row (boolean) default: false — One line of a FieldGroup. Clicking its non-interactive area focuses the text editor or activates the choice or popup control. Other div props reach the root only on a row
  - fill (boolean) default: false — On a row, the control takes the rest of the line after the label
  - action (ReactNode) — On a fill row, a control at the end of the row, such as a button that adds to a list. It stays on the list's first line, and on a phone it stands beside the label with the list under it
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Applies optical alignment to the child control via negative margin using its gutter
  - id (string) — Override the auto-generated id used for htmlFor/aria linking. A child's own id wins: it stays, and htmlFor follows it
  - children (ReactElement | (fieldProps) => ReactNode) — Form control; receives id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid, plus aria-labelledby unless it has its own name. A render prop receives aria-labelledby to spread
  - className (string) — Applied to the root wrapper
  FieldGroup:
    - title (ReactNode) — Heading over the block; it names the group
    - headerProminence ("standard" | "increased") default: "standard" — How much the title stands out: a quiet heading over the rows, or a title that leads its content (on a phone the iOS prominent list header, 20pt Semibold)
    - description (ReactNode) — Line under the title
    - action (ReactNode) — Content at the end of the header. On a phone a ghost text button reads as the list header's action: tinted text on the title's last line
    - footer (ReactNode) — Content under the block, such as a note; its paragraphs stand apart
    - columns (boolean) default: false — Every value starts at one column, --field-row-column-width into the row, on the web and on a phone. Off, values end at the row's edge
    - bodyClassName (string) — Applied to the block that holds the rows
    - children (ReactNode) — The rows
    - className (string) — Applied to the root section

### Overview
Field wraps a form control with a label, a description and an error message, and links them: the label's htmlFor, aria-describedby and aria-invalid reach the control. required adds an asterisk after the label; it is visual only, so give the control its own required for form validation. The layout control puts the label in its four places: above: the default, orientation="vertical". columns: orientation="horizontal", every value starting at one column. end: row, one line of a FieldGroup with the value at its end. A framed field is a pill there and takes --field-row-control-width, as its width cannot follow what is typed; pill={'{false}'} on the control keeps the rounded box. hidden: hideLabel. The label still names the control for screen readers; the placeholder shows what to type, and a description moves under the field. On Phone a field is always a cell of a FieldGroup on the grouped background, as in an iOS form, in the same four places: the label above its value (row orientation="vertical"), values in one column (FieldGroup columns), the value at the end of the row, or the placeholder alone (row hideLabel), its value starting at the row's edge. The row is the field's frame, so a framed or soft field loses its frame. The error stands inside the cell, under the value. The words that explain a field go in the group's footer, and a required field says so in its placeholder, as iOS account forms do. A disabled field dims its label with its value. A one-time code is the exception: OTPInput keeps its own digit cells on the screen, outside a group, as in Verify email.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Field label="Name" required>
<Input placeholder="Jane Appleseed" />
</Field>
<Field
label="Email"
required
description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
errorMessage="Enter a valid email address."
>
<Input type="email" defaultValue="jane@example" />
</Field>

// Phone: a cell of a FieldGroup; the words that explain it go in the footer.
<FieldGroup footer="We'll never share your email with anyone else.">
<Field row label="Name" orientation="vertical">
  <Input placeholder="Required" />
</Field>
<Field row label="Email" orientation="vertical" errorMessage="Enter a valid email address.">
  <Input type="email" defaultValue="jane@example" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>

// columns: <FieldGroup columns> with rows; end: rows; hidden: placeholder only
<Field row hideLabel label="Name">
<Input placeholder="Name" />
</Field>
```

### Group
FieldGroup holds the rows and draws the hairlines between them. Its title names the group, description stands under the title, action at the end of the header, and footer under the rows; paragraphs of a footer stand apart. columns starts every value at one column, --field-row-column-width into the row. headerProminence="increased" makes the title lead its content, as a section of a page. On Phone the standard title is the quiet heading of an iOS list, and the increased one is the list's prominent header, 20pt Semibold in the primary label. A ghost text button in the header is the list header's action: tinted text on the title's last line, with a 44pt target. The footer is 13/16 Footnote, its paragraphs one empty line apart, as in Settings.
```tsx
<FieldGroup
title="Billing address"
headerProminence="increased"
action={<Button color="primary" variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={clear}>Clear</Button>}
footer={<p>Your bank checks this address against your card. <TextLink href="/billing">Learn more</TextLink></p>}
columns
>
<Field row label="Street">
  <Input placeholder="Required" value={street} onChange={(event) => setStreet(event.target.value)} />
</Field>
<Field row label="City">
  <Input placeholder="Required" value={city} onChange={(event) => setCity(event.target.value)} />
</Field>
<Field row label="Postcode">
  <Input placeholder="Required" value={postcode} onChange={(event) => setPostcode(event.target.value)} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Other controls
Field works with any form control. A native one, such as a Textarea, is named by the label's htmlFor. A Select or DatePicker trigger is not a native form control, so Field points its aria-labelledby at the label, and the trigger adds its value: a screen reader hears "Role, Editor". A child with a name of its own (aria-label, aria-labelledby or label) keeps it. On Phone a Select or a date is the value at the end of its row, and a long text stands under its label. A group of checkboxes, radios or switches is a row per choice: see Checkbox, Radio Group and Switch.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Field label="Role" description="What this person can change.">
<Select value={role} onChange={(option) => setRole(option.value)} options={roles} />
</Field>
<Field label="Starts">
<DatePicker placeholder="Select date" value={start} onChange={setStart} />
</Field>
<Field label="Notes">
<Textarea placeholder="Anything the team should know" rows={3} />
</Field>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Role">
  <Select value={role} onChange={(option) => setRole(option.value)} options={roles} />
</Field>
<Field row label="Starts">
  <DatePicker triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy" triggerShowIcon={false} placeholder="Select date" value={start} onChange={setStart} />
</Field>
<Field row label="Notes" orientation="vertical">
  <Textarea placeholder="Anything the team should know" rows={3} autoResize />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Label action
Use labelAction for a link or a small control that acts on the field, at the end of the label row: a password reset, a template switch, a "Replace" link. It takes the label's font size.
