On Phone a row has no label line to hold it: the link stands under the group in the rows' text, as under the Apple Account sign-in. A group's footer is a footnote, for words to read.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Field
label="Password"
labelAction={<TextLink href="/reset-password">Forgot password?</TextLink>}
>
<Input type="password" placeholder="Enter password" />
</Field>

// Phone
<div className="flex flex-col">
<FieldGroup>
  <Field row label="Password">
    <Input type="password" placeholder="Required" />
  </Field>
</FieldGroup>
<TextLink primary href="/reset-password" className="mt-[15px] self-start text-[length:var(--field-row-label-font-size)] leading-[var(--field-row-label-line-height)]">
  Forgot password?
</TextLink>
</div>
```

### Several controls
For more than one control, or a control that needs its props placed by hand, pass a function as children. It receives {'{ id, "aria-labelledby", "aria-describedby", "aria-invalid" }'}: put the id and aria-labelledby on the first control, so the label names it, and give the others an aria-label of their own. On a phone a birthday is one row and one value, whose wheel sets the day, the month and the year, as in Contacts. PlexUI has no such wheel, so this example has no Phone view.
```tsx
<Field label="Birthday">
{(fieldProps) => (
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <div className="w-[130px]">
      <Select id={fieldProps.id} aria-labelledby={fieldProps["aria-labelledby"]} placeholder="Month" options={months} value={month} onChange={(option) => setMonth(option.value)} />
    </div>
    <div className="w-[84px]">
      <Select aria-label="Day" placeholder="Day" options={days} value={day} onChange={(option) => setDay(option.value)} />
    </div>
    <div className="w-[96px]">
      <Select aria-label="Year" placeholder="Year" options={years} value={year} onChange={(option) => setYear(option.value)} />
    </div>
  </div>
)}
</Field>
```

### Sizing
The label and description scale with the child control: Field reads the control's size, so {''} gets a lg label without repeating it. Pass size to Field to set the label size yourself, or when the child is a render prop. On a phone a row sets the field's height, insets and type, so this example has no Phone view. Outside a row, with touch.css a text field is 44px from 3xs to 2xl and 50px at 3xl, with the 17px text of iOS.
```tsx
<Field
label="Email"
description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
errorMessage="Enter a valid email address."
required
>
<Input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" size="md" />
</Field>
```

### Optical alignment
Use opticallyAlign="start" to apply a negative margin on the child control, aligning its text with the surrounding content. Works with pill inputs. The label, description, and error message stay at the container edge while the control extends past it. A phone row has no frame to align, so this example has no Phone view.
```tsx
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<div className="border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md py-6 px-8">
  <div className="mb-5 text-secondary text-sm">opticallyAlign="start"</div>
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-5">
    <Field label="Full name" opticallyAlign="start">
      <Input placeholder="Jane Doe" />
    </Field>
    <Field
      label="Email"
      description="We'll never share your email."
      errorMessage="Enter a valid email address."
      required
      opticallyAlign="start"
    >
      <Input placeholder="jane@example.com" />
    </Field>
  </div>
  <Button className="mt-6" color="primary" variant="soft">Submit</Button>
</div>
</div>
```

## File Upload
Mobile-first file upload with MIME-type and size validation, multi-file selection, error states, and read-only file cards.
Import: import { FileUpload, FileCard, FileCardGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/FileUpload"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/file-upload
Props:
  - variant ("compact" | "area") default: "compact" — Visual variant: compact button or larger tappable area
  - label (string) — Button label text
  - description (string) — Helper text below the icon (area variant only)
  - accept (string) — Accepted file types (e.g. ".pdf,.png,image/*")
  - multiple (boolean) default: false — Allow selecting multiple files. Without it, a new pick replaces the current file
  - maxFiles (number) — Maximum number of files. In multiple mode, the button disables at the limit. Single-file mode keeps the button available for replacement.
  - maxSize (number) — Maximum file size in bytes
  - value (File[]) — Controlled file list
  - onValueChange ((files: File[]) => void) — Callback when files are added or removed
  - onFileReject ((file: File, reason: string) => void) — Callback when a file is rejected (wrong type, too large, over limit)
  - errorMessage (string) — Error message. Sets the invalid visual state
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid state (auto-set when errorMessage is provided)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable all interactions
  - id (string) — Id of the hidden file input
  - className (string) — Additional CSS class
  FileCard:
    - file (File) — The file to display
    - onRemove (() => void) — Remove callback. When omitted, the delete button is hidden.
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the remove button
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class
  FileCardGroup:
    - children (ReactNode) — FileCard elements
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class

### Overview
The example starts with three files: the list stands under the button, each file with a type icon, its name truncated in the middle, its size and a remove button. Toggle errorMessage and disabled while keeping the selected files. The error control demonstrates a supplied message; it does not validate the number of files. Accepted types and size limits still apply.
```tsx
function Example({ errorMessage = false, disabled = false }) {
const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>(initialFiles);

return (
  <div className="w-[360px]">
    <FileUpload
      accept=".pdf,.png,.jpg,.jpeg"
      multiple
      maxFiles={5}
      maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024}
      value={files}
      onValueChange={setFiles}
      errorMessage={errorMessage ? "Please upload at least 2 documents." : undefined}
      disabled={disabled}
    />
  </div>
);
}
```

### File list
One file is a list of one. Turn off onRemove for read-only cards. After keyboard removal, focus moves to the next file, then the previous one, or the Files removed status when the list becomes empty, without scrolling. Pointer removal does not move focus if the remove button was not focused.
```tsx
function removeFileWithFocus(root, index, remove) {
  const buttons = Array.from(root?.querySelectorAll('button:not(:disabled)') ?? []);
  const source = buttons[index];
  const target = buttons[index + 1] ?? buttons[index - 1] ?? root?.querySelector('[data-file-removal-status]');
  const doc = source?.ownerDocument;
  const restore = source !== undefined && doc?.activeElement === source;
  remove();
  if (!restore || !source || !doc || !(target instanceof HTMLElement)) return;
  queueMicrotask(() => {
    if (!source.isConnected && target.isConnected && (doc.activeElement === doc.body || doc.activeElement === source)) {
      target.focus({ preventScroll: true });
    }
  });
}

function Example({ onRemove = true }) {
const cards = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>(initialFiles);

return (
  <div ref={cards} className="w-[360px]">
    {files.length > 0 && <FileCardGroup>
      {files.map((file, index) => (
        <FileCard
          key={`${file.name}-${file.size}`}
          file={file}
          onRemove={onRemove ? () => removeFileWithFocus(cards.current, index, () => setFiles((prev) => prev.filter((_, i) => i !== index))) : undefined}
        />
      ))}
    </FileCardGroup>}
    <div role="status" tabIndex={-1} data-file-removal-status className={files.length > 0 ? "sr-only" : "text-center text-sm text-tertiary"}>
      {files.length > 0 ? "" : "Files removed"}
    </div>
  </div>
);
}
```

## Float Input
Text input whose label floats above the value, with error and helper text, a clear button, a password reveal toggle, and a multi-line variant.
Import: import { FloatingLabelInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/floating-label-input
  FloatingLabelInput:
    - label (string) — Required. Floating label text
    - value (string) — Controlled value, with onChange
    - defaultValue (string) — Initial value when uncontrolled
    - errorMessage (string) — Validation message below input; sets invalid state
    - invalid (boolean) default: false (true if errorMessage) — Invalid visual state
    - description (ReactNode) — Helper text below the input
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable input interactions
    - readOnly (boolean) default: false — Read-only input state
    - type (string) default: "text" — Input type; password gets a reveal toggle
    - revealable (boolean) default: true for password without an endAdornment — Built-in reveal toggle
    - multiline (boolean) default: false — Render as an auto-growing textarea
    - rows (number) default: 2 — Initial visible text lines when multiline is true
    - labelPlacement ("border" | "inside") default: "border" — Where the label rests once it floats. inside keeps it in the box, with the value under it, and always takes the rounded box
    - pill (boolean) default: true — Pill shape; false takes the rounded box of the other fields
    - allowAutofillExtensions (boolean) default: false — Let password-manager extensions decorate the input
    - startAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered before the input, inside the field. Always shown; keeps the label floated
    - endAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered after the input, before the clear button
    - onClear (() => void) — Shows a clear button when the input has a value; focus returns to the input
    - onRevealedChange ((revealed: boolean) => void) — Called when the reveal toggle is clicked
    - onAutofill (() => void) — Called when the browser autofills the input
  FloatingLabelSelect:
    - label (string) — Required. Floating label text
    - selected (boolean) default: false — Whether a value is selected: floats the label and shows the children
    - open (boolean) default: false — Whether the attached list is open
    - errorMessage (string) — Validation message below the field; sets invalid state
    - invalid (boolean) default: false (true if errorMessage) — Invalid visual state
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the field
    - labelPlacement ("border" | "inside") default: "border" — Where the label rests once it floats. inside keeps it in the box, with the value under it, and always takes the rounded box
    - pill (boolean) default: true — Pill shape; false takes the rounded box of the other fields
    - onClearClick (() => void) — Shows a clear button when a value is selected
    - onInteract (() => void) — Called on pointer down and on the keys that open the field. Without it those keys click the field, so a wrapping trigger opens

### Overview
```tsx
// Desktop
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" />

// Phone: a cell of a FieldGroup, named by its placeholder.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row hideLabel label="Email address">
  <Input type="email" placeholder="Email address" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Types
Two things set the type: where the label rests, and the shape of the field. An empty field shows the label as a placeholder, so the difference appears once it has a value or the focus. Text fields, textareas and selects work the same in each. On Phone the label does not float, so this example has no Phone view.
```tsx
<div className="grid w-[44rem] max-w-[calc(100vw-5rem)] grid-cols-1 items-center gap-x-4 gap-y-6 py-8 sm:grid-cols-[10rem_1fr_1fr]">
<div className="max-sm:hidden" />
<div className="text-sm text-secondary max-sm:hidden">Empty</div>
<div className="text-sm text-secondary max-sm:hidden">Filled</div>
<div className="text-sm">
  <div>Label on the border</div>
  <div className="text-secondary">Pill</div>
</div>
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" />
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@example.com" />
<div className="text-sm">
  <div>Label on the border</div>
  <div className="text-secondary">Rounded box</div>
</div>
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" pill={false} />
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@example.com" pill={false} />
<div className="text-sm">
  <div>Label inside</div>
  <div className="text-secondary">Rounded box</div>
</div>
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" labelPlacement="inside" />
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@example.com" labelPlacement="inside" />
</div>
```

### Label inside
Use labelPlacement="inside" on FloatingLabelInput and FloatingLabelSelect for long forms such as an address: the label stays inside the box, with the value under it. It works with multiline, adornments, errors and the clear button, and always takes the rounded box. On Phone a cell names its field with the placeholder, so this example has no Phone view.
```tsx
const [country, setCountry] = useState("es")
const label = countries.find((option) => option.value === country)?.label
const trigger = useCallback(
({ open }: { open: boolean }) => (
  <FloatingLabelSelect label="Country or region" labelPlacement="inside" selected={!!label} open={open}>
    {label}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
),
[label],
)

<div className="flex w-[360px] flex-col gap-3">
<FloatingLabelInput label="Full name" labelPlacement="inside" defaultValue="Jane Doe" />
<Select
  value={country}
  options={countries}
  onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
  block
  trigger={trigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
<FloatingLabelInput label="Address line 1" labelPlacement="inside" />
<FloatingLabelInput label="Delivery notes" labelPlacement="inside" multiline />
</div>
```

### Rounded box
Set pill={'{false}'} to take the rounded box of Input and Select, with the label on the border. Both floating fields follow the same two tokens, so a form can set its radius and gutter in one place. On Phone the cell is the frame, so this example has no Phone view.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" pill={false} />
```

### Textarea
Use multiline to render an auto-growing textarea with the same floating-label treatment. The textarea starts at 2 rows and grows automatically as content is added. The border radius adjusts to half the input height. On Phone the cell grows with a Textarea that starts at one line.
```tsx
// Desktop
<FloatingLabelInput label="Message" multiline />

// Phone: the cell grows with the text.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row hideLabel label="Message">
  <Textarea placeholder="Message" rows={1} autoResize />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Password input
A type="password" field ships a built-in reveal toggle: click the eye to show or hide the value. Set revealable to false to remove it. On Phone the cell holds an Input with an Input.AdornmentButton at its end, as on the Input page.
```tsx
// Desktop
<FloatingLabelInput label="Password" type="password" />

// Phone: the reveal button stands at the end of the cell.
const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false)

<FieldGroup>
<Field row hideLabel label="Password">
  <Input
    placeholder="Password"
    type={visible ? "text" : "password"}
    endAdornment={
      <Input.AdornmentButton aria-label={visible ? "Hide" : "Show"} aria-pressed={visible} onClick={() => setVisible((v) => !v)}>
        {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
      </Input.AdornmentButton>
    }
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Phone input
A country code selector paired with a FloatingLabelInput that uses startAdornment to show the dial code as a non-editable prefix. The prefix is always shown, and it keeps the label floated. The country list, its search predicate and trigger, CountryOptionView, formatPhoneNumber and dialCodeOf are helpers of the example. On Phone the country and the number are two linked rows of one group, as in the Sign up (phone) form, so this example has no Phone view.
```tsx
const [country, setCountry] = useState("es")
const [phone, setPhone] = useState("")
const phoneInputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)

<div className="w-[360px] flex flex-col gap-3">
<Select
  value={country}
  options={phoneCountryOptions}
  onChange={(option) => {
    setCountry(option.value)
    setTimeout(() => phoneInputRef.current?.focus(), 0)
  }}
  searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
  OptionView={CountryOptionView}
  searchPredicate={phoneCountrySearchPredicate}
  listMinWidth={360}
  block
  size="3xl"
  trigger={phoneCountryTrigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
<FloatingLabelInput
  ref={phoneInputRef}
  label="Phone number"
  value={phone}
  onChange={(evt) => setPhone(formatPhoneNumber(evt.target.value.replace(/\D/g, ""), country))}
  type="tel"
  inputMode="tel"
  startAdornment={<span className="text-tertiary whitespace-nowrap select-none mr-2">{dialCodeOf(country)}</span>}
/>
</div>
```

### Select
Use FloatingLabelSelect for plain text dropdowns. The label floats up when a value is selected, matching FloatingLabelInput styling. On Phone the cell holds a plain Select named by its placeholder.
```tsx
// Desktop
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"
import { Select } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"

const [role, setRole] = useState("")
const selected = roles.find((option) => option.value === role)
// Select expects a stable trigger renderer
const trigger = useCallback(
({ open }: { open: boolean }) => (
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Role"
    selected={!!selected}
    open={open}
    onClearClick={selected ? () => setRole("") : undefined}
  >
    {selected?.label}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
),
[selected],
)

<div className="w-[360px]">
<Select
  value={role}
  options={roles}
  onChange={(option) => setRole(option.value)}
  searchPlaceholder="Search roles..."
  listMinWidth={360}
  block
  trigger={trigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
</div>

// Phone: a cell named by the placeholder.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row hideLabel label="Role">
  <Select value={role} options={roles} onChange={(option) => setRole(option.value)} placeholder="Role" block />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Multiple selection
Pair FloatingLabelSelect with a multiple Select to collect several values while keeping the floating-label treatment. The trigger shows the selected count and exposes a clear button that resets the whole list. On Phone this is the cell of the Select example with a multiple Select, so it has no Phone view.
```tsx
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"
import { Select } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"

const [skills, setSkills] = useState<string[]>([])
const hasSelection = skills.length > 0
const display =
skills.length === 1
  ? (skillOptions.find((option) => option.value === skills[0])?.label ?? "")
  : skills.length > 1
    ? `${skills.length} skills`
    : ""
const trigger = useCallback(
({ open }: { open: boolean }) => (
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Skills"
    selected={hasSelection}
    open={open}
    onClearClick={hasSelection ? () => setSkills([]) : undefined}
  >
    {display}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
),
[hasSelection, display],
)

<div className="w-[360px]">
<Select
  multiple
  clearable
  value={skills}
  options={skillOptions}
  onChange={(options) => setSkills(options.map((option) => option.value))}
  searchPlaceholder="Search skills..."
  listMinWidth={360}
  block
  trigger={trigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
</div>
```

### Country select
Use FloatingLabelSelect alongside FloatingLabelInput for consistent form styling. The select trigger shares the same floating-label visual shell. The label floats up when a value is selected. CountryLabel is a helper of the example that shows a flag next to the name. On Phone this is the cell of the Select example with a flag in its options, so it has no Phone view.
```tsx
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"
import { Select, type Option } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"

// Outside the component: Select needs a stable OptionView
const CountryOptionView = ({ value, label }: Option) => <CountryLabel code={value} label={label} />

const [country, setCountry] = useState("")
const selected = countries.find((option) => option.value === country)
const trigger = useCallback(
({ open }: { open: boolean }) => (
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Country"
    selected={!!selected}
    open={open}
    onClearClick={selected ? () => setCountry("") : undefined}
  >
    {selected && <CountryLabel code={selected.value} label={selected.label} />}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
),
[selected],
)

<div className="w-[360px]">
<Select
  value={country}
  options={countries}
  onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
  searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
  OptionView={CountryOptionView}
  listMinWidth={360}
  block
  trigger={trigger}
  checkPosition="end"
/>
</div>
```

### States
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("")

// Desktop
<FloatingLabelInput
  label="Email address"
  value={value}
  onChange={(evt) => setValue(evt.target.value)}
  errorMessage="Email is not valid."
  description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
  onClear={() => setValue("")}
/>

// Phone: a cell of a FieldGroup, named by its placeholder. The description goes in the
// group's footer, the error stands inside the cell.
<FieldGroup footer="We'll never share your email with anyone else.">
  <Field row hideLabel label="Email address" errorMessage="Email is not valid.">
    <Input
      type="email"
      placeholder="Email address"
      value={value}
      onChange={(evt) => setValue(evt.target.value)}
      onClear={() => setValue("")}
    />
  </Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

## Index Bar
"The section index of a phone list: a column of letters at the trailing edge that jumps to a section under the finger, as the iOS section index does. Desktop lists have no index, so an index bar never renders from 768px up."
Import: import { IndexBar } from "@plexui/ui/components/IndexBar"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/index-bar
Props:
  - items (string[]) — The titles of the sections, in order: usually letters, such as A to Z and #
  - onSelect ((item: string, index: number) => void) — Called with the title and the index of the section to show: on a press, on each new letter while dragging, and from the keys
  - id (string) — The id of the index bar
  - aria-label (string) default: "Section index" — Name of the index bar
  - aria-controls (string) — The id of the list the index scrolls
  - onFocus ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the index bar gains focus
  - onBlur ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the index bar loses focus
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the strip of the index bar

### Overview
Put the bar in a Page, or in any positioned container that holds the list: it runs down the trailing edge, centred between the bars of a Page (or the safe areas), as iOS centres its index, its letters 14px apart and centred 8px from the edge, in the info color, as native iOS draws its tint (Contacts and the iOS 27 kit). The rows keep the margins of the list, and the letters sit in the trailing one, as in Contacts. A press shows the section of the letter under the finger, and a drag moves through the sections letter by letter; onSelect receives the title and its index, and the list scrolls itself there. Where the letters do not fit, as in a short sheet, every other letter gives way to a dot, as UIKit&apos;s index does, and a drag over a dot still reaches the letters behind it.
```tsx
const content = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Title>Countries</Toolbar.Title>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content ref={content}>
  {sections.map(({ letter, names }) => (
    <FieldGroup key={letter} title={letter} data-section={letter}>...</FieldGroup>
  ))}
</Page.Content>
<IndexBar
  items={sections.map(({ letter }) => letter)}
  onSelect={(letter) => scrollToSection(content.current, letter)}
/>
</Page>
```

## Indicators
Loading and progress indicators, from circular spinners and determinate progress rings to animated dots, with configurable color and stroke.
Import: import { LoadingIndicator, CircularProgress, LoadingDots } from "@plexui/ui/components/Indicator"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/indicators
  LoadingIndicator:
    - size (number | string) default: "1em" — Size in px or any CSS length. Defaults to 20px with the optional touch stylesheet, also inside a field. Also accepts --indicator-size.
    - strokeWidth (number) default: 2 — Ring stroke or mobile spoke width in px. Mobile spokes default to the iOS 27 kit proportion: 2/14 of the size up to 16px, 4/30 to 27px, 5/35 from 28px.
  CircularProgress:
    - progress (number) — Static progress 0-100 (disables the simulated animation)
    - done (boolean) default: false — Fills the ring and ends the simulated progress
    - maxDuration (number) default: 15000 — Duration of the simulated progress in ms
    - size (number | string) default: "28px" — Diameter in px or any CSS length
    - strokeWidth (number) default: 2 — Stroke thickness in px, capped at 4
    - trackColor (string) — Track color (CSS variable or value)
    - trackActiveColor (string) — Active segment color

### Overview
The demos restart every few seconds through a done flag that fills the ring before the simulation starts over.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-6">
<LoadingIndicator size={20} />
<CircularProgress size={24} />
<LoadingDots />
</div>
```

### LoadingIndicator
Simple spinning indicator for general loading states.
```tsx
<LoadingIndicator />
```

### Sizing & stroke
By default, the indicator adapts to the surrounding font-size and color of text. You can control the size of the LoadingIndicator using the --indicator-size CSS custom property.
```tsx
<LoadingIndicator size={30} strokeWidth={2} />
```

### Color
The indicator defaults to currentcolor, inheriting the surrounding text color. This can also be customized by altering the --indicator-color variable around the DOM scope of the component.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-danger">
<LoadingIndicator size={16} /> <span>Destroying forever...</span>
</div>
```

### Duration
You can control the rotation speed of the spinner with --indicator-rotate-duration.
```tsx
<div style={{ '--indicator-rotate-duration': '3s' } as React.CSSProperties}>
<LoadingIndicator />
</div>
```

### CircularProgress
Circular progress ring with simulated progress animation.
```tsx
<CircularProgress />
```

### Progress
Use progress to show static progress and prevent the animation.
```tsx
<CircularProgress progress={25} />
```

### Sizing & stroke
Use size and strokeWidth. Or use --circular-progress-size and --circular-progress-stroke CSS variables.
```tsx
<CircularProgress size={30} strokeWidth={2} />
```

### Color
Customize the color of the indicator with the --circular-progress-track-color and --circular-progress-track-active-color variables.
```tsx
<CircularProgress trackColor="var(--alpha-15)" trackActiveColor="var(--gray-1000)" />
```

### LoadingDots
Indicate typing progress with staggered pulsing dot animation.
```tsx
<LoadingDots />
```

### Color
The indicator defaults to currentcolor, inheriting the surrounding text color. You can customize the color by providing a different color value or context.
```tsx
<div className="text-danger">
<LoadingDots />
</div>
```

### Phone spinner
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-6">
<LoadingIndicator size={14} />
<LoadingIndicator />
<LoadingIndicator size={35} />
</div>
```

## Input Group
Input or textarea with icons, text, buttons and menus attached inside one frame, inline or as header and footer rows, in every input size and style.
Import: import { InputGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/InputGroup"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/input-group
Props:
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Control height, on the same scale as Input (22px to 48px)
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style of the frame
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded frame, with pill buttons inside
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disables the control and the buttons inside
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid border; sets aria-invalid on the control
  - className (string) — Applied to the root <div>
  InputGroup.Addon:
    - align ("inline-start" | "inline-end" | "block-start" | "block-end") default: "inline-start" — Before or after the control on its line, or a row above or below it
    - className (string) — Applied to the addon <div>

### Overview
Put an InputGroup.Input and one or more InputGroup.Addons inside an InputGroup. The group draws the frame and passes size, pill, disabled and invalid down to the control and the buttons.
```tsx
// Desktop
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search..." />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <Search />
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>12 results</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>

// Phone: the group is the value of a row; with a prefix the rows take columns.
<FieldGroup columns>
<Field row label="Website" errorMessage={invalid ? "Enter a valid address." : undefined}>
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup disabled={disabled} invalid={invalid}>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} placeholder="acme.com" inputMode="url" autoCapitalize="none" spellCheck={false} />
      <InputGroup.Addon>
        <InputGroup.Text>https://</InputGroup.Text>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field row label="Amount">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup disabled={disabled}>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} placeholder="0.00" inputMode="decimal" />
      <InputGroup.Addon>
        <InputGroup.Text>$</InputGroup.Text>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Variants
Use variant to stylize the group, like Input. On Phone the row is the frame, so a group in a row keeps the default outline, which the row draws without a border, and the row places the value: at its end, or, with columns, at one column shared by the group's rows.
```tsx
// Desktop
<InputGroup variant="outline">...</InputGroup>
<InputGroup variant="soft">...</InputGroup>

// Phone: the row is the frame and places the value.
<FieldGroup title="Value at the end">
<Field row label="Distance">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} defaultValue="5" inputMode="decimal" />
      <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
        <InputGroup.Text>km</InputGroup.Text>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<FieldGroup title="Values in a column" columns>
<Field row label="Handle">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} placeholder="username" autoCapitalize="none" spellCheck={false} />
      <InputGroup.Addon>
        <InputGroup.Text>@</InputGroup.Text>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field row label="Price">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} placeholder="0.00" inputMode="decimal" />
      <InputGroup.Addon>
        <InputGroup.Text>€</InputGroup.Text>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Sizes
Every Input size from 3xs to 3xl. Icons, text and InputGroup.Button scale with the group: buttons in inline addons fit the control height and keep a 4px inset. On a phone with touch.css, 3xs to xl are all 44px, and in a row the row sets the height: the iOS 26 field is one 52px row, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
// Desktop
<InputGroup size="lg">
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search..." />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <Search />
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Button>Search</InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>

// Phone: one size, the 52px row.
<FieldGroup columns>
<Field row label="Domain">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} defaultValue="plexui.com" inputMode="url" autoCapitalize="none" spellCheck={false} />
      <InputGroup.Addon>
        <InputGroup.Text>https://</InputGroup.Text>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Align
Use align on InputGroup.Addon to place it before (inline-start, the default) or after (inline-end) the control, or as a row above (block-start) or below (block-end) it. Place addons after the control in the markup so the tab order starts with the field; align handles the visual position. On Phone the inline addons stay in the row (see Variants), a block-start text becomes the row's label and a block-end text the group's footer.
```tsx
// Desktop
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Ada Lovelace" />
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-start">
  <InputGroup.Text>Full name</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>

// Phone: block-start text is the row's label, block-end text the group's footer.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Full name">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} placeholder="Ada Lovelace" />
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<FieldGroup footer="Amount in USD">
<Field row label="Amount">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} placeholder="0.00" inputMode="decimal" />
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Text
Use InputGroup.Text for prefixes, suffixes, units and counters. Clicking text or icons in an addon focuses the field.
```tsx
// Desktop
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="0.00" inputMode="decimal" />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <InputGroup.Text>$</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>USD</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>

// Phone: a prefix in a row; a counter is the group's footer.
<FieldGroup columns>
<Field row label="Page">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} placeholder="docs" autoCapitalize="none" spellCheck={false} />
      <InputGroup.Addon>
        <InputGroup.Text>plexui.com/</InputGroup.Text>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<FieldGroup footer={`${280 - post.length} characters left`}>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Post">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" placeholder="What's happening?" maxLength={280} value={post} onChange={(event) => setPost(event.target.value)} autoResize rows={2} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Button
InputGroup.Button is a Button that defaults to ghost and secondary and takes its size from the group. Pass uniform for icon buttons.
```tsx
// Desktop
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search the docs..." />
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Button variant="soft">Search</InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>

// Phone: the main action is the button under the rows.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Link">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} defaultValue="plexui.com/r/input-group" readOnly />
      <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
        <InputGroup.Button uniform aria-label="Copy link">
          <Copy />
        </InputGroup.Button>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field row label="Card">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} placeholder="Card number" inputMode="numeric" autoComplete="cc-number" />
      <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
        <InputGroup.Button uniform aria-label="Scan card">
          <CameraPhoto />
        </InputGroup.Button>
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<Button color="primary" size="3xl" pill block>Pay</Button>
```

### Dropdown
Wrap an InputGroup.Button in a Menu to pick a unit of measurement next to the value.
```tsx
const WEIGHT_UNITS = [
{ value: "kg", label: "Kilograms" },
{ value: "lb", label: "Pounds" },
{ value: "st", label: "Stones" },
]
const LENGTH_UNITS = [
{ value: "cm", label: "Centimeters" },
{ value: "m", label: "Meters" },
{ value: "in", label: "Inches" },
{ value: "ft", label: "Feet" },
]
const [weightUnit, setWeightUnit] = useState("kg")
const [lengthUnit, setLengthUnit] = useState("cm")

// Desktop: the unit is a button with a menu at the end of the field.
const unitMenu = (units, unit, setUnit, label) => (
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <InputGroup.Button aria-label={`${label} unit`}>
      {unit}
      <ChevronDownMd />
    </InputGroup.Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={160}>
    {units.map((item) => (
      <Menu.CheckboxItem
        key={item.value}
        checked={unit === item.value}
        onCheckedChange={() => setUnit(item.value)}
        indicatorVariant="ghost"
      >
        {item.label} ({item.value})
      </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    ))}
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
)

return (
<>
  <InputGroup>
    <InputGroup.Input defaultValue="72" inputMode="decimal" aria-label="Weight" />
    <InputGroup.Addon>
      <InputGroup.Text>Weight</InputGroup.Text>
    </InputGroup.Addon>
    <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
      {unitMenu(WEIGHT_UNITS, weightUnit, setWeightUnit, "Weight")}
    </InputGroup.Addon>
  </InputGroup>
  <InputGroup>
    <InputGroup.Input defaultValue="180" inputMode="decimal" aria-label="Height" />
    <InputGroup.Addon>
      <InputGroup.Text>Height</InputGroup.Text>
    </InputGroup.Addon>
    <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
      {unitMenu(LENGTH_UNITS, lengthUnit, setLengthUnit, "Height")}
    </InputGroup.Addon>
  </InputGroup>
</>
)

// Phone: the label names the value; the unit after it is a pop-up button in the accessory tone.
const phoneUnitMenu = (units, unit, setUnit) => (
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <InputGroup.Button aria-label={`Unit: ${unit}`} className="text-secondary font-normal">
      {unit}
      <span className="ms-1"><DropdownIcon iconType="dropdown" /></span>
    </InputGroup.Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content align="end" minWidth="auto">
    {units.map((item) => (
      <Menu.CheckboxItem
        key={item.value}
        checked={unit === item.value}
        onCheckedChange={() => setUnit(item.value)}
        indicatorPosition="start"
        indicatorVariant="ghost"
      >
        {item.label}
      </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    ))}
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
)

<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Weight">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} defaultValue="72" inputMode="decimal" />
      <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
        {phoneUnitMenu(WEIGHT_UNITS, weightUnit, setWeightUnit)}
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field row label="Height">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} defaultValue="180" inputMode="decimal" />
      <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
        {phoneUnitMenu(LENGTH_UNITS, lengthUnit, setLengthUnit)}
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Spinner
Show a LoadingIndicator in an addon while a value is searched, checked or saved. On a phone with touch.css an indicator in a field is 20px, the iOS 27 Regular spinner, as a standalone one is.
```tsx
// Desktop
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input defaultValue="Saving changes" readOnly />
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>Saving...</InputGroup.Text>
  <LoadingIndicator />
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>

// Phone: a value being checked; in a field the indicator is the kit's Small 22.
<FieldGroup footer="Checking availability...">
<Field row label="Username">
  {(control) => (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroup.Input {...control} defaultValue="ada" autoCapitalize="none" spellCheck={false} />
      <InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
        <LoadingIndicator />
      </InputGroup.Addon>
    </InputGroup>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Textarea
With InputGroup.Textarea, use block-start and block-end addons for a header and a footer. Utility classes such as ml-auto push a button to the far side.
```tsx
// Desktop
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Textarea placeholder="console.log('Hello, world!');" rows={4} className="font-mono" />
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-start">
  <InputGroup.Text>
    <FileCode />
    script.js
  </InputGroup.Text>
  <InputGroup.Button uniform aria-label="Copy" className="ml-auto">
    <Copy />
  </InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>Line 1, Column 1</InputGroup.Text>
  <InputGroup.Button variant="solid" color="primary" className="ml-auto">
    Run
    <Play />
  </InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>

// Phone: the header is the row's label, the status line the group's footer.
<FieldGroup footer="Line 1, Column 1">
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="script.js">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" placeholder="console.log('Hello, world!');" rows={4} className="font-mono" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<Button color="primary" size="3xl" pill block>Run</Button>
```

## Input
Text input with start and end adornments, a clear button, a password visibility toggle, and presets for SSN and birthday.
Import: import { Input } from "@plexui/ui/components/Input"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/input
Props:
  - variant ("outline" | "soft" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Visual style of the input; ghost has no border and no fill
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Controls the size of the input
  - gutterSize ("2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Controls gutter on the edges; defaults to value from size
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disables the input visually and from interactions
  - readOnly (boolean) default: false — Makes the input read-only and hides the clear button
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark the input as invalid
  - allowAutofillExtensions (boolean) default: type === "password" || !!name — Allow autofill extensions to appear in the input
  - autoSelect (boolean) default: false — Select all contents of the input when mounted
  - startAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the start of the input
  - endAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the end of the input
  - onClear (() => void) — When provided, displays a clear button that appears when the input has a value
  - onAutofill (() => void) — Called when the browser autofills the input
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded pill shape
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Applies a negative margin using the current gutter to optically align with surrounding content
  Input.AdornmentButton:
    - color (SemanticColor) — Tint of the pressed (aria-pressed="true") state; the neutral primary-soft tint when unset
    - type (string) default: "button" — Button type

### Overview
```tsx
// Desktop
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." />

// Phone: the input is the value of a row.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Email">
  <Input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Variants
Use variant to stylize the input. ghost has no border and no fill, for a field its container already frames, such as the search line at the top of a dialog; it still turns red when invalid. The state control shows each variant empty, with a value, invalid and disabled. You decide how the invalid state is removed, whether that's through onFocus, onChange, an onSubmit handler, etc.; [data-invalid] is applied to the container for custom styling. disabled greys the input out and prevents user interactions. On Phone the row is the frame, and the value stands in one of three places: at the end of the row, at one column for the whole group with FieldGroup columns, or under the label with orientation="vertical". A row has no frame to color, so an error is the row's errorMessage under it.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-[320px]">
<Input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" variant="outline" />
<Input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" variant="soft" />
<Input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" variant="ghost" />
</div>

// States
<Input type="email" defaultValue="jane@example.com" />
<Input type="email" defaultValue="jane@example" invalid />
<Input type="email" defaultValue="jane@example.com" disabled />

// Phone: the value at the end of the row, at one column, or under the label.
<FieldGroup title="Value at the end">
<Field row label="Name">
  <Input placeholder="Required" defaultValue="Jane Appleseed" />
</Field>
<Field row label="Email" errorMessage="Enter a valid email address.">
  <Input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" defaultValue="jane@example" invalid />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<FieldGroup title="Values in a column" columns>
<Field row label="Name">
  <Input placeholder="Required" defaultValue="Jane Appleseed" />
</Field>
<Field row label="Email">
  <Input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<FieldGroup title="Value under the label">
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Name">
  <Input variant="ghost" placeholder="Required" defaultValue="Jane Appleseed" disabled />
</Field>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Email">
  <Input variant="ghost" type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" disabled />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Sizing & roundness
Sizing of the input is controlled with size and gutterSize props. size sets the input to a specific control height, and gutterSize sets the horizontal padding. Each size provides default values for gutterSize, as well as font-size. Each of these values can be overridden independently. On Phone, a row sets the input's height, insets and type, and with touch.css the 3xs to xl sizes are all 44px, so this example has no Phone switch.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5 justify-start items-start w-[320px]">
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." size="lg" />
<Input placeholder="Search..." startAdornment={<Search className="fill-tertiary" />} size="lg" />
<Input value={username} placeholder="Username" onChange={(evt) => setUsername(evt.target.value)} maxLength={16} endAdornment={<span className="mt-[1.5px] tabular-nums text-tertiary text-[.875em]">{username.length}/16</span>} />
</div>

// Phone: the row sets the height, insets and type.
<FieldGroup columns>
<Field row label="Name">
  <Input placeholder="Enter text..." />
</Field>
<Field row label="Username">
  <Input value={username} placeholder="Required" onChange={(evt) => setUsername(evt.target.value)} maxLength={16} endAdornment={<span className="tabular-nums text-secondary">{username.length}/16</span>} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Adornments
Add arbitrary content to the beginning of an input with startAdornment, like a search icon, or to its end with endAdornment, like a character counter or custom icon; position switches between the two. Ideally, the spacing will look pretty good by default. If you need to customize the spacing: gutterSize determines the amount of spacing on the edges of the container, which you can fine-tune as needed (if you need precise spacing not supported by gutterSize, use a negative margin on your adornment directly, e.g. -ml-2). The spacing between the adornment and the input is controlled with gap on the container, which you can customize as needed with Tailwind classes. On Phone, search is the Toolbar search field; in a row a start adornment is a prefix of the value, such as a currency, and trailing text-secondary text takes the row's accessory color.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Input
placeholder="Search"
startAdornment={<Search className="fill-tertiary" />}
/>
<Input
placeholder="Username"
value={username}
onChange={(evt) => setUsername(evt.target.value)}
maxLength={16}
endAdornment={
  <span className="mt-[1.5px] tabular-nums text-tertiary text-[.875em]">
    {username.length}/16
  </span>
}
/>

// Phone: a prefix of the value, which starts at the column, or trailing text.
<FieldGroup columns>
<Field row label="Amount">
  <Input placeholder="0.00" inputMode="decimal" startAdornment={<span className="text-secondary">$</span>} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Username">
  <Input placeholder="Required" value={username} onChange={(evt) => setUsername(evt.target.value)} maxLength={16} endAdornment={<span className="tabular-nums text-secondary">{username.length}/16</span>} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Clear button
Use the onClear prop to display a built-in clear button. The button appears when the input has a value and is not disabled or read-only. Clicking it keeps focus in the input.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Input
placeholder="Enter text..."
value={value}
onChange={(evt) => setValue(evt.target.value)}
onClear={() => setValue("")}
pill
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Name">
  <Input placeholder="Enter text..." value={value} onChange={(evt) => setValue(evt.target.value)} onClear={() => setValue("")} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Password with visibility toggle
Combine endAdornment with an Input.AdornmentButton to switch between type="password" and type="text". Works across all sizes, variants, and with pill. On Phone, the button stands at the end of the row.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Input
placeholder="Password"
type={visible ? 'text' : 'password'}
endAdornment={
  <Input.AdornmentButton aria-pressed={visible} onClick={toggle}>
    {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
  </Input.AdornmentButton>
}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Password">
  <Input
    placeholder="Required"
    type={visible ? 'text' : 'password'}
    endAdornment={
      <Input.AdornmentButton aria-pressed={visible} onClick={toggle}>
        {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
      </Input.AdornmentButton>
    }
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### SSN input
A masked SSN field that formats input as XXX-XX-XXXX, hides digits behind bullets when masked, and reveals the value via an Input.AdornmentButton in endAdornment. An inline mask suffix highlights the next expected segment. Adapts to all sizes automatically. On Phone the row is the input's frame, and the overlay needs a wrapper that the row cannot frame: the field formats as you type and hides as a secure field.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Input
placeholder="Social Security Number"
value={formatted}
inputMode="numeric"
endAdornment={
  <Input.AdornmentButton aria-pressed={visible} onClick={toggle}>
    {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
  </Input.AdornmentButton>
}
style={!visible && rawDigits ? { color: 'transparent', caretColor: 'var(--color-text)' } : undefined}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="SSN">
  <Input
    placeholder="XXX-XX-XXXX"
    value={formatted}
    type={visible ? 'text' : 'password'}
    maxLength={11}
    inputMode="numeric"
    autoComplete="off"
    allowAutofillExtensions={false}
    endAdornment={
      <Input.AdornmentButton aria-pressed={visible} onClick={toggle}>
        {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
      </Input.AdornmentButton>
    }
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Birthday input
A date-of-birth input with inline formatting that inserts separators as you type (MM / DD / YYYY). An inline mask suffix highlights the next expected segment. Works across all sizes, variants, and with pill. On Phone the field formats as you type and the pattern is its placeholder, as in the About you form.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Input
placeholder="Birthday (MM / DD / YYYY)"
value={birthday}
inputMode="numeric"
maxLength={14}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Birthday">
  <Input placeholder="MM / DD / YYYY" value={birthday} inputMode="numeric" maxLength={14} autoComplete="bday" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Birthday with validation
Use invalid and FieldError to display a validation state when the entered date is not valid. On Phone, give the message to the row's Field as errorMessage: it stands under the row.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Input
placeholder="Birthday (MM / DD / YYYY)"
value={birthday}
inputMode="numeric"
invalid={!!errorMessage}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Birthday" errorMessage={errorMessage}>
  <Input placeholder="MM / DD / YYYY" value={birthday} inputMode="numeric" maxLength={14} invalid={!!errorMessage} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Behavior
Pass autoSelect to select all text in the input, useful when pairing with other copy actions. This prop behaves like an imperative action when toggled and allows selection to change. By default, autofill extensions are prevented by Input. For the occasions where you want browser extensions to be present, pass allowAutofillExtensions to remove the disabling. When name is passed, or type is set to "password", this value will default to true. Both behave the same in a phone row, so this example has no Phone switch.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Input autoSelect placeholder="Add text..." defaultValue="Toggle to auto select" />
<Input allowAutofillExtensions name="email" placeholder="Allowed" />

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Name">
  <Input autoSelect placeholder="Add text..." defaultValue="Toggle to auto select" />
</Field>
<Field row label="Email">
  <Input allowAutofillExtensions name="email" placeholder="Allowed" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### With button
You can pair Input and Button components together by using the same size value. On Phone, the button is the 50px main action under the group, size="3xl".
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="flex gap-2">
<Input placeholder="jane.doe@gmail.com" size="lg" variant="outline" />
<Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="outline" pill={false}>Subscribe</Button>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Email">
  <Input type="email" placeholder="jane.doe@gmail.com" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<Button color="primary" size="3xl" pill block>Subscribe</Button>
```

### Optical alignment
```tsx
// Desktop
<Field label="Full name" opticallyAlign="start">
<Input placeholder="Jane Doe" pill />
</Field>
<Field
label="Email"
description="We'll never share your email."
errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address."
required
opticallyAlign="start"
>
<Input placeholder="jane@example.com" pill />
</Field>
<Button className="mt-6" color="primary" variant="soft" pill>
Submit
</Button>

// Phone: the help is the group's footer.
<FieldGroup footer="We'll never share your email.">
<Field row label="Full name">
  <Input placeholder="Jane Doe" />
</Field>
<Field row label="Email" errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address.">
  <Input placeholder="jane@example.com" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
<Button color="primary" size="3xl" pill block>Submit</Button>
```

## Kbd
A key or a keyboard shortcut, such as ⌘K, set inline in text, in a tooltip or at the end of a menu item.
Import: import { Kbd } from "@plexui/ui/components/Kbd"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/kbd
Props:
  - size ("xs" | "sm" | "md") default: "sm" — Height and text size: 16px, 20px or 24px
  - variant ("soft" | "outline") default: "soft" — soft fills the key, outline draws its edge; both mix the text color
  - className (string) — Applied to the kbd element

### Overview
Kbd renders a {''} element: the semantic tag for keyboard input. It sits on the text baseline, so it can stand in a sentence.
```tsx
<p>
Press <Kbd>/</Kbd> to search, <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to close.
</p>
```

### Shortcut
Use Kbd.Group for keys pressed together. Each key keeps its own frame.
```tsx
<Kbd.Group>
<Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
<Kbd>K</Kbd>
</Kbd.Group>

<Kbd.Group>
<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>
<Kbd>P</Kbd>
</Kbd.Group>
```

### Sizes and variants
Three sizes: xs (16px) for tooltips and menu items, sm (20px, default) for text, md (24px) next to larger controls. soft (default) fills the key, outline draws its edge. Both mix the surrounding text color, so a key reads on a page, in a dark tooltip and in a highlighted menu item alike.
```tsx
<Kbd size="xs">⌘K</Kbd>
<Kbd size="sm">⌘K</Kbd>
<Kbd size="md">⌘K</Kbd>

<Kbd variant="outline">⌘K</Kbd>
```

### In a tooltip and a menu
Show a control's shortcut in its tooltip, or at the end of a menu item. Kbd only shows the keys: announce the shortcut to assistive technology with aria-keyshortcuts on the control that has it.
```tsx
<Tooltip
content={
  <span className="flex items-center gap-2">
    Search
    <Kbd.Group>
      <Kbd size="xs">⌘</Kbd>
      <Kbd size="xs">K</Kbd>
    </Kbd.Group>
  </span>
}
>
<Button color="secondary" variant="outline" uniform aria-label="Search" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K">
  <Search />
</Button>
</Tooltip>

<Menu.Item onSelect={undo}>
<span className="flex-1">Undo</span>
<Kbd size="xs" variant="outline">⌘Z</Kbd>
</Menu.Item>
```

## Label
Accessible form label that points at any control by its id, so clicking it focuses or toggles the control, with consistent typography across forms.
Import: import { Label } from "@plexui/ui/components/Label"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/label
Props:
  - htmlFor (string) default: — — id of the associated control. Clicks on the label focus or activate the control.
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <label> element

### Overview
Clicking the label toggles the checkbox it points at. Here accepted starts as true. On Phone the label takes the body type of a list row, 17/22 regular, the same as the labels of Checkbox, Switch and a Field row.
```tsx
const [accepted, setAccepted] = useState(true);

return (
<div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <Checkbox id="terms" checked={accepted} onCheckedChange={setAccepted} />
  <Label htmlFor="terms">Accept terms and conditions</Label>
</div>
);
```

## Markdown Editor
Compact rich text editor powered by Tiptap, embedded in a form field, with a markdown formatting toolbar, variants, and an invalid state.
Import: import { MarkdownEditor } from "@plexui/ui/components/MarkdownEditor"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/markdown-editor
Props:
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style of the editor
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the editor
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark as invalid
  - placeholder (string) — Placeholder text when empty
  - value (string) — Controlled markdown value
  - defaultValue (string) — Initial markdown for uncontrolled mode
  - onChange ((markdown: string) => void) — Called on content change
  - toolbarEnd (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the end of the toolbar
  - rows (number) default: 1 — Minimum visible rows
  - id (string) — id of the editable element (Field sets it)
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible name of the editable element
  - aria-labelledby (string) — Id of the element that names the editor, such as a visible label
  - aria-describedby (string) — aria-describedby of the editable element (Field sets it)
  - aria-invalid (boolean) — Sets aria-invalid on the editable element and the invalid style (Field sets it with errorMessage)
  - className (string) — Applied to the container

### Placeholder
Use placeholder for empty content. Toggle invalid and disabled without replacing the entered markdown. The invalid state is controlled by this example, not by a validator.
```tsx
function Example({ invalid = false, disabled = false }) {
const [value, setValue] = useState("");

return (
  <MarkdownEditor aria-label="Markdown content" placeholder="Enter text..."
    value={value} onChange={setValue} invalid={invalid} aria-invalid={invalid} disabled={disabled} />
);
}
```

### All formatting
Example with all supported formatting: bold, italic, links, ordered lists, and unordered lists. Click inside formatted text to see toolbar buttons toggle.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor defaultValue={allFormattingMd} />
```

### With Field
Wrap with Field to add a description and a linked error message. The editor receives id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid automatically. Set an accessible name with aria-label. The errorMessage control demonstrates the error state without validating or replacing the content.
```tsx
function Example({ errorMessage = false }) {
const [value, setValue] = useState("");

return (
  <Field label="Description" description="Supports bold, italic, lists, and links."
    errorMessage={errorMessage ? "This field is required." : undefined}>
    <MarkdownEditor aria-label="Description" placeholder="Enter description..."
      value={value} onChange={setValue} />
  </Field>
);
}
```

### Toolbar end slot
Use toolbarEnd to render custom content at the end of the toolbar, for example an &ldquo;Edit translations&rdquo; button. markdownEditorStyles.toolbarButton gives it the style of the built-in toolbar buttons.
```tsx
import { MarkdownEditor, markdownEditorStyles } from "@plexui/ui/components/MarkdownEditor"
import { Translate } from "@plexui/ui/components/Icon"

<Field label="Text markdown">
<MarkdownEditor
  placeholder="Enter text..."
  toolbarEnd={
    <button
      type="button"
      className={markdownEditorStyles.toolbarButton}
      aria-label="Edit translations"
      title="Edit translations"
    >
      <Translate />
    </button>
  }
/>
</Field>
```

### Variants
Use variant to switch between outline (default) and soft styles.
```tsx
<Field label="Outline">
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Outline variant..." variant="outline" />
</Field>
<Field label="Soft">
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Soft variant..." variant="soft" />
</Field>
```

## Markdown
Markdown renderer for rich formatted content, with headings, lists, tables, code blocks, and KaTeX math expressions out of the box.
Import: import { Markdown } from "@plexui/ui/components/Markdown"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/markdown
Props:
  - children (string) — Required. Markdown source
  - includeMath (boolean) default: false — Enable LaTeX math rendering
  - breakNewLines (boolean) default: false — Turn single newlines into line breaks
  - copyableCodeBlocks (boolean) default: true — Show a copy button on code blocks
  - collapsibleCodeBlocks (boolean) default: true — Render code blocks in the collapsible view with a View Code button
  - components (Record<string, MarkdownComponent>) — Tag name to component overrides, applied over the built-in ones
  - directives (MarkdownDirective[]) — Custom directives, each rendered by its own component
  - remarkPlugins (PluggableList) — Extra remark plugins, after the built-in ones
  - rehypePlugins (PluggableList) — Extra rehype plugins
  - allowedElements (string[]) — Only render these elements
  - disallowedElements (string[]) — Never render these elements
  - skipHtml (boolean) default: false — Ignore raw HTML in the source
  - urlTransform ((url: string) => string) — Rewrites URLs; the default drops unsafe protocols (javascript:) and keeps tel: and sms:
  - className (string) — Applied to the wrapping element

### Overview
Use Markdown to render rich markdown text.
```tsx
<Markdown>{markdownContent}</Markdown>
```

### Math
Use includeMath to enable LaTeX rendering. The KaTeX styles and fonts come with @plexui/styles, so formulas need no other setup.
```tsx
<Markdown includeMath>{markdownWithLatex}</Markdown>
```

## Menu
Dropdown menu for structured actions with grouped items, submenus, checkbox and radio items, and horizontal layouts.
Import: import { Menu } from "@plexui/ui/components/Menu"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/menu
Props:
  - forceOpen (boolean) — Keep menu open (controlled)
  - onOpen (() => void) — Called when menu opens
  - onClose (() => void) — Called when menu closes
  - modal (boolean) default: false — Whether menu is modal (focus trap)
  Menu.Trigger:
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent the menu from opening
  Menu.Content:
    - width (number | "auto") default: fits content, 250 on a phone — Panel width in px. Without it the panel fits its content, or with touch.css on a phone is 250px, as an iOS menu; "auto" fits the content there too
    - minWidth (number | "auto") default: 300 — Minimum panel width in px (vertical layout)
    - maxHeight (number) — Maximum panel height in px
    - pill (boolean) default: false — Rounder list with fully rounded rows, for menus beside pill controls. Menu.SubContent takes it too
    - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred placement. Without it, and without sideOffset, a menu on a phone opens upward from a trigger in the lower half of the screen
    - sideOffset (number) default: 5 — Distance from the trigger in px. Without it a menu on a phone covers its trigger
    - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Alignment relative to trigger
    - alignOffset (number) default: -5 — Offset from the start or end alignment in px. 0 with center alignment, and on a phone when the menu covers its trigger
    - layout ("vertical" | "horizontal") default: "vertical" — Layout direction. Use horizontal for icon toolbars
    - size ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Size of horizontal menu items (icon size + padding)
    - onCloseAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called before focus returns to the trigger; call event.preventDefault() to keep it from moving there
    - onOpenAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called before focus moves into the menu as it opens; call event.preventDefault() to leave focus where it is, as for a menu that stands open when its screen appears
  Menu.Item:
    - description (ReactNode) — Second line under the label. The label turns semibold on its own
    - onSelect ((event: Event) => void) — Called when item is selected; call event.preventDefault() to keep the menu open
    - onClick ((event: MouseEvent) => void) — Called when the item is clicked; also makes the item interactive
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the item
    - danger (boolean) default: false — Destructive action: the item is drawn in the danger color
    - className (string) — Applied to the item
  Menu.Header:
    - media (ReactNode) — Picture before the title: an image, an icon or an Avatar in a 32px square (40px on a phone). An image or icon fills it; an image gets small rounded corners
    - description (ReactNode) — Line under the title, such as the kind and size of a file
    - action (ReactNode) — Round action at the end: a Menu.HeaderAction
    - className (string) — Applied to the header
  Menu.HeaderAction:
    - aria-label (string) — Accessible name of the icon-only action (required)
    - onSelect ((event: Event) => void) — Called when the action is pressed; call event.preventDefault() to keep the menu open
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the action
  Menu.CheckboxItem:
    - checked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Checked state
    - onCheckedChange ((checked: boolean) => void) — When checkbox toggles
    - onSelect ((event: Event) => void) — Use with preventDefault() to keep menu open
    - indicatorPosition ("start" | "end") default: "end" — Checkbox position
    - indicatorVariant ("solid" | "ghost") default: "solid" — Checkbox indicator style
    - disabled (boolean) — Disable the item

### Overview
A folder's menu, as Files opens it on iOS: actions with their icons, then the view and the sort order as radio items, Date with its order under it (description) while it is the chosen sort, and Group By in a submenu. Turn off icons for the same menu in plain text, and checkmarks for the folder's actions alone, a shorter menu with no checkmark column. pill on Menu.Content makes a rounder list with fully rounded rows, for menus beside pill controls. On a phone each example is a screen whose menu opens from the More button of its top bar, as iOS opens the menu of an album in Photos. There the panel covers the button, its top and end at the button's top and end, and is the 250px panel of iOS menus, so the phone code leaves out width, minWidth and size. A pill menu is the same panel there, so the phone view leaves out pill.
```tsx
// Desktop
const [icons] = useState(true)
const [checkmarks] = useState(true)
const [pill] = useState(false)
const [view, setView] = useState("list")
const [sort, setSort] = useState("date")
const [group, setGroup] = useState("date")

<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Downloads <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth={220} pill={pill}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>{icons && <CheckCircle />} Select</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>{icons && <FolderPlus />} New Folder</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>{icons && <FileDocument />} Scan Documents</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>{icons && <Desktop />} Connect to Server</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  {checkmarks && (
    <>
      <Menu.RadioGroup value={view} onChange={setView}>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="icons">{icons && <VideoGrid />} Icons</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="list">{icons && <List />} List</Menu.RadioItem>
      </Menu.RadioGroup>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.RadioGroup value={sort} onChange={setSort}>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="name">Name</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="kind">Kind</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="date" description={sort === "date" ? "Newest to Oldest" : undefined}>Date</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="size">Size</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="tags">Tags</Menu.RadioItem>
      </Menu.RadioGroup>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Sub>
        <Menu.SubTrigger>Group By</Menu.SubTrigger>
        <Menu.SubContent>
          <Menu.RadioGroup value={group} onChange={setGroup}>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="none">None</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="kind">Kind</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="date">Date</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="size">Size</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="shared">Shared by</Menu.RadioItem>
          </Menu.RadioGroup>
        </Menu.SubContent>
      </Menu.Sub>
    </>
  )}
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>View Options</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>

// Phone: the More button of the top bar opens the menu
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
  <Toolbar.Title>Overview</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Menu>
    <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
    <Menu.Content align="end">
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>{icons && <CheckCircle />} Select</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>{icons && <FolderPlus />} New Folder</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>{icons && <FileDocument />} Scan Documents</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>{icons && <Desktop />} Connect to Server</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Separator />
      {checkmarks && (
        <>
          <Menu.RadioGroup value={view} onChange={setView}>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="icons">{icons && <VideoGrid />} Icons</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="list">{icons && <List />} List</Menu.RadioItem>
          </Menu.RadioGroup>
          <Menu.Separator />
          <Menu.RadioGroup value={sort} onChange={setSort}>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="name">Name</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="kind">Kind</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="date" description={sort === "date" ? "Newest to Oldest" : undefined}>Date</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="size">Size</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="tags">Tags</Menu.RadioItem>
          </Menu.RadioGroup>
          <Menu.Separator />
          <Menu.Sub>
            <Menu.SubTrigger>Group By</Menu.SubTrigger>
            <Menu.SubContent>
              <Menu.RadioGroup value={group} onChange={setGroup}>
                <Menu.RadioItem value="none">None</Menu.RadioItem>
                <Menu.RadioItem value="kind">Kind</Menu.RadioItem>
                <Menu.RadioItem value="date">Date</Menu.RadioItem>
                <Menu.RadioItem value="size">Size</Menu.RadioItem>
                <Menu.RadioItem value="shared">Shared by</Menu.RadioItem>
              </Menu.RadioGroup>
            </Menu.SubContent>
          </Menu.Sub>
        </>
      )}
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>View Options</Menu.Item>
    </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Natural sizing
Menu supports several sizing strategies:Natural sizing: use minWidth="auto" to have the menu fit naturally to the size of the content.Fixed size: use width and minWidth to set the menu to a fixed size, regardless of content size.Flexible sizing: minWidth can be used by itself to describe a menu that must be a given size, but can grow larger depending on its content.Max sizing: apply max-width to the children of Menu.Content. maxWidth isn't exposed as a prop because it's reserved for Radix variables used in collision detection.Desktop only: on a phone a menu is the 250px panel of iOS menus, unless it sets a width or a larger minimum width of its own.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost" className="font-semibold gap-1.5"><Tools /> Tools</Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth="auto">
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Functions height={18} width={18} /> Function</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Search height={18} width={18} /> File Search</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Globe height={18} width={18} /> Web Search</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Code height={18} width={18} /> Code Interpreter</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><ImageSquare height={18} width={18} /> Image Generation</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Horizontal (icons only)
Set layout="horizontal" on Menu.Content for an icon toolbar. Give each icon-only item a visually hidden label so screen readers can name the action. Desktop only: iOS has no row of icons alone; on a phone a horizontal row is the labelled mode switch at the top of a menu, as in Mode switch below.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Actions <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content layout="horizontal" size="md" minWidth="auto">
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><EditPencil /><span className="sr-only">Edit</span></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><SettingsCog /><span className="sr-only">Settings</span></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Play /><span className="sr-only">Play</span></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><UnfoldHorizontal /><span className="sr-only">Expand</span></Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Mode switch
Set layout="horizontal" on a Menu.RadioGroup at the top of a menu for a mode switch: one mode of several, the options side by side, each an icon over its label, with the chosen one on a fill, above the list, as Photos orders by Added or by Captured. The options are radio items, so the fill moves with the value, no radio indicator is drawn, and choosing one closes the menu, as any item does. On a phone with touch.css they are equal 56px-tall tiles with a 20px icon over a 12px label, 10px from the panel's edges, the chosen one on black at 12%, as in Photos. Phone only: the mode switch is an iOS pattern, which desktop menus do not have; there modes are radio items of the list, as in Radio items below.
```tsx
const [sort, setSort] = useState("added")
const [filter, setFilter] = useState("all")

<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
  <Toolbar.Title>Mode switch</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Menu>
    <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
    <Menu.Content align="end">
      <Menu.RadioGroup layout="horizontal" value={sort} onChange={setSort}>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="added"><Clock /> Added</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="captured"><CameraPhoto /> Captured</Menu.RadioItem>
      </Menu.RadioGroup>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Label>Filter</Menu.Label>
      <Menu.RadioGroup value={filter} onChange={setFilter}>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="all"><Grid /> All items</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="favorites"><Heart /> Favorites</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="edited"><EditPencil /> Edited</Menu.RadioItem>
      </Menu.RadioGroup>
    </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Header
Put a Menu.Header first to name what the menu acts on: a picture, the name and a line under it, with a round Menu.HeaderAction at its end, as the Files menu of a file in iOS opens. The header is not an item; its action is, reached with the arrow keys like the items. On a phone with touch.css the picture is 40px, 16px from the panel's edges, the name 15px Semibold and the line under it 13px; the action is a 34px circle with a 44px target. A separator under the header stands 16px below the picture; without one the first item starts 24px below it. Phone only: the header is an iOS pattern, which desktop menus do not have.
```tsx
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
  <Toolbar.Title>Header</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Menu>
    <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
    <Menu.Content align="end">
      <Menu.Header
        media={<img src="/demo/picture-1.svg" alt="" />}
        description="Image · 382 KB"
        action={<Menu.HeaderAction aria-label="Share" onSelect={() => {}}><Share /></Menu.HeaderAction>}
      >
        Sunset.png
      </Menu.Header>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><EditPencil /> Rename</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Copy /> Copy</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Folder /> Move</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><InfoCircle /> Get info</Menu.Item>
    </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Grouped items
Use Menu.Group and Menu.Label to organize related items into labeled sections. The example is the filter of the message list, as Messages opens it on iOS: the mailboxes, a section labeled Filter By, and Manage Filtering under a separator. Both radio groups hold one value, so one checkmark marks the list shown. On a phone a section label and a row without an icon start after the checkmark column, where the icons of the other rows start, as in iOS menus.
```tsx
// Desktop
const [filter, setFilter] = useState("messages")

<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button variant="ghost" color="primary"><Filter /> Filter <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth={220}>
  <Menu.RadioGroup value={filter} onChange={setFilter}>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="messages"><Chats /> Messages</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="spam"><XSquare /> Spam</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="deleted"><Trash /> Recently Deleted</Menu.RadioItem>
  </Menu.RadioGroup>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Group>
    <Menu.Label>Filter By</Menu.Label>
    <Menu.RadioGroup value={filter} onChange={setFilter}>
      <Menu.RadioItem value="unread"><Chat /> Unread</Menu.RadioItem>
      <Menu.RadioItem value="drafts"><ChatTripleDots /> Drafts</Menu.RadioItem>
    </Menu.RadioGroup>
  </Menu.Group>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Manage Filtering</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>

// Phone: the More button of the top bar opens the menu
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
  <Toolbar.Title>Grouped items</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Menu>
    <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
```
