```tsx
    <Menu.Content align="end">
      <Menu.RadioGroup value={filter} onChange={setFilter}>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="messages"><Chats /> Messages</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="spam"><XSquare /> Spam</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="deleted"><Trash /> Recently Deleted</Menu.RadioItem>
      </Menu.RadioGroup>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Group>
        <Menu.Label>Filter By</Menu.Label>
        <Menu.RadioGroup value={filter} onChange={setFilter}>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="unread"><Chat /> Unread</Menu.RadioItem>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="drafts"><ChatTripleDots /> Drafts</Menu.RadioItem>
        </Menu.RadioGroup>
      </Menu.Group>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Manage Filtering</Menu.Item>
    </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Submenus
A list's menu, as Reminders opens it on iOS: Manage Sections and Sort By open submenus, and Sort By shows the order it has chosen under its label (description on Menu.SubTrigger). Use Menu.Sub, Menu.SubTrigger, and Menu.SubContent for nested menus. On a phone a submenu opens over its menu, as iOS 26 submenus do: its row heads it in Semibold with a separator under it and a chevron that points down, and the menu behind steps back, its rows at half strength and the panel slightly smaller, until the row is tapped again. The menu behind is out of reach while the submenu stands over it: a press on it closes the submenu and chooses nothing, and screen readers skip it, with focus in the submenu. The heading row stays in place and only the items under it scroll in a submenu taller than the screen, so the row that closes it is always in reach.
```tsx
// Desktop
const [sort, setSort] = useState("Manual")

<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform aria-label="List actions">
    <DotsHorizontal />
  </Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={220}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Storyboard /> View as Columns</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><InfoCircle /> Show List Info</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><CheckCircle /> Select Items</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Sub>
    <Menu.SubTrigger><List /> Manage Sections</Menu.SubTrigger>
    <Menu.SubContent>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Plus /> New Section</Menu.Item>
    </Menu.SubContent>
  </Menu.Sub>
  <Menu.Sub>
    <Menu.SubTrigger description={sort}><Sort /> Sort By</Menu.SubTrigger>
    <Menu.SubContent>
      <Menu.RadioGroup value={sort} onChange={setSort}>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="Manual">Manual</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="Due Date">Due Date</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="Creation Date">Creation Date</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="Priority">Priority</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="Title">Title</Menu.RadioItem>
      </Menu.RadioGroup>
    </Menu.SubContent>
  </Menu.Sub>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><EyeOff /> Hide Completed</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><UploadDocuments /> Save as Template</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><FileDocument /> Print</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}} danger><Trash /> Delete List</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>

// Phone: the More button of the top bar opens the menu
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
  <Toolbar.Title>Submenus</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Menu>
    <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
    <Menu.Content align="end">
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Storyboard /> View as Columns</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><InfoCircle /> Show List Info</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><CheckCircle /> Select Items</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Sub>
        <Menu.SubTrigger><List /> Manage Sections</Menu.SubTrigger>
        <Menu.SubContent>
          <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Plus /> New Section</Menu.Item>
        </Menu.SubContent>
      </Menu.Sub>
      <Menu.Sub>
        <Menu.SubTrigger description={sort}><Sort /> Sort By</Menu.SubTrigger>
        <Menu.SubContent>
          <Menu.RadioGroup value={sort} onChange={setSort}>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="Manual">Manual</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="Due Date">Due Date</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="Creation Date">Creation Date</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="Priority">Priority</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="Title">Title</Menu.RadioItem>
          </Menu.RadioGroup>
        </Menu.SubContent>
      </Menu.Sub>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><EyeOff /> Hide Completed</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><UploadDocuments /> Save as Template</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><FileDocument /> Print</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}} danger><Trash /> Delete List</Menu.Item>
    </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Checkbox items
Use Menu.CheckboxItem with checked, onCheckedChange, and {"onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}"} to keep the menu open. The example is the view options of a mailbox, as Mail opens them on iOS: three options that are each on or off, and About Categories under a separator. On a phone with touch.css the checkmark leads the row, as in iOS menus, whatever indicatorPosition and indicatorVariant say, so the phone view leaves out those controls. A row without a checkmark keeps its column, so every icon and label lines up, and a long label wraps under itself.
```tsx
// Desktop
const [view, setView] = useState({
categories: true,
priority: true,
contactPhotos: false,
})

return (
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <Button variant="ghost" color="primary">
      View <ChevronDownMd />
    </Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content minWidth={220}>
    <Menu.Label>View Options</Menu.Label>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={view.categories}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setView((v) => ({ ...v, categories: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      <Storyboard /> Show Categories
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={view.priority}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setView((v) => ({ ...v, priority: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      <Atom /> Show Priority
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={view.contactPhotos}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setView((v) => ({ ...v, contactPhotos: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      <AvatarProfile /> Show Contact Photos
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    <Menu.Separator />
    <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><InfoCircle /> About Categories</Menu.Item>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
)

// Phone: the More button of the top bar opens the menu
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
  <Toolbar.Title>Checkbox items</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Menu>
      <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content align="end">
        <Menu.Label>View Options</Menu.Label>
        <Menu.CheckboxItem
          checked={view.categories}
          onCheckedChange={(checked) => setView((v) => ({ ...v, categories: checked }))}
          onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
          indicatorPosition="end"
          indicatorVariant="solid"
        >
          <Storyboard /> Show Categories
        </Menu.CheckboxItem>
        <Menu.CheckboxItem
          checked={view.priority}
          onCheckedChange={(checked) => setView((v) => ({ ...v, priority: checked }))}
          onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
          indicatorPosition="end"
          indicatorVariant="solid"
        >
          <Atom /> Show Priority
        </Menu.CheckboxItem>
        <Menu.CheckboxItem
          checked={view.contactPhotos}
          onCheckedChange={(checked) => setView((v) => ({ ...v, contactPhotos: checked }))}
          onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
          indicatorPosition="end"
          indicatorVariant="solid"
        >
          <AvatarProfile /> Show Contact Photos
        </Menu.CheckboxItem>
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><InfoCircle /> About Categories</Menu.Item>
      </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Radio items
Use Menu.RadioGroup and Menu.RadioItem for single-selection options. On a phone with touch.css the checkmark leads the row, as in iOS menus, whatever indicatorPosition says, so the phone view leaves out that control.
```tsx
// Desktop
const [value, setValue] = useState("any")

<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" variant="ghost">
    Radio menu <ChevronDownMd />
  </Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content align="start" minWidth="auto" width="auto">
  <Menu.RadioGroup
    indicatorPosition="end"
    value={value}
    onChange={setValue}
  >
    <Menu.RadioItem value="any">Any time</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="today" disabled>Today</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last7d">Last 7 days</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last30d">Last 30 days</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last3m">Last 3 months</Menu.RadioItem>
  </Menu.RadioGroup>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>

// Phone: the More button of the top bar opens the menu
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
  <Toolbar.Title>Radio items</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Menu>
    <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
    <Menu.Content align="end">
      <Menu.RadioGroup
        indicatorPosition="end"
        value={value}
        onChange={setValue}
      >
        <Menu.RadioItem value="any">Any time</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="today" disabled>Today</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="last7d">Last 7 days</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="last30d">Last 30 days</Menu.RadioItem>
        <Menu.RadioItem value="last3m">Last 3 months</Menu.RadioItem>
      </Menu.RadioGroup>
    </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Item actions
Use Menu.ItemActions and Menu.ItemAction for hover actions (e.g. delete) on an item.Accessibility note: these actions are not keyboard accessible due to how Radix Menu works, so they should not be critical actions with no other parity.Desktop only: the rows of an iOS menu carry no actions of their own.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost" className="font-semibold gap-1.5"><History /> Conversations</Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content width={270}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Sample thread title</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Another sample thread title</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Long thread title that is going to be clipped off</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Destructive items
Mark a destructive action (delete, remove, leave) with danger: the label and the highlight take the danger color, and a description keeps its secondary color. Menu.Link takes danger too. Put such items last, after a separator.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform aria-label="More actions">
    <DotsHorizontal />
  </Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={200}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={rename}><EditPencil /> Rename</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={duplicate}><Copy /> Duplicate</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={remove} danger><Trash /> Delete project</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>

// Phone: the More button of the top bar opens the menu
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
  <Toolbar.Title>Destructive items</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Menu>
    <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
    <Menu.Content align="end">
      <Menu.Item onSelect={rename}><EditPencil /> Rename</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={duplicate}><Copy /> Duplicate</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Item onSelect={remove} danger><Trash /> Delete project</Menu.Item>
    </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

## OTP Input
Input for one-time passwords and verification codes, with split digit cells, grouped layouts, error states, and autofill.
Import: import { OTPInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/OTPInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/otp-input
Props:
  - length (number) default: 6 — Number of digit cells
  - value (string) — Controlled value
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called when value changes
  - onComplete ((value: string) => void) — Called when all digits filled
  - grouping (number[]) — Grouping pattern with extra gap (e.g. [3,3])
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid visual state
  - errorMessage (string) — Error message below the input
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable all cells
  - autoFocus (boolean) default: false — Auto-focus first cell on mount
  - className (string) — Applied to the root element

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("")
const [error, setError] = useState(false)
const [disabled, setDisabled] = useState(false)

<OTPInput
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
invalid={error}
errorMessage={error ? "Invalid verification code." : undefined}
disabled={disabled}
/>
```

### Grouped (3+3)
```tsx
<OTPInput grouping={[3, 3]} />
```

## Page Control
A row of dots, one for each page, the current one solid, that shows where a person is in a flat list of pages and moves between them, as the iOS 26 page control does.
Import: import { PageControl } from "@plexui/ui/components/PageControl"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/page-control
Props:
  - count (number) — Number of pages
  - value (number) — Controlled index of the current page, from 0
  - defaultValue (number) default: 0 — Initial page (uncontrolled)
  - onChange ((index: number, details: { scrubbing: boolean }) => void) — Called with the index of the next page; scrubbing is true while a drag scrubs
  - background ("automatic" | "prominent" | "minimal") default: "automatic" — When the capsule behind the dots shows; minimal also turns off scrubbing
  - valueText ((index: number, count: number) => string) default: Page 2 of 5 — Text assistive technology reads for the current page
  - aria-label (string) default: "Pages" — Name of the page control, when no visible label names it
  - aria-labelledby (string) — The id of the visible label of the page control
  - aria-controls (string) — The id of the element that shows the pages
  - id (string) — The id of the page control
  - onFocus (FocusEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>) — Called when the page control gains focus
  - onBlur (FocusEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>) — Called when the page control loses focus
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the page control

### Overview
Tap the leading or trailing side of the current dot for the previous or next page; with a mouse, click a dot. Drag across the dots to scrub, or past either end to reach the first or last page. Scroll the pages without animation while scrubbing, as details.scrubbing tells, and with reduced motion, as motion-reduce:scroll-auto does here.
```tsx
const pagesId = useId()
const scroller = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
const [page, setPage] = useState(0)

<div
id={pagesId}
ref={scroller}
className="flex snap-x snap-mandatory overflow-x-auto scroll-smooth motion-reduce:scroll-auto"
onScroll={(event) => setPage(Math.round(event.currentTarget.scrollLeft / event.currentTarget.clientWidth))}
>
{pages.map((number) => <div key={number} className="w-full shrink-0 snap-center">{number}</div>)}
</div>
<PageControl
count={pages.length}
value={page}
aria-controls={pagesId}
onChange={(index, { scrubbing }) => {
  setPage(index)
  scroller.current?.scrollTo({ left: index * scroller.current.clientWidth, behavior: scrubbing ? 'instant' : 'auto' })
}}
/>
```

### Many pages
From seven pages the dots past a window around the current page shrink to 6px and 4px, suggesting more pages, and the rest hide, as the kit variants show.
```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(0)

<PageControl count={12} value={page} onChange={setPage} />
```

### Background
The capsule behind the dots shows while a pointer presses or scrubs with automatic, always with prominent, for a page control that is the main navigation of the screen, and never with minimal, which also turns off scrubbing since it gives no feedback.
```tsx
<PageControl count={4} />
<PageControl count={4} background="prominent" />
<PageControl count={4} background="minimal" />
```

## Page
"The frame of an app page: header and content share one column, a line comes as the content scrolls, and on a phone the header becomes a floating glass bar."
Import: import { Page } from "@plexui/ui/components/Page"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/page
Props:
  - width ("full" | "wide" | "column") default: "full" — Column that header and content share: edge to edge, 1280px or 768px, centred
  - surface ("plain" | "grouped") default: "plain" — Mobile canvas and field-group palette; desktop colors stay unchanged
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root element
  Page.Header:
    - background ("soft" | "hard" | "glass" | "solid") default: "glass" — How the bar meets the content scrolled under it on a phone, see Background
    - divider (boolean) default: true — Shows a divider once the content has scrolled under the header: on a desktop layout, and on a phone with a hard or glass background
    - className (string) default: — — Applied to the band
  Page.Content:
    - fill (boolean) default: false — The content fills the page and scrolls inside itself, from 768px up
    - onScroll (UIEventHandler) default: — — Called on every scroll, after the page has read the position
    - className (string) default: — — Applied to the element that scrolls

### Overview
The header has no line at rest. Scroll the content: the line comes after 4px and goes again at the top.
```tsx
<Page>
<Page.Header>
  <Page.Bar>
    <Page.Title>Orders</Page.Title>
    <Page.Actions>
      <Button color="primary" pill size="md">New order</Button>
    </Page.Actions>
  </Page.Bar>
</Page.Header>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
</Page>
```

### Widths
The width belongs to the page, so the line, the title, the buttons and the content always stand in one column. Take full for tables, wide for overviews and column for settings and forms. For any other width set --page-width on the page. This frame is narrower than a screen, so the preview shows both widths at half their size. On a phone a page takes the width of the screen at every width, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
<Page width="column">
<Page.Header>...</Page.Header>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
</Page>

<Page width="column" style={{ "--page-width": "860px" }}>...</Page>
```

### Heading
Page.Heading groups the title with metadata. On a phone the badge and subtitle share a second row below the centered title. The header grows when metadata wraps, and the content keeps the corresponding space below it.
```tsx
<Page.Bar>
<Page.Heading>
  <Page.Title>Menu</Page.Title>
  <Page.Subtitle>
    <Badge color="info" size="sm" variant="outline">Draft</Badge>
    <span>Saved a minute ago</span>
  </Page.Subtitle>
</Page.Heading>
<Page.Actions>...</Page.Actions>
</Page.Bar>
```

### Fill
fill stops the page scrolling from 768px up, so a table can scroll inside itself. A table that draws its own line under a sticky head turns the header's off with divider.
```tsx
<Page>
<Page.Header divider={false}>...</Page.Header>
<Page.Content fill>
  <div className="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto">...</div>
</Page.Content>
</Page>
```

### Background
background sets how the header and the footer meet the content scrolled under them on a phone, as a Toolbar does: glass, the header's default, is a translucent, blurred bar with a hairline, soft, the footer's default, fades the canvas color out under a header and leaves the content clear under the footer's actions, as native iOS 26 does, hard is an opaque bar with a line, and solid an opaque bar with no line. Glass and hard show themselves once content is under the bar; divider={false} keeps a header without its line.
```tsx
<Page>
<Page.Header background="hard">...</Page.Header>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
<Page.Footer background="hard">
  <Button color="primary" pill block>New order</Button>
</Page.Footer>
</Page>
```

## Phone Layout
Lays out the components inside it as on a phone at any window width, such as a phone frame on a desktop page, and keeps their dialogs inside its box.
Import: import { PhoneLayout } from "@plexui/ui/components/PhoneLayout"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/phone-layout
Props:
  - className (string) — Class on the box, such as its size and corners
  - style (CSSProperties) — Style on the box

### Overview
The box is the screen of the phone: a Dialog opened inside it portals into the box and covers it instead of the window. Give the box a size; let a child of it scroll rather than the box, so a dialog stays in place.
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

<PhoneLayout style={{ width: 375, height: 600, borderRadius: 40, border: '1px solid var(--color-border)' }}>
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Dialog.Trigger>
    <Button color="primary">New list</Button>
  </Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog.Content mobileVariant="sheet">
    <Dialog.Header>
      <Dialog.Title>New list</Dialog.Title>
    </Dialog.Header>
    <Dialog.Body>
      <Field label="Name">
        <Input placeholder="Groceries" />
      </Field>
    </Dialog.Body>
    <Dialog.Footer>
      <Button color="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Create</Button>
    </Dialog.Footer>
  </Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
</PhoneLayout>
```

### Menu
A menu opened inside the box is a phone menu at any window width: it covers the button that opens it and opens in the box. A submenu opens over its menu, which steps back: a press on the menu behind closes the submenu and chooses nothing, and screen readers skip its rows until then.
```tsx
const [sort, setSort] = useState("Manual")

<PhoneLayout style={{ width: 375, height: 600, borderRadius: 40, border: '1px solid var(--color-border)' }}>
<Page>
  <Toolbar titleStyle="large">
    <Toolbar.Title>Groceries</Toolbar.Title>
    <Toolbar.Trailing>
      <Menu>
        <Menu.Trigger>
          <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
        </Menu.Trigger>
        <Menu.Content align="end">
          <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><CheckCircle /> Select Items</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Sub>
            <Menu.SubTrigger description={sort}><Sort /> Sort By</Menu.SubTrigger>
            <Menu.SubContent>
              <Menu.RadioGroup value={sort} onChange={setSort}>
                <Menu.RadioItem value="Manual">Manual</Menu.RadioItem>
                <Menu.RadioItem value="Due Date">Due Date</Menu.RadioItem>
                <Menu.RadioItem value="Title">Title</Menu.RadioItem>
              </Menu.RadioGroup>
            </Menu.SubContent>
          </Menu.Sub>
          <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}} danger><Trash /> Delete List</Menu.Item>
        </Menu.Content>
      </Menu>
    </Toolbar.Trailing>
  </Toolbar>
</Page>
</PhoneLayout>
```

## Popover
A floating panel for contextual UI, with flexible sizing, hover triggers, a controllable open state and nesting.
Import: import { Popover } from "@plexui/ui/components/Popover"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/popover
Props:
  - open (boolean) — Controlled open state; uncontrolled when omitted
  - onOpenChange ((nextState: boolean) => void) — Called when the popover opens or closes
  - showOnHover (boolean) default: false — Open on hover and focus instead of click
  - hoverOpenDelay (number) default: 150 — Delay before a hover popover opens (ms)
  Popover.Content:
    - width (number | "auto") default: "auto" — Panel width in px
    - minWidth (number | "auto") default: 300 — Minimum panel width in px
    - maxWidth (number) default: 700 — Maximum panel width in px, capped by the space available in the viewport
    - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred placement; flips when it collides
    - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Alignment relative to trigger
    - sideOffset (number) default: 8 — Offset from trigger (px)
    - alignOffset (number) default: -5 — Offset from the start or end alignment (px)
    - avoidCollisions (boolean) default: true — Reposition to stay inside the viewport and scroll containers
    - collisionPadding (number) default: 20 — Space in px to keep from viewport and scroll container boundaries
    - translucent (boolean) default: false — Translucent, blurred surface
    - autoFocus (boolean) default: true — Move focus into the panel when it opens (hover popovers never take focus)
    - data-* (string) — Data attributes land on the panel
    - className (string) — Applied to the panel

### Overview
```tsx
import { useBreakpoint } from '@plexui/ui/hooks/useBreakpoints';

function Example() {
const wide = useBreakpoint('md');
return (
  <Popover>
    <Popover.Trigger><Button color="primary">Generate</Button></Popover.Trigger>
    <Popover.Content side={wide ? 'right' : 'bottom'}>...</Popover.Content>
  </Popover>
);
}
```

### Sizing the popover
The popover can be sized with any combination of width, minWidth, or maxWidth. All popovers default to a minWidth of 300px, and a maxWidth of 700px, capped by the space available in the viewport.
```tsx
<Popover>
<Popover.Trigger>...</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content minWidth="auto" side="top">...</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Open on hover
Use showOnHover to create popovers that appear on hover and focus events. This should be used sparingly and with clear intention. A phone has no hover: a tap opens it, as in the Overview, so this example is desktop only.By default, hover popovers will not alter the focused element on the page, nor restore focus to the trigger on close. However, if interactive content is present in the popover, and tab is used to navigate into the popover, focus will be restored to the trigger on close.
```tsx
import { useBreakpoint } from '@plexui/ui/hooks/useBreakpoints';

function Example() {
const wide = useBreakpoint('md');
return (
  <Popover showOnHover>
    <Popover.Trigger>...</Popover.Trigger>
    <Popover.Content side={wide ? 'right' : 'bottom'}>...</Popover.Content>
  </Popover>
);
}
```

### Using the controller
You can access usePopoverController() controller context from components within Popover.Content. The hook exposes two methods, close() and shake(). They do exactly what you think they do.Attempting to submit an empty form calls the shake() methodAfter the simulated two-second request, close() dismisses the popup. Closing or unmounting cancels the pending request; reopening starts a fresh session.
```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import { Button } from '@plexui/ui/components/Button';
import { Sparkles } from '@plexui/ui/components/Icon';
import { Popover, usePopoverController } from '@plexui/ui/components/Popover';
import { Textarea } from '@plexui/ui/components/Textarea';
import { useBreakpoint } from '@plexui/ui/hooks/useBreakpoints';

function PopoverTextarea({
  value,
  onChange,
}: {
  value?: string;
  onChange?: (next: string) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Textarea
      value={value}
      onChange={(evt) => onChange?.(evt.target.value)}
      aria-label="Prompt"
      variant="ghost"
      gutterSize="xl"
      rows={3}
      className="w-full"
      placeholder="Describe what you're using the model for, and we'll generate system instructions."
    />
  );
}

function PopoverActionBar({ loading }: { loading?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <div className="px-3 pb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
      <div className="flex gap-1.5 items-center font-normal text-sm text-tertiary">
        <Sparkles width={16} height={16} />
        Free beta
      </div>
      <Button color="primary" size="xs" pill={false} loading={loading} type="submit">
        Create
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}

function PopoverControllerForm({ value, onChange, submitting, onSubmit }: {
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  submitting: boolean;
  onSubmit: (close: () => void, shake: () => void) => void;
}) {
  const { shake, close } = usePopoverController();

  const handleSubmit = (evt: FormEvent) => {
    evt.preventDefault();
    onSubmit(close, shake);
  };

  return (
    <form className="pt-2" onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <PopoverTextarea value={value} onChange={onChange} />
      <PopoverActionBar loading={submitting} />
    </form>
  );
}

export function PopoverControllerDemo() {
  const wide = useBreakpoint('md');
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');
  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
  const timer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined>(undefined);
  const session = useRef(0);

  useEffect(() => () => {
    session.current++;
    clearTimeout(timer.current);
  }, []);

  const changeOpen = (next: boolean) => {
    session.current++;
    clearTimeout(timer.current);
    timer.current = undefined;
    if (next) {
      setSubmitting(false);
      setValue('');
    }
    setOpen(next);
  };

  const submitPrompt = (close: () => void, shake: () => void) => {
    if (!value) {
      shake();
      return;
    }
    if (timer.current !== undefined) return;
    setSubmitting(true);
    const currentSession = session.current;
    timer.current = setTimeout(() => {
      if (session.current !== currentSession) return;
      timer.current = undefined;
      close();
    }, 2000);
  };

  return (
    <Popover open={open} onOpenChange={changeOpen}>
      <Popover.Trigger>
        <Button color="primary" pill={false}>Generate</Button>
      </Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Content side={wide ? 'right' : 'bottom'}>
        <PopoverControllerForm value={value} onChange={setValue} submitting={submitting} onSubmit={submitPrompt} />
      </Popover.Content>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

### Confirmation
Confirm a destructive action from the button that asks for it. On a desktop the panel opens above the button. On a phone it covers the button, as iOS 26 presents an action sheet from its source: no Cancel button, since a tap anywhere else cancels, the message in the body text and the action as a 48px capsule. Opening moves focus to the panel, not to the action. Copy the shared styles with the example.
```tsx
import { Button } from '@plexui/ui/components/Button';
import { Popover, usePopoverController } from '@plexui/ui/components/Popover';
import { useBreakpoint } from '@plexui/ui/hooks/useBreakpoints';
import styles from './PopoverConfirmation.module.css';

function ConfirmationBody({ wide }: { wide: boolean }) {
  const { close } = usePopoverController();
  return (
    <>
      <p className={styles.Message}>Are you sure you want to delete this event?</p>
      <Button color="danger" variant="soft" block pill={!wide} className={styles.Action} onClick={close}>
        Delete event
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}

export function PopoverConfirmationDemo() {
  const wide = useBreakpoint('md');
  return (
    <Popover>
      <Popover.Trigger>
        <Button color="danger" variant="soft" size={wide ? 'md' : '3xl'} block={!wide} pill={!wide}>
          Delete event
        </Button>
      </Popover.Trigger>
      {/* On a phone the panel covers its 50px button and ends 16px above the button's bottom edge. */}
      <Popover.Content side="top" sideOffset={wide ? 8 : -34} className={styles.Confirmation}>
        <ConfirmationBody wide={wide} />
      </Popover.Content>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

## Progress Steps
Stepper for multi-step flows like checkouts and onboarding, with horizontal or vertical layout, icons, navigation, and color tokens.
Import: import { ProgressSteps } from "@plexui/ui/components/ProgressSteps"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/progress-steps
Props:
  - current (number) — Required. Current active step (1-based)
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Layout direction
  - size ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Step indicator size
  - color ("default" | "success") default: "default" — Color scheme for completed/active steps
  - connectorStyle ("solid" | "dashed") default: "solid" — Connector line style
  - variant ("default" | "minimal") default: "default" — "minimal" renders a compact bar (requires total)
  - total (number) — Total steps for minimal variant
  - className (string) — Class applied to the container
  ProgressSteps.Step:
    - icon (ReactNode) — Custom icon instead of step number

### Overview
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2}>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Your details</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Please provide your name and email</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Company details</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>A few details about your company</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Invite your team</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Start collaborating with your team</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Add your socials</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Share posts to your social accounts</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Sizes
Use size to control the scale of step indicators.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2} size="md">
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 1</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 2</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 3</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 4</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Vertical
Use orientation="vertical" to display steps in a vertical layout, ideal for sidebar navigation or multi-step forms. The example also shows the dashed connector style. On a phone the four columns of a horizontal row cannot hold a step's description, so the Overview and With Icons examples show the steps vertically there; Overview leaves out its orientation control. Progress steps have no iOS control of their own; With Navigation shows a compact composition for a phone screen. The Overview already shows these vertical steps on a phone, with the dashed connector among its settings, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2} orientation="vertical">...</ProgressSteps>
<ProgressSteps current={3} orientation="vertical" connectorStyle="dashed">...</ProgressSteps>
```

### With Icons
Use icon prop on ProgressSteps.Step to display custom icons instead of step numbers.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={3}>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Email />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Globe />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Users />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Bolt />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### With Navigation
Example of integrating with navigation controls.
```tsx
const steps = ["Your details", "Company details", "Invite your team", "Add your socials"]
const [step, setStep] = useState(1)

return (
<div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-6">
  <ProgressSteps variant="minimal" current={step} total={4} />
  <div className="text-center">
    <h3 className="text-lg font-semibold">Step {step} of 4</h3>
    <p className="text-secondary mt-1">{steps[step - 1]}</p>
  </div>
  <div className="flex gap-3">
    <Button color="secondary" variant="outline" className="w-28" disabled={step === 1} onClick={() => setStep((s) => Math.max(1, s - 1))}>
      Previous
    </Button>
    <Button color="primary" className="w-28" disabled={step === 4} onClick={() => setStep((s) => Math.min(4, s + 1))}>
      Next
    </Button>
  </div>
</div>
)
```

### Minimal
Use variant="minimal" for a compact horizontal bar indicator. Requires total prop.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps variant="minimal" current={3} total={4} color="default" />
```

### Icons Only
Omit Title and Description for a minimal indicator when step details are shown elsewhere.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2}>
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Colors
Use color to change the color scheme of completed and active steps.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={3}>...</ProgressSteps>
<ProgressSteps current={3} color="success">...</ProgressSteps>
```

## Progress
A horizontal bar that shows task completion, with determinate and indeterminate modes, labelled layouts, and smooth value transitions.
Import: import { Progress } from "@plexui/ui/components/Progress"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/progress
Props:
  - value (number | null) default: null — Current progress between 0 and max. Pass null for indeterminate.
  - max (number) default: 100 — Maximum progress value
  - getValueLabel ((value: number, max: number) => string) default: — — Accessible value text (aria-valuetext). Defaults to the rounded percentage, e.g. "67%".
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <div>

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(13);
useEffect(() => {
const t = setTimeout(() => setValue(66), 500);
return () => clearTimeout(t);
}, []);

return <Progress value={value} aria-label="Loading" />;
```

### With label
Pair a Label with a value readout above the bar, the typical upload / onboarding progress pattern.
```tsx
<div>
<div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <Label id="progress-upload-label">Uploading plex-ui.zip</Label>
  <span>3.2 / 4.8 MB</span>
</div>
<Progress aria-labelledby="progress-upload-label" value={67} />
</div>
```

### Controlled
Bind value to any source. Here it follows a Slider.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(50);

return (
<>
  <Progress value={value} aria-label="Progress" />
  <Slider value={value} onChange={setValue} min={0} max={100} step={1} aria-label="Progress value" />
</>
);
```

## Radio Group
Radio group for single-choice selection with row or column layout, right-aligned indicators, rich item content, and card-style options.
Import: import { RadioGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/RadioGroup"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/radio-group
Props:
  - value (string) — Controlled selected value
  - defaultValue (string) — Initial selected value (uncontrolled)
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called when selected option changes
  - direction ("col" | "row") default: "row" — Item flow direction
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the whole group
  - name (string) — Name of the hidden radio inputs submitted with the owning form
  - required (boolean) default: false — Marks the group and every hidden radio input as required
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible group label
  - className (string) — Extra classes on the group element
  RadioGroup.Item:
    - value (string) — Item value
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable this item only
    - required (boolean) — Marks this item as required
    - block (boolean) default: false — Stretch item to fill available width
    - orientation ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Position of the radio indicator relative to the label
    - description (ReactNode) — Second line below the option's label, linked via aria-describedby
    - className (string) — Extra classes on the label element

### Overview
```tsx
const [frequency, setFrequency] = useState("daily")

// Desktop
<RadioGroup direction="col" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} aria-label="Notification frequency">
<RadioGroup.Item value="daily">Daily</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="weekly">Weekly</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="never">Never</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>

// Phone: each option is a row; the selected row ends with a checkmark.
<RadioGroup direction="col" className="w-full" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} aria-label="Notification frequency">
<FieldGroup title="Notification frequency">
  <Field row label="Daily"><RadioGroup.Item value="daily" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Weekly"><RadioGroup.Item value="weekly" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Monthly"><RadioGroup.Item value="monthly" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Never"><RadioGroup.Item value="never" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With Checkbox
Place RadioGroup alongside Checkbox controls to verify that indicator sizes, label baselines, and spacing align consistently in both horizontal and vertical layouts. This check is desktop only: on a phone both live in rows, where the radio is a checkmark and the checkbox a circle at the end of the row.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6 w-full max-w-md">
<Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
  {() => (
    <RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="email" aria-label="Notification channel">
      <RadioGroup.Item value="email">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">Email</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Messages delivered to your inbox.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="sms">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">SMS</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Text messages to your phone number.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="push">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">Push</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Real-time alerts on your device.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field label="Topics" description="Select the topics you want to follow.">
  {() => (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
      <Checkbox defaultChecked label={...} />
      ...
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Descriptions
Combine Field-level label and description with item-level descriptions for options that need additional context. Use a plain label without descriptions when the options are self-explanatory. On a phone the group title, its description and row descriptions do this, as With description and With Field show, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={channel} onChange={setChannel} aria-label="Notification channel">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="email">
          <div className="flex flex-col">
            <span className="font-medium">Email</span>
            <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Messages delivered to your inbox.</span>
          </div>
        </RadioGroup.Item>
        ...
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Notification sound">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={sound} onChange={setSound} aria-label="Notification sound">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="default">Default</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="chime">Chime</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="none">None</RadioGroup.Item>
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

### Direction
Use direction to control whether the items flow in a column or row. An optimal gap will be dynamically applied based on the orientation. A phone list is always a column of rows, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
<RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="light" aria-label="Theme">
<RadioGroup.Item value="light">Light</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="dark">Dark</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="system">System</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Orientation
Use orientation="right" on RadioGroup.Item to place the radio indicator after the label text. Useful for settings lists and card-style selections where the content should lead. In a phone row the checkmark always ends the row, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="w-[320px]" direction="col" defaultValue="medium" aria-label="Text size">
<RadioGroup.Item value="small" orientation="right" block>Small</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="medium" orientation="right" block>Medium</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="large" orientation="right" block>Large</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Group disabled
Use disabled on RadioGroup to disable all radio options. In a phone row the label of a disabled option is dimmed with it.
```tsx
// Desktop
<RadioGroup disabled defaultValue="automatic" aria-label="Video quality">
<RadioGroup.Item value="automatic">Automatic</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="high">High</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="data-saver">Data saver</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>

// Phone
<RadioGroup direction="col" className="w-full" disabled defaultValue="automatic" aria-label="Video quality">
<FieldGroup title="Video quality">
  <Field row label="Automatic"><RadioGroup.Item value="automatic" /></Field>
  <Field row label="High"><RadioGroup.Item value="high" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Data saver"><RadioGroup.Item value="data-saver" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Item disabled
Use disabled on single RadioGroup.Item to disable only that option. A long label wraps; in a phone row it wraps inside the row.
```tsx
// Desktop
<RadioGroup aria-label="Delivery method" direction="col">
<RadioGroup.Item value="standard">Standard shipping (3-5 days)</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="express" disabled>Express shipping (1-2 days)</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="same-day">
  Same-day delivery, available in select metro areas with a minimum order of $50
</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>

// Phone
<RadioGroup direction="col" className="w-full" aria-label="Delivery method">
<FieldGroup title="Delivery method">
  <Field row label="Standard shipping (3-5 days)"><RadioGroup.Item value="standard" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Express shipping (1-2 days)"><RadioGroup.Item value="express" disabled /></Field>
  <Field row label="Same-day delivery, available in select metro areas with a minimum order of $50">
    <RadioGroup.Item value="same-day" />
  </Field>
</FieldGroup>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With description
Use description on an item for a second line under its label. It sits outside the label, so the radio keeps the label as its name and gets the description through aria-describedby; clicking it does not select the option. In a phone row the row's description takes this place.
```tsx
// Desktop
<RadioGroup direction="col" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Spacing">
<RadioGroup.Item value="default" description="Standard spacing for most use cases.">
  Default
</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="comfortable" description="More space between elements.">
  Comfortable
</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="compact" description="Minimal spacing for dense layouts.">
  Compact
</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>

// Phone
<RadioGroup direction="col" className="w-full" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Spacing">
<FieldGroup title="Spacing">
  <Field row label="Default" description="Standard spacing for most use cases."><RadioGroup.Item value="default" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Comfortable" description="More space between elements."><RadioGroup.Item value="comfortable" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Compact" description="Minimal spacing for dense layouts."><RadioGroup.Item value="compact" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With Field
Wrap a RadioGroup in a Field for a shared label and description. Spread the field props from the render prop onto the group so it is described by the Field's description (aria-describedby). On a phone the FieldGroup title and description above the rows take this place.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Field label="Notification method" description="Choose how you want to receive notifications.">
{(fieldProps) => (
  <RadioGroup direction="col" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Notification method" {...fieldProps}>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="email">Email</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="sms">SMS</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="push">Push notification</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
)}
</Field>

// Phone
<RadioGroup direction="col" className="w-full" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Notification method">
<FieldGroup title="Notification method" description="Choose how you want to receive notifications.">
  <Field row label="Email"><RadioGroup.Item value="email" /></Field>
  <Field row label="SMS"><RadioGroup.Item value="sms" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Push notification"><RadioGroup.Item value="push" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With Field error
When a Field has an errorMessage, it sets aria-invalid on the child control for screen readers. The error message is displayed below the group. On a phone a FieldError in the group's footer shows it under the rows; link it to the group with aria-describedby.
```tsx
const errorId = useId()

// Desktop
<Field
label="Subscription plan"
description="Select a plan to continue."
errorMessage={showError ? "Please select a subscription plan." : undefined}
>
{(fieldProps) => (
  <RadioGroup direction="col" aria-label="Subscription plan" {...fieldProps}>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly ($9.99/month)</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="yearly">Yearly ($99.99/year)</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="lifetime">Lifetime ($299.99)</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
)}
</Field>

// Phone
<RadioGroup
direction="col"
className="w-full"
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
aria-label="Subscription plan"
aria-invalid={showError || undefined}
aria-describedby={showError ? errorId : undefined}
>
<FieldGroup
  title="Subscription plan"
  description="Select a plan to continue."
  footer={showError ? <FieldError id={errorId}>Please select a subscription plan.</FieldError> : undefined}
>
  <Field row label="Monthly ($9.99/month)"><RadioGroup.Item value="monthly" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Yearly ($99.99/year)"><RadioGroup.Item value="yearly" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Lifetime ($299.99)"><RadioGroup.Item value="lifetime" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Choice card
Style each radio option as a bordered card with visual selection state. The selected card gets a highlighted border using design tokens. Use orientation="right" to place the indicator after the content. Wrap each RadioGroup.Item in a card container with border and borderRadius on the same element. On a phone a choice with a description is a row, as in With description, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="flex-col w-[320px] gap-3" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Workspace type">
<div style={{
  border: "1px solid",
  borderColor: isSelected ? "var(--color-background-primary-solid)" : "var(--color-border-primary-outline)",
  borderRadius: "var(--radius-lg)",
  backgroundColor: isSelected ? "var(--color-background-primary-soft-alpha)" : undefined,
}}>
  <RadioGroup.Item value="personal" block orientation={orientation} className="gap-3 p-3">
    <div className="flex flex-col flex-1">
      <span className="font-semibold">Personal</span>
      <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">For hobby projects and experimentation.</span>
    </div>
  </RadioGroup.Item>
</div>
...
</RadioGroup>
```

### Card selection
Leverage component composition and className overrides to build card-style radio selections with rich content per option. Desktop only, like Choice card.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="flex-col w-full min-w-0 max-w-[390px] gap-4">
<RadioGroup.Item className="gap-2.5" value="basic">
  <div><h4>Basic Plan</h4><p className="text-secondary text-sm">5 GB storage</p></div>
</RadioGroup.Item>
...
</RadioGroup>
```

### Grouped sections
Use dividers to separate radio groups into logical sections. Each section can be wrapped in a Field with its own label and description.
```tsx
// BackButton is your app's navigation action.
<Page className="h-dvh [--page-content-padding-top:10px] [--page-content-padding-bottom:16px] [--page-footer-gutter:24px] [--page-footer-padding-bottom:max(24px,env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))]">
<Page.Header style={{ paddingTop: 'env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)' }}><Page.Bar><Page.Leading><BackButton /></Page.Leading><Page.Title>Preferences</Page.Title></Page.Bar></Page.Header>
<Page.Content>
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
    <RadioGroup direction="col" className="w-full" value={visibility} onChange={setVisibility} aria-label="Visibility">
      <FieldGroup title="Visibility" description="Control who can see project resources.">
        <Field row label="Hidden"><RadioGroup.Item value="hidden" /></Field>
        <Field row label="Visible to organization owners"><RadioGroup.Item value="owners" /></Field>
        <Field row label="Visible to everyone"><RadioGroup.Item value="everyone" /></Field>
      </FieldGroup>
    </RadioGroup>
    <RadioGroup direction="col" className="w-full" value={view} onChange={setView} aria-label="Default view">
      <FieldGroup title="Default view" description="What opens first in a project.">
        <Field row label="Board"><RadioGroup.Item value="board" /></Field>
        <Field row label="List"><RadioGroup.Item value="list" /></Field>
        <Field row label="Timeline"><RadioGroup.Item value="timeline" /></Field>
      </FieldGroup>
    </RadioGroup>
  </div>
</Page.Content>
</Page>
```

## Select Control
Select control primitive for building custom dropdowns, with variants, sizing, start and dropdown icons, and clearable, loading, and invalid states.
Import: import { SelectControl } from "@plexui/ui/components/SelectControl"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/select-control
Props:
  - selected (boolean) default: false — Whether a value is selected (affects placeholder styling)
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Visual variant
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Control size (3xs to 3xl)
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded trigger
  - StartIcon (ComponentType) — Icon at start
  - onClearClick (() => void) — Enables the clear button when set
  - interactOnEnter (boolean) default: false — Enter interacts too, as on a combobox button. Off by default, as Enter may be an attempt to submit a form
  - onInteract (() => void) — Called on pointer down, ArrowDown, ArrowUp and Space. Without it, a wrapping trigger opens on pointer down
  - dropdownIconType ("chevronDown" | "dropdown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Dropdown indicator style
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid state
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable control
  - block (boolean) default: false — Full width
  - loading (boolean) default: false — Loading state (aria-busy); hides the indicators and ignores interaction
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Optical alignment
  - className (string) — Applied to the control

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("")

// Desktop
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <SelectControl className="w-[200px]" selected={!!value} onClearClick={() => setValue("")} StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>
    {value || "Select date..."}
  </SelectControl>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth={200} width={200}>
  <Menu.RadioGroup value={value} onChange={setValue}>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="Today">Today</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="Last week">Last week</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="Last month">Last month</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="Last 3 months">Last 3 months</Menu.RadioItem>
  </Menu.RadioGroup>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>

// Phone: the control is the value of a row; its label reaches the trigger, and None clears it.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Period">
  {(control) => (
    <Menu>
      <Menu.Trigger>
        <SelectControl {...control} selected={!!value}>
          {value || "None"}
        </SelectControl>
      </Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content minWidth={200} align="end">
        <Menu.RadioGroup value={value} onChange={setValue}>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="">None</Menu.RadioItem>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="Today">Today</Menu.RadioItem>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="Last week">Last week</Menu.RadioItem>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="Last month">Last month</Menu.RadioItem>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="Last 3 months">Last 3 months</Menu.RadioItem>
        </Menu.RadioGroup>
      </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  )}
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Variants
Use the variant prop to stylize the select control. Available variant styles are similar to {""}, but aligned with subtle differences from {""} variant treatments. In a phone row the row is the frame, so this example is desktop only; Invalid and Disabled show the row's states.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="flex w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px] flex-col gap-6">
<SelectControl className="w-full" variant="soft" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
<SelectControl className="w-full" variant="outline" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
<SelectControl className="w-full" variant="ghost" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Folder" errorMessage={invalid ? "Choose a folder you can edit." : undefined}>
  <SelectControl selected invalid={invalid} disabled={disabled}>Sample value</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Sizing & roundness
Sizing of the control is determined with the size prop. Each size provides dynamic values for various aspects of the control, including icon and indicator placement, as well font-size and gutter values.Create fully rounded controls with the pill prop. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied, and the clear action is also set to pill. On Phone the row sets the control's size, so a row's control takes no size or pill, and this example is desktop only.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl size="md" pill={false} dropdownIconType="none">Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md" loading>Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md">Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md" StartIcon={Tools} dropdownIconType="none">Tool calls</SelectControl>
...

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Model">
  <SelectControl>None</SelectControl>
</Field>
<Field row label="Tools">
  <SelectControl loading>Loading...</SelectControl>
</Field>
<Field row label="Date">
  <SelectControl selected>Today</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Selected
Use selected to indicate if the control has a selected value, which toggles visual placeholder styling.As you'll notice here, this doesn't do anything to the content of the control. That's up to you. In a phone row a selected value takes the secondary label color (the primary one in a group with columns), a placeholder the tertiary one.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl selected={false}>Select...</SelectControl>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Fruit">
  <SelectControl selected={false}>Mango</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Start icon
Use StartIcon to display an icon in the control. Sizing, spacing, and coloring are handled automatically. In a phone row the value stands alone at the row's end, so the row's control has no start icon, and this example is desktop only.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Select date...</SelectControl>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <SelectControl>None</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Dropdown icon
Use dropdownIconType to control the presentation of the dropdown indicator. In a phone row the indicator is always the up-down chevrons of an iOS pop-up button, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl selected dropdownIconType="dropdown" StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Select date...</SelectControl>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <SelectControl selected>Today</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Clearable
Pass a callback onClearClick to enable the clearable action.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl selected onClearClick={() => setValue("")} StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>
{value || "Select..."}
</SelectControl>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <SelectControl selected={!!value} onClearClick={() => setValue("")}>
    {value || "None"}
  </SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Loading
During loading, the dropdown icon and clear action are automatically hidden, the control is marked aria-busy, and it ignores pointer and keyboard interaction. Use disabled to add visual disablement.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl selected loading StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Loading...</SelectControl>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Calendar">
  <SelectControl selected loading>Loading...</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Invalid
Use invalid to visually indicate the control is in an invalid state. A row has no frame to color: on Phone, pair invalid with the row's errorMessage.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl invalid selected>Pineapple on pizza</SelectControl>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Topping" errorMessage="Choose another topping.">
  <SelectControl invalid selected>Pineapple</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to both visually and accessibly disable the control.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl disabled selected StartIcon={User}>Reader</SelectControl>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Role">
  <SelectControl disabled selected>Reader</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Block
Create full-width controls with the block prop. In a phone row the value sits at the row's end, so the row's control takes no block, and this example is desktop only.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-[290px] text-center p-2 border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md">
<SelectControl block size="lg" StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Select...</SelectControl>
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Date">
  <SelectControl>None</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Country selector
A plain country selector built with Select. Shows flag icons with country names, no dial codes. Useful for profile forms, shipping addresses, and other country-only fields. The search box appears on its own because the list has more than 15 options; there is no prop for it.
```tsx
const countries = [
{ value: "us", label: "United States" },
{ value: "gb", label: "United Kingdom" },
// ...60 countries
];

const CountryView = ({ value, label }: Option) => (
<span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <img src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${value}.svg`} alt="" width={20} />
  {label}
</span>
);

// Desktop
<Select
value={country}
options={countries}
onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
placeholder="Select country..."
size="lg"
block
searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
TriggerView={CountryView}
OptionView={CountryView}
listMinWidth={300}
/>

// Phone: the country at the row's end; the flags stay in the list.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Country">
  <Select
    value={country}
    options={countries}
    onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
    block={false}
    align="end"
    searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
    OptionView={CountryView}
    listMinWidth={300}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Country code selector
A searchable country selector built with Select. Custom TriggerView and OptionView render flag icons and dial codes. Search matches both country name and dial code.
```tsx
const countries = [
{ value: "us", label: "United States (+1)", dialCode: "+1" },
{ value: "gb", label: "United Kingdom (+44)", dialCode: "+44" },
// ...60 countries
];

const CountryTriggerView = ({ value }) => {
const country = lookup.get(value);
return (
  <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
    <img src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${value}.svg`} alt="" width={20} />
    {country.label} ({country.dialCode})
  </span>
);
};

// Desktop
<Select
value={country}
options={countries}
onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
placeholder="Select country..."
size="lg"
block
searchPredicate={searchPredicate}
TriggerView={CountryTriggerView}
listMinWidth={300}
/>

// Phone: the country and its code at the row's end; the flags stay in the list.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Country">
  <Select
    value={country}
    options={countries}
    onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
    block={false}
    align="end"
    searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
    searchPredicate={searchPredicate}
    OptionView={CountryOptionView}
    listMinWidth={300}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Phone form
Country selector with flag icons and phone input composed into a form. Selecting a country updates the dial code prefix and clears the phone field. Phone numbers are formatted as you type using per-country patterns (e.g. 123 456 7890 for US, 1234 567 890 for UK). Search works by both country name and dial code. Validation runs on submit: the phone field shows an error state with FieldError when the number is too short or too long.
```tsx
import { useState, useCallback, useRef } from 'react';
import { Input } from '@plexui/ui/components/Input';
import { Select, type Option } from '@plexui/ui/components/Select';
import { Button } from '@plexui/ui/components/Button';
import { Field } from '@plexui/ui/components/Field';
import { FieldGroup } from '@plexui/ui/components/FieldGroup';
import { Page } from '@plexui/ui/components/Page';
// BackButton is your app's navigation action.

// Country data: include all 245 countries in production
type Country = { value: string; label: string; dialCode: string; flag: string };

const COUNTRIES: Country[] = [
{ value: 'us', label: 'United States', dialCode: '+1', flag: '🇺🇸' },
{ value: 'gb', label: 'United Kingdom', dialCode: '+44', flag: '🇬🇧' },
{ value: 'de', label: 'Germany', dialCode: '+49', flag: '🇩🇪' },
{ value: 'fr', label: 'France', dialCode: '+33', flag: '🇫🇷' },
{ value: 'es', label: 'Spain', dialCode: '+34', flag: '🇪🇸' },
{ value: 'it', label: 'Italy', dialCode: '+39', flag: '🇮🇹' },
{ value: 'jp', label: 'Japan', dialCode: '+81', flag: '🇯🇵' },
{ value: 'au', label: 'Australia', dialCode: '+61', flag: '🇦🇺' },
{ value: 'br', label: 'Brazil', dialCode: '+55', flag: '🇧🇷' },
{ value: 'in', label: 'India', dialCode: '+91', flag: '🇮🇳' },
// ... full list of 245 countries
];

const COUNTRY_LOOKUP = new Map(COUNTRIES.map((c) => [c.value, c]));
const COUNTRY_OPTIONS = COUNTRIES.map((c) => ({
...c,
label: `${c.label} (${c.dialCode})`,
}));

// Per-country phone number format patterns
const PHONE_FORMATS: Record<string, number[]> = {
us: [3, 3, 4], ca: [3, 3, 4],   // 123 456 7890
gb: [4, 3, 3], de: [3, 4, 4],   // 1234 567 890 | 123 4567 8901
fr: [1, 2, 2, 2, 2],            // 1 23 45 67 89
es: [3, 2, 2, 2],               // 123 45 67 89
it: [3, 3, 4], jp: [2, 4, 4],
au: [3, 3, 3], br: [2, 5, 4],
in: [5, 5],                      // 12345 67890
// ... add more countries as needed
};

function formatPhoneNumber(raw: string, countryCode?: string) {
const digits = raw.replace(/\D/g, '');
if (!digits) return '';
const format = (countryCode && PHONE_FORMATS[countryCode]) || [3, 3, 4];
const groups: string[] = [];
let i = 0;
for (const size of format) {
  if (i >= digits.length) break;
  groups.push(digits.slice(i, i + size));
  i += size;
}
if (i < digits.length) groups.push(digits.slice(i));
return groups.join(' ');
}

// Flag icon: SVG flags from lipis/flag-icons, all 4:3
function FlagIcon({ code, trigger }: { code: string; trigger?: boolean }) {
return (
  <span
    style={{
      display: 'block',
      height: trigger ? 'var(--start-icon-size, 18px)' : 16,
      aspectRatio: '4 / 3',
      borderRadius: 2,
      overflow: 'hidden',
      flexShrink: 0,
    }}
  >
    <img
      src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${code}.svg`}
      alt=""
      loading="lazy"
      style={{
        display: 'block',
        width: '100%',
        height: '100%',
      }}
    />
  </span>
);
}

// Custom trigger and option renderers
const CountryTriggerView = ({ value }: Option) => {
const country = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(value);
if (!country) return null;
return (
  <span style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, height: '100%' }}>
    <FlagIcon code={value} trigger />
    {country.label} ({country.dialCode})
  </span>
);
};

const CountryOptionView = ({ value, label }: Option) => (
<span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <FlagIcon code={value} />
  {label}
</span>
);

// Search matches country name or dial code
const searchPredicate = (option: Option, term: string) => {
const country = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(option.value);
if (!country) return false;
return (
  country.label.toLowerCase().includes(term) ||
  country.dialCode.includes(term)
);
};

function PhoneForm() {
const [country, setCountry] = useState('us');
const [phone, setPhone] = useState('');
const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false);
const phoneRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);

const dialCode = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(country)?.dialCode ?? '+1';
const digits = phone.replace(/\D/g, '');
const isValid = digits.length >= 7 && digits.length <= 15;
const showError = submitted && !isValid;

const handleCountryChange = useCallback((option: Option) => {
  setCountry(option.value);
  setPhone('');
  setSubmitted(false);
  setTimeout(() => phoneRef.current?.focus(), 0);
}, []);

const handlePhoneChange = useCallback(
  (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    setPhone(formatPhoneNumber(e.target.value.replace(/\D/g, ''), country));
    setSubmitted(false);
  },
  [country]
);

return (
  <Page className="h-dvh [--page-content-padding-top:10px] [--page-content-padding-bottom:16px] [--page-footer-gutter:24px] [--page-footer-padding-bottom:max(24px,env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))]">
    <Page.Header style={{ paddingTop: 'env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)' }}><Page.Bar><Page.Leading><BackButton /></Page.Leading><Page.Title>Phone number</Page.Title></Page.Bar></Page.Header>
    <Page.Content>
      <form id="phone-form" onSubmit={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); setSubmitted(true); }} noValidate>
        <FieldGroup title="Phone number" description="Choose your country and enter the number you want to use." columns>
      <Field row label="Country">
        <Select value={country} options={COUNTRY_OPTIONS} onChange={handleCountryChange}
          searchPlaceholder="Search countries..." searchPredicate={searchPredicate}
          OptionView={CountryOptionView} listMinWidth={300} />
      </Field>
      <Field row label="Phone" errorMessage={showError ? 'Phone number is not valid.' : undefined}>
        <Input ref={phoneRef} value={phone} onChange={handlePhoneChange}
          placeholder="Phone number" type="tel" inputMode="tel" autoComplete="tel-national"
          startAdornment={<span className="text-tertiary whitespace-nowrap select-none mr-2">{dialCode}</span>} />
      </Field>
    </FieldGroup>
      </form>
    </Page.Content>
    <Page.Footer><Button color="primary" size="3xl" pill block form="phone-form" type="submit">Continue</Button></Page.Footer>
  </Page>
);
}
```

### Optical alignment
Use opticallyAlign with either "start" or "end" to offset the gutter of the control. In a phone row the row aligns the value with its inset, so opticallyAlign is for desktop, and so is this example.
```tsx
// Desktop
<SelectControl selected variant="ghost" opticallyAlign="start">Ghost control</SelectControl>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Theme">
  <SelectControl selected>System</SelectControl>
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

## Select
Select dropdown with grouped options, per-item descriptions, multiple selection, action items, and column-based layouts.
Import: import { Select } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/select
Props:
  - options (Options<T>) — Array of options or grouped options
  - value (string | string[]) — Selected value (single) or values (multiple)
  - onChange ((option: T) => void | (options: T[]) => void) — Called when selection changes, with the selected option (or options with multiple)
  - multiple (boolean) default: false — Allow multiple selection
  - placeholder (string) default: "Select..." — Trigger placeholder
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Trigger variant
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Trigger size (3xs to 3xl)
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Rounded trigger
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button
  - block (boolean) default: variant !== "ghost" — Full width trigger
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable select. A disabled select is not submitted or validated with its form
  - loading (boolean) default: false — Loading state; shows loadingPlaceholder and keeps the menu closed
  - loadingPlaceholder (string) default: "Loading..." — Trigger text while loading
  - allSelectedLabel (string) default: "All selected" — Text of a multiple trigger when every option is selected
  - name (string) — Name of the hidden form input. With multiple, every selected value is submitted
  - required (boolean) — Required for native form validation
  - id (string) — Id of the hidden form input
  - actions (array) — Actions below options list
  - checkPosition ("start" | "end" | "none") default: "start" — Where the check indicator sits in the list. "none" removes the indicator column for lists that never carry a selection
  - OptionView (React.FC) — Custom option render
  - TriggerView (React.FC) — Custom trigger render: the selected option, or { values, selectedAll } with multiple
  - TriggerStartIcon (ComponentType) — Icon at the start of the trigger
  - trigger (({ open, onToggle }) => ReactNode) — Custom trigger element, wrapped as the popover trigger
  - dropdownIconType ("chevronDown" | "dropdown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Indicator at the end of the trigger
  - side ("top" | "bottom") default: "bottom" — Preferred side of the list
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "end" at the end of a Field row ("start" in a FieldGroup with columns), "center" when block, otherwise "start" — Alignment of the list against the trigger
  - listWidth (number | "auto") default: trigger width (fits the options when not block or at the end of a Field row) — Width of the list in px
  - listMinWidth (number | "auto") default: trigger width — Minimum width of the list in px
  - listMaxWidth (number | "auto") default: "auto" (300 when it fits the options) — Maximum width of the list in px
  - searchPlaceholder (string) — Search input placeholder
  - searchAriaLabel (string) default: "Search options" — Accessible name of the search input, independent of the trigger label
  - searchEmptyMessage (ReactNode) default: "No results found." — Shown when the search matches nothing
  - searchSize (ControlSize) default: "md" — Size of the search input in the menu, such as 2xl for 44px touch targets on phones
  - searchPredicate ((option, term) => boolean) — Filters options while searching
  - aria-label / aria-labelledby (string) — Accessible name of the trigger and the list

### Overview
Pass the selection as value: a string, or an array of strings with multiple. onChange receives the selected option (or options).
```tsx
const [fruit, setFruit] = useState("")

// Desktop
<Select
value={fruit}
options={fruits}
onChange={({ value }) => setFruit(value)}
placeholder="Select a fruit..."
name="fruits"
variant="outline"
size="md"
/>

// Phone: the select is the value of a row.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Fruit">
  <Select
    value={fruit}
    options={fruits}
    onChange={({ value }) => setFruit(value)}
    placeholder="None"
    name="fruits"
    block={false}
    align="end"
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### With descriptions
Options carrying a description field render a secondary line under each label. The title stays semibold in every state (idle, highlighted, selected). The component handles that automatically, no optionClassName needed. Use TriggerStartIcon to reflect the selected option's identity in the trigger. In a phone row the value stands alone at the row's end, so the row has no trigger icon.
```tsx
const RoleOptionDescription = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => (
<div className="font-normal text-secondary text-[0.935em] leading-[1.45]">
  {children}
</div>
);

const roles = [
{
  value: "owner",
  label: "Owner",
  description: (
    <RoleOptionDescription>
      Can modify project information and manage project members
    </RoleOptionDescription>
  ),
},
{
  value: "reader",
  label: "Reader",
  description: (
    <RoleOptionDescription>
      Can make API requests that read or modify data
    </RoleOptionDescription>
  ),
},
];

<Select
value={role}
options={roles}
placeholder="Select role..."
align="start"
listMinWidth={260}
variant="outline"
size="md"
onChange={({ value }) => setRole(value)}
TriggerStartIcon={role === "owner" ? UserLock : User}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Role">
  <Select
    value={role}
    options={roles}
    block={false}
    align="end"
    listMinWidth={260}
    onChange={({ value }) => setRole(value)}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Actions
Custom, arbitrary actions can be displayed below the options list via the actions prop.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Select
value={value}
onChange={handleChange}
options={items}
placeholder="Select..."
align="start"
listMinWidth={240}
actions={[
  { id: "create", label: "Create project", Icon: Plus, onSelect: () => {} },
  { id: "overview", label: "Organization overview", Icon: Workspace, onSelect: () => {} },
]}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Project">
  <Select
    value={value}
    onChange={handleChange}
    options={items}
    placeholder="None"
    block={false}
    align="end"
    listMinWidth={240}
    actions={actions}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Grouped options
