Select supports option groups, similar to the native &lt;optgroup&gt; element. Each group is announced as a group named by its label. All selects are searchable by default, but will only present a searchbox when it makes sense. Currently, this means when there are more than 15 options.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Select
value={value}
options={groupedItems}
onChange={(v) => setValue(v.value)}
variant="outline"
size="lg"
side="bottom"
listMinWidth={300}
searchPlaceholder="Select an option..."
clearable
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Plan">
  <Select
    value={value}
    options={groupedItems}
    onChange={(v) => setValue(v.value)}
    block={false}
    align="end"
    listMinWidth={300}
    searchPlaceholder="Select an option..."
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Multiple selection
Multiple selection is supported through the multiple property. This changes how value, onChange, and TriggerView are typed, accepting and returning arrays of values.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Select
variant="soft"
placeholder="Select fruits..."
options={fruitsOptions}
name="fruits"
multiple
clearable
value={fruits}
onChange={(values) => setFruits(values.map(({ value }) => value))}
TriggerView={MultiFruitTriggerView}
/>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Fruits">
  <Select
    placeholder="None"
    options={fruitsOptions}
    name="fruits"
    multiple
    clearable
    block={false}
    align="end"
    value={fruits}
    onChange={(values) => setFruits(values.map(({ value }) => value))}
    TriggerView={MultiFruitTriggerView}
  />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Column configuration
A column-visibility panel built with Popover and Switch. Toggling a switch moves the column between shown and hidden groups. On a phone the panel is a sheet (Dialog with mobileVariant="sheet") of Field rows with switches, in a fixed order: as in iOS settings, a row stays in place when its switch changes.
```tsx
const allColumns = [
{ id: "name", label: "Name" },
{ id: "email", label: "Email" },
{ id: "role", label: "Role" },
{ id: "status", label: "Status" },
{ id: "created", label: "Created at" },
{ id: "lastLogin", label: "Last login" },
{ id: "avatar", label: "Avatar" },
{ id: "phone", label: "Phone" },
]
const [shown, setShown] = useState(["name", "email", "role", "status"])
const heading = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
const toggle = (id: string) => {
setShown((prev) =>
  prev.includes(id) ? prev.filter((c) => c !== id) : [...prev, id]
)
}
const shownColumns = allColumns.filter((c) => shown.includes(c.id))
const hiddenColumns = allColumns.filter((c) => !shown.includes(c.id))

// Desktop: a popover; a switch moves its column between the shown and hidden lists
<Popover>
<Popover.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline" size="sm">
    <SettingsSlider width={15} height={15} /> Columns
  </Button>
</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content minWidth={240} side="bottom" align="start">
  <div className="py-1.5">
    {shownColumns.map((col) => (
      <div
        key={col.id}
        className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 px-3 py-1.5 cursor-pointer hover:bg-alpha/5"
        onClick={() => toggle(col.id)}
      >
        <span className="text-sm">{col.label}</span>
        <Switch checked aria-label={col.label} />
      </div>
    ))}
    {hiddenColumns.map((col) => (
      <div
        key={col.id}
        className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 px-3 py-1.5 cursor-pointer hover:bg-alpha/5"
        onClick={() => toggle(col.id)}
      >
        <span className="text-sm text-tertiary">{col.label}</span>
        <Switch checked={false} aria-label={col.label} />
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
</Popover.Content>
</Popover>

// Phone: a sheet of switch rows in a fixed order
<Dialog>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline" size="sm">
    <SettingsSlider width={15} height={15} /> Columns
  </Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="sheet" onOpenAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); heading.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }}>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <div ref={heading} tabIndex={-1} className="outline-none"><Dialog.Title>Columns</Dialog.Title></div>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Body>
    <FieldGroup>
      {allColumns.map((col) => (
        <Field row key={col.id} label={col.label}>
          <Switch color="accent" checked={shown.includes(col.id)} onCheckedChange={() => toggle(col.id)} />
        </Field>
      ))}
    </FieldGroup>
  </Dialog.Body>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

## Separator
A thin divider between content, horizontal or vertical, decorative by default or exposed to assistive technology when it marks a real grouping.
Import: import { Separator } from "@plexui/ui/components/Separator"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/separator
Props:
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Direction of the divider
  - decorative (boolean) default: true — When true, the separator is ignored by assistive technologies. Set false when the divider carries semantic grouping (renders role="separator").
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <div>

### Overview
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 16, maxWidth: 384 }}>
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Aisha Cooper</div>
  <div className="text-tertiary">Engineering · Platform team</div>
</div>
<Separator />
<div>Shipped 24 pull requests this week across CI/CD and developer tooling.</div>
</div>
```

### Vertical
Use orientation="vertical" between inline items. Works for meta-strips, breadcrumbs, and dot-less separators.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', height: 20, alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
<div>MIT license</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>12k weekly downloads</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>48 kB bundle</div>
</div>
```

### Menu
Vertical separators between menu items with a short caption underneath each label.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Starter</div>
  <div className="text-tertiary">Free · 1 project</div>
</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Pro</div>
  <div className="text-tertiary">$19/mo · Unlimited</div>
</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Enterprise</div>
  <div className="text-tertiary">Custom · Priority SLA</div>
</div>
</div>
```

### List
Horizontal separators between rows in a definition list.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 8, maxWidth: 384 }}>
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Version</dt><dd>0.9.0</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Published</dt><dd>2 days ago</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Bundle</dt><dd>48 kB</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>License</dt><dd>MIT</dd>
</dl>
</div>
```

## Shimmer Text
Text with a shimmer animation for loading and in-progress states, always on or toggled with a graceful stop.
Import: import { ShimmerText, ShimmerableText } from "@plexui/ui/components/ShimmerText"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/shimmer-text
Props:
  - as ("p" | "span" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" | "div") default: "div" — HTML element to render
  - children (ReactNode) — Text content to shimmer
  - className (string) — Additional CSS classes
  ShimmerableText:
    - as ("p" | "span" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" | "div") default: "div" — HTML element to render
    - shimmer (boolean) default: false — Whether the shimmer animation is active
    - children (ReactNode) — Text content to shimmer
    - className (string) — Additional CSS classes

### Overview
ShimmerText applies a continuous shimmer animation to text content. Useful for loading states, AI-generated content indicators, or visual emphasis.
```tsx
<ShimmerText className="text-lg font-semibold">
Thinking...
</ShimmerText>
```

### Semantic elements
Use the as prop to render as any text element: p, span, h1 to h6, or div.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<ShimmerText as="h2" className="text-2xl font-bold">Heading shimmer</ShimmerText>
<ShimmerText as="p" className="text-base">Paragraph shimmer effect</ShimmerText>
<ShimmerText as="span" className="text-sm text-secondary">Inline shimmer</ShimmerText>
</div>
```

### Controllable shimmer
ShimmerableText allows toggling the shimmer on and off. When shimmer is set to false, the animation finishes its current iteration and then pauses gracefully, with no abrupt cut. Use this variant when text transitions between a loading and idle state.
```tsx
const [shimmer, setShimmer] = useState(true)

<ShimmerableText shimmer={shimmer} className="text-lg font-semibold">
Generating response...
</ShimmerableText>
```

## Sidebar
Composable navigation sidebar for app shells with collapsible sections, search and filter, tree views with hover actions, and a mobile menu
Import: import { SidebarProvider, SidebarLayout, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarInset, SidebarTrigger } from "@plexui/ui/components/Sidebar"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/sidebar
Props:
  - variant ("sidebar" | "docs") default: "sidebar" — Visual variant
  - side ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Which side the sidebar is on
  SidebarProvider:
    - collapsible ("offcanvas" | "icon" | "none") default: "offcanvas" — Collapse behavior: offcanvas (drawer on mobile, full collapse on desktop), icon (icon rail), or none
    - variant ("sidebar" | "app") default: "sidebar" — Look of the whole shell. "app" is the sidebar of a product: 260px, pill rows on a grey ground, a page with no inset, and on a phone a menu under the page
    - defaultOpen (boolean) default: true — Initial open state (uncontrolled)
    - open (boolean) — Controlled open state
    - onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void) — Called when open state changes. Without open the provider keeps its own state and still calls it
    - className (string) — Class of the provider's wrapper
    - style (CSSProperties) — Style of the provider's wrapper, e.g. --sidebar-width
  SidebarGroup:
    - defaultOpen (boolean) default: true — Whether the group is open initially. A closed group hides its SidebarGroupContent
    - open (boolean) — Controlled open state, also exposed as data-state. The group has no toggle of its own: change open from your own control
  SidebarGroupLabel:
    - size ("sm" | "lg") default: "lg" — sm: compact, tertiary. lg: larger, primary, more spacing
    - asChild (boolean) default: false — Render the single child element as the label
  SidebarMenuItem:
    - expanded (boolean) — Marks the item expanded, which turns its SidebarMenuChevron. Pair it with open on its SidebarMenuSub
  SidebarMenuButton:
    - isActive (boolean) default: false — Highlight the current page (aria-current="page")
    - tooltip (string | ReactNode) — Label shown on hover when collapsed (icon mode). Hidden on mobile.
    - asChild (boolean) default: false — Render the single child element (e.g. a router link) as the button. The button attributes go on the child and its content is wrapped like the button's
  SidebarMenuSub:
    - open (boolean) default: true — Whether submenu is expanded. A closed submenu is inert, so its links and buttons leave the tab order and the accessibility tree
    - hasIcons (boolean) default: false — Align child items with parent text that has icons
  SidebarMenuSubButton:
    - isActive (boolean) default: false — Highlight the current page (aria-current="page")
    - indent (0 | 1 | 2 | 3) default: 0 — Nesting level; each level adds 12px of left margin
    - asChild (boolean) default: false — Render the single child element (e.g. a router link) as the button
  SidebarCard:
    - variant ("default" | "elevated") default: "default" — Visual variant
    - dismissible (boolean) default: false — Shows dismiss button
    - onDismiss (() => void) — Callback when dismissed

### App Shell
A multi-section app shell with a workspace selector, expandable parent sections with sub-items, and a footer with a documentation link plus a user menu. Inbox carries a quiet count Badge, as the inbox of a platform does. When collapsed (icon mode), hovering a parent icon opens a Popover flyout listing the section&apos;s items so users keep one-click access without expanding the rail.
```tsx
<ResponsiveSidebarProvider collapsible="icon">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 600 }}>
  <ResponsiveSidebar>
    <SidebarHeader>
      <span>Console</span>
      <SidebarTrigger />
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      {/* Workspace selector */}
      <SidebarMenuItem>
        <Menu>
          <Menu.Trigger>
            <SidebarMenuButton tooltip="Default workspace">
              <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Cube /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
              <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Default</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              <ChevronUpDown className="ml-auto" />
            </SidebarMenuButton>
          </Menu.Trigger>
          <Menu.Content>...</Menu.Content>
        </Menu>
      </SidebarMenuItem>

      {/* Parent section: hover flyout when collapsed */}
      {state === "collapsed" ? (
        <Popover showOnHover>
          <Popover.Trigger>
            <SidebarMenuButton>
              <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><SettingsWrench /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
              <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Build</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              <SidebarMenuChevron />
            </SidebarMenuButton>
          </Popover.Trigger>
          <Popover.Content side="right" minWidth={220}>
            <div>Build / Workbench / Files / Skills / Batches</div>
          </Popover.Content>
        </Popover>
      ) : (
        <SidebarMenuItem expanded={isExpanded}>
          <SidebarMenuButton onClick={toggle}>
            <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><SettingsWrench /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
            <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Build</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
            <SidebarMenuChevron />
          </SidebarMenuButton>
          <SidebarMenuSub open={isExpanded} hasIcons>
            <SidebarMenuSubButton indent={1}>Workbench</SidebarMenuSubButton>
            ...
          </SidebarMenuSub>
        </SidebarMenuItem>
      )}
    </SidebarContent>
    <SidebarFooter>
      <SidebarMenuButton><Book /> Documentation</SidebarMenuButton>
      <Menu>
        <Menu.Trigger>
          <SidebarMenuButton>
            <Avatar name="Alex" />
            <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Alex · Admin</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
          </SidebarMenuButton>
        </Menu.Trigger>
        <Menu.Content>...</Menu.Content>
      </Menu>
    </SidebarFooter>
  </ResponsiveSidebar>
  <SidebarDemoPage title={activePage}>...</SidebarDemoPage>
</SidebarLayout>
</ResponsiveSidebarProvider>
```

### App
The sidebar of a product: 260px, pill rows on a grey ground and a page with no inset. Rows keep their place as it folds, the labels fade, and along the rail the next tooltip opens at once. A Badge in SidebarMenuBadge sits as far from the row's edge as from its top and bottom, and its digits end where plain counts and the chevron end; in the folded rail it becomes a dot of its color above the icon, while plain text such as a count fades. A group lists its items in a Menu beside the icon when folded. The person row in the footer is 40px tall, so the round end of its highlight is concentric with the avatar on the icons' axis. In these examples, the phone toolbar opens the same navigation tree in a full-screen drawer. Set --sidebar-menu-sub-max-height to a group's real height for an even fold.
```tsx
<ResponsiveSidebarProvider collapsible="icon" variant="app">
```

### Collapsible Sections
Build collapsible nested menus with chevron toggles for documentation and API reference sidebars. A parent is a SidebarMenuItem whose SidebarMenuSub holds the next level; expanded on the item turns its SidebarMenuChevron and open on the submenu shows it.
```tsx
const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState<string[]>([]);
const toggle = (id: string) =>
setExpanded((prev) => (prev.includes(id) ? prev.filter((i) => i !== id) : [...prev, id]));

return (
<ResponsiveSidebarProvider collapsible="none">
  <SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
    <ResponsiveSidebar variant="docs">
      <SidebarContent>
        <SidebarGroup>
          <SidebarGroupLabel>API Reference</SidebarGroupLabel>
          <SidebarGroupContent>
            <SidebarMenu>
              <SidebarMenuItem expanded={expanded.includes("responses")}>
                <SidebarMenuSubButton onClick={() => toggle("responses")}>
                  Responses
                  <SidebarMenuChevron />
                </SidebarMenuSubButton>
                <SidebarMenuSub open={expanded.includes("responses")}>
                  <SidebarMenuSubItem>
                    <SidebarMenuSubButton indent={1} isActive>Create</SidebarMenuSubButton>
                  </SidebarMenuSubItem>
                  ...
                </SidebarMenuSub>
              </SidebarMenuItem>
              ...
            </SidebarMenu>
          </SidebarGroupContent>
        </SidebarGroup>
      </SidebarContent>
    </ResponsiveSidebar>
    <SidebarDemoPage title={activePage}>...</SidebarDemoPage>
  </SidebarLayout>
</ResponsiveSidebarProvider>
);
```

### Search and Filter
Combine search and type-based filtering with nested tree navigation. Each item has an icon based on its type. A Menu with checkbox items filters items by type.
```tsx
const subMenuId = useId();

<ResponsiveSidebarProvider collapsible="none">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 650 }}>
  <ResponsiveSidebar>
    <SidebarHeader>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2 w-full">
        <div className="flex-1">
          <SidebarInput
            variant="soft"
            placeholder="Search"
            value={search}
            onChange={(e) => setSearch(e.target.value)}
            onClear={() => setSearch("")}
          />
        </div>
        <Menu>
          <Menu.Trigger>
            <Button variant="soft" color="secondary" uniform aria-label="Filter by type">
              {typeFilters.length > 0 ? <FilterBadge /> : <Filter />}
            </Button>
          </Menu.Trigger>
          <Menu.Content minWidth="auto" align="end">
            {stepFilterOptions.map((option) => (
              <Menu.CheckboxItem
                key={option.value}
                checked={typeFilters.includes(option.value)}
                indicatorPosition="end"
                indicatorVariant="ghost"
                onCheckedChange={(checked) =>
                  setTypeFilters((prev) =>
                    checked ? [...prev, option.value] : prev.filter((v) => v !== option.value),
                  )
                }
                onSelect={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
              >
                {option.label}
              </Menu.CheckboxItem>
            ))}
          </Menu.Content>
        </Menu>
      </div>
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem expanded={expanded}>
              <div className="flex items-center">
                <SidebarMenuButton className="!w-auto min-w-0 flex-1" isActive={activeItem === id} onClick={() => setActiveItem(id)}>
                  <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Desktop /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
                  <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>{label}</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
                </SidebarMenuButton>
                <Button variant="ghost" color="secondary" size="xs" uniform
                  className="!size-[26px] max-md:!size-11 [&_svg]:!size-4"
                  aria-label={(expanded ? "Collapse " : "Expand ") + label}
                  aria-expanded={expanded} aria-controls={subMenuId} onClick={() => setExpanded(!expanded)}>
                  <ChevronDownMd aria-hidden="true" style={{ transform: expanded ? "rotate(0deg)" : "rotate(-90deg)" }} />
                </Button>
              </div>
              <SidebarMenuSub id={subMenuId} open={expanded}>...</SidebarMenuSub>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
            ...
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarGroupContent>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </ResponsiveSidebar>
  <SidebarDemoPage title={activePage}>...</SidebarDemoPage>
</SidebarLayout>
</ResponsiveSidebarProvider>
```

### Tree with Hover Actions
Tree navigation with independent selection, disclosure and action buttons. Tab reaches each control; Enter and Space activate it. Actions appear on hover or keyboard focus on desktop and stay visible on Phone. The controls occupy separate columns, with 44px touch targets on Phone.
```tsx
const treeId = useId();
const subMenuId = treeId + "-" + id;

<SidebarMenuItem expanded={isExpanded}>
<div className="group/row flex items-center">
  <Button variant="ghost" color="secondary" size="xs" uniform
    className="!size-6 max-md:!size-11 [&_svg]:!size-4"
    aria-label={(isExpanded ? "Collapse " : "Expand ") + label}
    aria-expanded={isExpanded} aria-controls={subMenuId}
    onClick={() => toggleExpanded(id)}>
    <ChevronDownMd aria-hidden="true" style={{ transform: isExpanded ? "rotate(0deg)" : "rotate(-90deg)" }} />
  </Button>
  <SidebarMenuButton className="!w-auto min-w-0 flex-1" isActive={activeItem === id} onClick={() => setActiveItem(id)}>
    <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Icon /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
    <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>{label}</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
  </SidebarMenuButton>
  <span className="flex shrink-0 opacity-0 pointer-events-none group-hover/row:opacity-100 group-hover/row:pointer-events-auto group-focus-within/row:opacity-100 group-focus-within/row:pointer-events-auto max-md:opacity-100 max-md:pointer-events-auto">
    <Menu>
      <Menu.Trigger>
        <Button variant="ghost" color="secondary" size="xs" uniform className="!size-6 max-md:!size-11" aria-label={"Add to " + label}>
          <Plus />
        </Button>
      </Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content minWidth="auto" align="end">...</Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </span>
</div>
<SidebarMenuSub id={subMenuId} open={isExpanded} hasIcons>...</SidebarMenuSub>
</SidebarMenuItem>
```

### Mobile Menu
Use Phone preview, then open the menu in the page toolbar. The same navigation tree renders in a desktop rail or a full-screen mobile drawer. Selecting a leaf closes the drawer; expanding a group keeps it open.

## Skeleton
Loading placeholders that match the shape of the content they stand in for, from avatars and text to cards, forms, and tables.
Import: import { Skeleton } from "@plexui/ui/components/Skeleton"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/skeleton
Props:
  - circle (boolean) default: false — Render a circular skeleton
  - className (string) — Set dimensions and custom styling

### Overview
Use a circular skeleton to represent loading avatars, combined with text placeholders.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
<Skeleton circle className="size-12" />
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[200px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Card
Compose multiple skeletons to represent loading cards with images and text content.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 w-[300px] p-4 border border-default rounded-xl">
<Skeleton className="h-[150px] w-full rounded-lg" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-3/4" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
</div>
```

### Text
Multiple text lines with varying widths create natural-looking paragraph placeholders.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-[300px]">
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-4/5" />
</div>
```

### Form
Form skeletons use Plex UI control sizing (32px height for inputs and buttons).
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4 w-[300px]">
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-8 w-full rounded-lg" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-8 w-full rounded-lg" />
</div>
<Skeleton className="h-8 w-[120px] rounded-lg" />
</div>
```

### Table
Table skeletons show header and row structure while data loads.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<div className="flex gap-4 pb-2 border-b border-default">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
</div>
{Array.from({ length: 4 }).map((_, i) => (
  <div key={i} className="flex gap-4 py-2">
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
  </div>
))}
</div>
```

## Slider
Slider for fine-tuning numeric values with single or range thumbs, marks, an editable value input, and vertical orientation.
Import: import { Slider } from "@plexui/ui/components/Slider"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/slider
Props:
  - value (number | number[]) — Required. Current value; array when range is true
  - min (number) — Required. Minimum value
  - max (number) — Required. Maximum value
  - step (number) — Required. Step increment
  - range (boolean) default: false — Enable multi-thumb range mode
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Layout direction of the slider
  - resetValue (number) — Value for reset option (single mode only)
  - resetTooltip (string) default: "Reset to default" — Tooltip and accessible name of the reset button
  - unit (string) — Unit displayed (e.g. ms, px)
  - prefixUnit (string) — Unit displayed before the value (e.g. $)
  - label (ReactNode) — Label (string or JSX). Also names the slider thumbs for assistive technology
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible name when there is no visible label. Range thumbs add Minimum / Maximum (or Value n of m)
  - aria-labelledby (string) — Id of an element that names the slider; takes precedence over label
  - marks (Array<{ value: number, label: string }>) — Marks below track (horizontal only)
  - onChange ((value: number | number[]) => void) — Required. Change handler; receives array when range is true
  - minStepsBetweenThumbs (number) — Minimum steps between thumbs (range mode only)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable slider
  - trackColor (string) — Color of the slider track
  - rangeColor (string) — Color of the filled range
  - className (string) — Applied to the root element
  - onFocus ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the value input or a thumb gains focus
  - onBlur ((event: FocusEvent) => void) — Called when the value input or a thumb loses focus

### Overview
```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Slider } from '@plexui/ui/components/Slider';

export default function SliderExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(1000);
  const [disabled] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Slider
      label="Example field"
      min={0}
      max={2000}
      resetValue={1000}
      step={10}
      unit="ms"
      value={value}
      onChange={setValue}
      disabled={disabled}
    />
  );
}
```

### Adding a tooltip
A tooltip can easily be added to the Slider label by providing JSX instead of a simple string. A tooltip opens on hover, which a phone does not have, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(1000)

return (
<Slider
  label={
    <Tooltip content="More details about this field">
      <Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>Example field</Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>
    </Tooltip>
  }
  min={0}
  max={2000}
  resetValue={1000}
  step={10}
  unit="ms"
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
/>
)
```

### Marks
Slider marks can be easily added by passing an array of values to the marks prop. Responsive behaviors are handled automatically.
```tsx
<Slider
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
label="Passing grade"
min={1}
max={5}
step={1}
marks={[
  { value: 1, label: "1" },
  { value: 2, label: "2" },
  { value: 3, label: "3" },
  { value: 4, label: "4" },
  { value: 5, label: "5" },
]}
trackColor="#61C454"
rangeColor="#EF4146"
/>
```

### Range
Set range to enable a dual-thumb slider for selecting a value range. The value and onChange props accept arrays instead of single numbers.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState([25, 75])
<Slider
range
label="Price range"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
prefixUnit="$"
/>
```

### Multiple thumbs
Pass three or more values to create a multi-thumb slider. Use minStepsBetweenThumbs to enforce minimum spacing between thumbs.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState([10, 40, 70])
<Slider
range
label="Breakpoints"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
minStepsBetweenThumbs={5}
/>
```

### Vertical
Set orientation="vertical" to render a vertical slider. Marks are not supported in vertical orientation.
```tsx
<Slider
label="Volume"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
orientation="vertical"
/>
```

## Sortable
"Reorders a list by dragging: rows of a group, table rows, images, tags and cards. The order changes on the drop."
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/sortable
Props:
  - value (T[]) — The list, in the order of the children
  - onChange ((value: T[]) => void) — Called with the new order after a drop
  - layout ('list' | 'grid') default: list — list for rows one under another, grid for items that stand side by side
  - as (ElementType) default: div — Element to render, such as TableBody for table rows
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Turns dragging off
  - handles (boolean) default: true in a table, otherwise false — Shows the grips of Sortable.Handle. A hidden grip still takes the keyboard, and the item drags from anywhere but a control
  - group (string) — Lists of one group trade items, and a Sortable.Target of that group takes them. Give each list a name
  - name (string) — Names the list in onMove
  - onMove ((move: SortableMove<T>) => void) — An item moved, inside this list or out of it, with { item, from, fromIndex, to, toIndex }. Out of it the app updates both lists: onChange is for a move inside one
  - onHold ((name: string) => void) — A drag rests on a Sortable.Target of the group for half a second
  - children (ReactNode) — The items: one direct child per entry of value, keyed by the entry and not by its index
  - aria-label (string) default: Reorder — Name of the handle for assistive technology

### Rows
Every direct child is an item, in the order of value. A row drags from anywhere but a control, so the switch keeps working. Its grip is hidden and still takes the keyboard: Tab to the row and press the arrow keys. On a touch screen a row lifts after a short hold, and a swipe still scrolls the page. Esc cancels a drag. A wrapper with data-row keeps the lines of the group, and rows that touch hold still: the line alone marks the gap. On a phone the rows sit on the grouped background of an iOS settings screen.
```tsx
const [rows, setRows] = useState(sections);

<FieldGroup title="Home screen">
<Sortable value={rows} onChange={setRows}>
  {rows.map((row) => (
    <div key={row.id} data-row>
      <Sortable.Handle aria-label={`Reorder ${row.label}`} />
      <Field row label={row.label} description={row.description}>
        <Switch defaultChecked />
      </Field>
    </div>
  ))}
</Sortable>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Rows with a handle
A row that is mostly a field needs a grip: handles shows it, and then only the grip drags the row. On a phone with touch.css the grip ends the row, after its value, in the tertiary label color, where iOS puts its reorder control; it stays first in the reading order. A grip drags at once, so on a phone show it while the list is being edited, as iOS shows its reorder controls only in Edit mode.
```tsx
<FieldGroup title="Contact details">
<Sortable value={rows} onChange={setRows} handles>
  {rows.map((row) => (
    <div key={row.id} data-row>
      <Sortable.Handle aria-label={`Reorder ${row.label}`} />
      <Field row label={row.label}>
        <Input variant="ghost" defaultValue={row.value} />
      </Field>
    </div>
  ))}
</Sortable>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Stacked rows
A long value under its label sorts the same way.
```tsx
<FieldGroup title="Questions">
<Sortable value={rows} onChange={setRows}>
  {rows.map((row) => (
    <div key={row.id} data-row>
      <Sortable.Handle aria-label={`Reorder ${row.question}`} />
      <Field row orientation="vertical" label={row.question}>
        <Textarea variant="ghost" rows={1} autoResize defaultValue={row.answer} />
      </Field>
    </div>
  ))}
</Sortable>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Different controls
The kind of control does not matter: each row keeps its state when it moves.
```tsx
<Sortable value={rows} onChange={setRows}>
{rows.map((row) => (
  <div key={row.id} data-row>
    <Sortable.Handle aria-label={`Reorder ${row.label}`} />
    <Field row label={row.label}>{controls[row.id]}</Field>
  </div>
))}
</Sortable>
```

### Table
Pass as={"{TableBody}"} and the rows sort inside the table. Columns keep their width. Grips show here without handles.
```tsx
<Table>
<TableHeader>
  <TableRow>
    <TableHead className="w-10" aria-label="Order" />
    <TableHead>Product</TableHead>
    <TableHead>SKU</TableHead>
    <TableHead>Stock</TableHead>
    <TableHead className="text-end">Price</TableHead>
  </TableRow>
</TableHeader>
<Sortable as={TableBody} value={rows} onChange={setRows}>
  {rows.map((row) => (
    <TableRow key={row.id}>
      <TableCell><Sortable.Handle aria-label={`Reorder ${row.name}`} /></TableCell>
      <TableCell>{row.name}</TableCell>
      <TableCell>{row.sku}</TableCell>
      <TableCell>{row.stock}</TableCell>
      <TableCell className="text-end">{row.price}</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  ))}
</Sortable>
</Table>
```

### Images
layout="grid" for items side by side: the line stands between two items, and the chip shows the picture. With tabIndex an item takes the arrow keys itself.
```tsx
<Sortable value={pictures} onChange={setPictures} layout="grid" className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-3">
{pictures.map((picture) => (
  <div key={picture.id} tabIndex={0} className="aspect-square overflow-hidden rounded-xl">
    <img src={picture.src} alt={picture.alt} className="block size-full object-cover" />
  </div>
))}
</Sortable>
```

### Tags
The grid layout also fits a line that wraps: the end of one line and the start of the next are separate places to land.
```tsx
<Sortable value={tags} onChange={setTags} layout="grid" className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
{tags.map((tag) => (
  <div key={tag} tabIndex={0} className="rounded-full">
    <Badge color="secondary" size="lg" pill>{tag}</Badge>
  </div>
))}
</Sortable>
```

### Cards
Any element can be an item, such as a StatCard.
```tsx
<Sortable value={cards} onChange={setCards} layout="grid" className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-3">
{cards.map((card) => (
  <div key={card.label} tabIndex={0} className="rounded-xl">
    <StatCard label={card.label} value={card.value} />
  </div>
))}
</Sortable>
```

### Between lists
Lists of one group trade items, and an empty list takes a drop. Each list has a name. onMove fires for every move, also inside one list, and the handler updates both lists. Past the end of a list the arrow keys go on to the next one. A data-sortable-static child, such as a head or a message, stays out of the items.
```tsx
const move = ({ item, from, to, toIndex }) =>
setLists((current) => {
  const left = { ...current, [from]: current[from].filter((task) => task !== item) }
  const target = [...left[to]]
  target.splice(toIndex ?? target.length, 0, item)
  return { ...left, [to]: target }
})

{Object.entries(lists).map(([name, tasks]) => (
<Sortable key={name} group="tasks" name={name} value={tasks} onMove={move}>
  {tasks.map((task) => <div key={task}>{task}</div>)}
  {!tasks.length && <p data-sortable-static>Nothing here</p>}
</Sortable>
))}
```

## Stat Card
Stat card for dashboards displaying KPIs with trend deltas, an info tooltip, an icon, a progress bar, and accent border styling.
Import: import { StatCard } from "@plexui/ui/components/StatCard"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/stat-card
Props:
  - label (string) — Required. Label describing the metric
  - value (ReactNode) — Required. The primary metric value
  - description (string) — Subtitle below the value
  - trend ({ value: number; label?: string }) — Trend indicator with percentage
  - invertTrend (boolean) default: false — Invert trend colors (positive = bad)
  - trendPosition ("value" | "header") default: "value" — Where the trend indicator is rendered
  - trendVariant ("text" | "badge") default: "text" — Render trend as text or badge
  - size ("default" | "sm") default: "default" — Card size. Use sm for compact analytics layouts
  - icon (ReactNode) — Icon displayed on the left with a soft background
  - sparkline (ReactNode) — Chart rendered at the bottom
  - progress (number) — Progress bar value (0-100)
  - progressLabel (string) — Label next to progress bar
  - tooltip (string) — Shows an info icon next to the label with tooltip text
  - variant ("default" | "accent") default: "default" — Visual variant
  - accentColor ("primary" | "secondary" | "danger" | "info" | "discovery" | "success" | "caution" | "warning") default: "primary" — Left border color (accent variant)
  - className (string) — Extra classes on the card element

### Overview
Dashboard-ready stat cards with trends, icons, and progress bars. Use the controls below to explore all available props.
```tsx
const [size, setSize] = useState("default")
const [variant, setVariant] = useState("default")
const [trendPosition, setTrendPosition] = useState("value")
const [trendVariant, setTrendVariant] = useState("text")
const [showTrend, setShowTrend] = useState(true)
const [showTooltip, setShowTooltip] = useState(false)
const [invertTrend, setInvertTrend] = useState(false)

<StatCard
label="Total Revenue"
value="$45,231"
size={size}
variant={variant}
trendPosition={trendPosition}
trendVariant={trendVariant}
trend={showTrend ? { value: 12.5, label: "vs last month" } : undefined}
tooltip={showTooltip ? "Sum of all revenue streams" : undefined}
invertTrend={invertTrend}
/>
```

### Sizes
Use size="sm" for compact analytics rows with denser spacing and smaller typography. The small size also pairs well with the tooltip prop for info icons.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
{/* Default size */}
<div className="grid w-full min-w-0 grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
  <StatCard label="Total Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
  <StatCard label="Active Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
  <StatCard label="Conversion Rate" value="3.24%" trend={{ value: -1.8 }} />
</div>
{/* Small size */}
<div className="grid w-full min-w-0 grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-3">
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Total Inquiries" value="3,544" trend={{ value: -2.6 }} tooltip="Total inquiries in period" />
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Completion Rate" value="89.2%" trend={{ value: 0.5 }} tooltip="Average across templates" />
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Approval Rate" value="84.6%" trend={{ value: 1.8 }} tooltip="Average across templates" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Trend position
Control where the trend appears: next to the value (default) or right-aligned in the header row.
```tsx
<div className="grid w-full min-w-0 grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-4" style={{ maxWidth: 480 }}>
<StatCard label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} trendPosition="value" />
<StatCard label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} trendPosition="header" />
</div>
```

### Trend variant
Display the trend as plain text or wrapped in a badge.
```tsx
<div className="grid w-full min-w-0 grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-4" style={{ maxWidth: 480 }}>
<StatCard label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} trendVariant="text" />
<StatCard label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} trendVariant="badge" />
</div>
```

### Info tooltip
Pass a tooltip string to render an info icon next to the label with a tooltip on hover.
```tsx
<StatCard label="Avg Completion Rate" value="89.2%" trend={{ value: 0.5 }} tooltip="Percentage of inquiries reaching final state" />
```

### With icon
Pass an icon to display it on the left side with a soft background. The layout automatically switches to a horizontal icon + content arrangement. Works with both default and sm sizes.
```tsx
import { DollarCircle, Users, ShoppingBag } from "@plexui/ui/components/Icon"

{/* Default size */}
<div className="grid w-full min-w-0 grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<StatCard icon={<DollarCircle />} label="Total Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
<StatCard icon={<Users />} label="Active Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
</div>

{/* Small size */}
<div className="grid w-full min-w-0 grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-3">
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<DollarCircle />} label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<Users />} label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<ShoppingBag />} label="Orders" value="1,234" trend={{ value: -3.1 }} />
</div>
```

### With progress
Progress bars show a visual representation of completion or usage percentage.
```tsx
<StatCard label="Storage Used" value="7.2 GB" progress={72} progressLabel="72%" description="of 10 GB" />
```

### Accent border
The accent variant adds a colored left border. Choose from eight semantic colors.
```tsx
const [accentColor, setAccentColor] = useState("primary")

<StatCard
label="Total Revenue"
value="$45,231"
variant="accent"
accentColor={accentColor}
trend={{ value: 12.5, label: "vs last month" }}
/>
```

### Inverted trend
Use invertTrend for metrics where positive values are bad (e.g., error rate, response time). Toggle the switch to see the color flip.
```tsx
const [invertTrend, setInvertTrend] = useState(true)

<StatCard
label="Avg Response Time"
value="234ms"
trend={{ value: 15.3, label: "vs last hour" }}
invertTrend={invertTrend}
/>
```

## Stepper
Two segments that decrease and increase a number in steps, within a range or wrapping around, as the iOS 26 stepper does.
Import: import { Stepper } from "@plexui/ui/components/Stepper"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/stepper
Props:
  - value (number) — Controlled value
  - defaultValue (number) default: min — Initial value (uncontrolled)
  - onChange ((value: number) => void) — Called with the next value after a step
  - min (number) default: 0 — Lowest value
  - max (number) default: 100 — Highest value
  - step (number) default: 1 — Amount each step adds or removes
  - wrap (boolean) default: false — A step past max continues from min, and one below min from max
  - autoRepeat (boolean) default: true — Holding a segment keeps stepping: after 400ms, every 100ms
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent interaction and focus
  - pill (boolean) default: true — Fully rounded ends
  - decrementLabel (string) default: "Decrease" — Accessible name of the minus segment
  - incrementLabel (string) default: "Increase" — Accessible name of the plus segment
  - name (string) — Submits the value with the owning form through a hidden input
  - aria-label (string) — Name of the value, when no visible label names it
  - aria-labelledby (string) — The id of the visible label of the value
  - aria-describedby (string) — The id of an element that describes the stepper
  - id (string) — The id of the stepper
  - onFocus (FocusEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>) — Called when the stepper gains focus
  - onBlur (FocusEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>) — Called when the stepper loses focus
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the stepper

### Overview
Name the stepper with aria-labelledby, the visible label of its value. A segment at the end of the range turns tertiary and stops stepping. Holding a segment keeps stepping, as a native stepper does.
```tsx
const label = useId()
const [guests, setGuests] = useState(2)

<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
<span id={label}>Guests</span>
<span className="min-w-5 text-end font-medium tabular-nums" aria-hidden="true">{guests}</span>
<Stepper aria-labelledby={label} value={guests} onChange={setGuests} min={1} max={8} />
</div>
```

### In rows
In a Field row the label names the stepper. Put the value in the label, such as 3 copies. On a phone the rows sit on the grouped background of an iOS settings screen.
```tsx
const [copies, setCopies] = useState(1)
const [nights, setNights] = useState(3)

<FieldGroup footer="Up to 20 copies and 14 nights.">
<Field row label={copies === 1 ? '1 copy' : `${copies} copies`}>
  <Stepper value={copies} onChange={setCopies} min={1} max={20} />
</Field>
<Field row label={nights === 1 ? '1 night' : `${nights} nights`}>
  <Stepper value={nights} onChange={setNights} min={1} max={14} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Range, step and wrap
Decimal steps add without rounding drift. With wrap a step past max continues from min, so the hour goes from 23 to 0, and neither segment stops.
```tsx
<Stepper aria-labelledby={opacityLabel} value={opacity} onChange={setOpacity} min={0} max={1} step={0.1} />
<Stepper aria-labelledby={hourLabel} value={hour} onChange={setHour} min={0} max={23} wrap />
```

### States
At the lowest value the minus segment is tertiary. A disabled stepper takes no focus. On a desktop set pill to false for square ends, as other controls in a dense layout have; on a phone the stepper stays the capsule of iOS.
```tsx
<Stepper aria-label="At the lowest value" defaultValue={0} />
<Stepper aria-label="Disabled" defaultValue={3} disabled />
<Stepper aria-label="Square ends" defaultValue={3} pill={false} />
```

## Swipe Actions
"Actions behind a row of a list, as the swipe actions of an iOS list: a swipe across the row reveals them, a full swipe runs the first one, and each is a button for the keys."
Import: import { SwipeActions } from "@plexui/ui/components/SwipeActions"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/swipe-actions
Props:
  - leading (SwipeAction[]) default: [] — Actions revealed by a swipe toward the trailing edge, the first one at the leading edge
  - trailing (SwipeAction[]) default: [] — Actions revealed by a swipe toward the leading edge, the first one at the trailing edge
  - labelPlacement ("hidden" | "inside" | "below") default: "hidden" — Where the actions show their labels: symbols only, inside the capsule, or below it (for rows of 68px and taller)
  - fullSwipe (boolean) default: true — A swipe past the middle between the open actions and the far edge runs the first action of that side
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the row
  - children (ReactNode) — The content of the row
  SwipeAction:
    - id (string) — Unique ID of the action within its side
    - label (string) — Name of the action: shown inside or below the capsule (and on an action without an icon), and its accessible name always
    - Icon (ComponentType<SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>>) — Icon of the action
    - color ("primary" | "secondary" | "danger" | "success" | "info" | "discovery" | "caution" | "warning") default: "secondary" — Solid color of the action
    - onSelect (() => void) — Called when the action is pressed, or by a full swipe when it is the first action of its side

### Overview
Wrap the content of a row of a FieldGroup: the swipe row is the data-row of the group, so its separators and corners follow the card. The actions are solid capsules behind the content, 10px apart and 16px from the edge, as in the iOS 27 kit; the first action of a side stands at its edge. Swiped aside, the content becomes a capsule of the row&apos;s color on the background of the list. A swipe past half of the actions opens them, a press on an action runs it and closes the row, and a press on the content or anywhere outside closes it too; one row is open at a time. A swipe past the middle between the open actions and the far edge stretches the first action across the row, and letting go runs it.
```tsx
<FieldGroup>
{lists.map((name) => (
  <SwipeActions
    key={name}
    leading={[{ id: "pin", label: "Pin", Icon: Pin, color: "warning", onSelect: () => pin(name) }]}
    trailing={[
      { id: "delete", label: "Delete", Icon: RemoveTrash, color: "danger", onSelect: () => remove(name) },
      { id: "archive", label: "Archive", Icon: Archive, color: "info", onSelect: () => archive(name) },
    ]}
  >
    <div className="row">{name}</div>
  </SwipeActions>
))}
</FieldGroup>
```

### Labels inside
With labelPlacement=&quot;inside&quot; each capsule holds a smaller symbol and its label, as the kit&apos;s Symbol and Label row. An action without an icon always shows its label inside.
```tsx
<SwipeActions
labelPlacement="inside"
leading={[{ id: "pin", label: "Pin", Icon: Pin, color: "warning", onSelect: () => pin(name) }]}
trailing={[
  { id: "delete", label: "Delete", Icon: RemoveTrash, color: "danger", onSelect: () => remove(name) },
  { id: "archive", label: "Archive", Icon: Archive, color: "info", onSelect: () => archive(name) },
]}
>
<div className="row">{name}</div>
</SwipeActions>
```

### Labels below
With labelPlacement=&quot;below&quot; a lower capsule stands over its label, as the kit&apos;s Symbol and Label Tall row. It takes a row of 68px or taller, such as a row of two lines.
```tsx
<SwipeActions
labelPlacement="below"
leading={[{ id: "flag", label: "Flag", Icon: Flag, color: "warning", onSelect: () => flag(message) }]}
trailing={[
  { id: "delete", label: "Delete", Icon: RemoveTrash, color: "danger", onSelect: () => remove(message) },
  { id: "archive", label: "Archive", Icon: Archive, color: "info", onSelect: () => archive(message) },
]}
>
<div className="row">
  <div>{message.from}</div>
  <div>{message.subject}</div>
</div>
</SwipeActions>
```

## Switch
Toggle switch for turning settings on or off, with an optional label, a supporting description linked for screen readers, and a configurable label position.
Import: import { Switch } from "@plexui/ui/components/Switch"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/switch
Props:
  - checked (boolean) — Controlled state
  - defaultChecked (boolean) — Initial state (uncontrolled)
  - onCheckedChange ((next: boolean) => void) — Called when toggled
  - label (ReactNode) — Accessible label rendered next to the switch
  - description (ReactNode) — Secondary text below the label, linked via aria-describedby
  - labelPosition ("start" | "end") default: "end" — Label on left (start) or right (end)
  - color ("primary" | "accent") default: "primary" — Checked track color. Accent reads --switch-accent-color, with platform green as its fallback. Disabled checked controls retain a muted accent.
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent interaction
  - required (boolean) — Required for form submission
  - name (string) — Form field name
  - value (string) default: "on" — Value when submitted
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to wrapper node
  - id (string) — The id of the switch element (generated when omitted)
  - onFocus (FocusEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>) — Called when the switch gains focus
  - onBlur (FocusEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>) — Called when the switch loses focus

### Overview
Compare off and on across enabled and disabled states. Enabled controls are interactive. Choose accent for the configured application accent (platform green by default), or primary for the default Switch style. Disabled on retains a muted accent; disabled off uses the neutral track.
```tsx
// Desktop: four states, shown together.
<Switch color="accent" aria-label="Enabled, initially off" />
<Switch color="accent" defaultChecked aria-label="Enabled, initially on" />
<Switch color="accent" disabled aria-label="Disabled, off" />
<Switch color="accent" disabled defaultChecked aria-label="Disabled, on" />

// Phone: keep each switch inside a labelled row.
{[false, true].map((disabled) => (
<FieldGroup key={String(disabled)} title={disabled ? "Disabled" : "Enabled"}>
  <Field row label="Initially off"><Switch color="accent" disabled={disabled} /></Field>
  <Field row label="Initially on"><Switch color="accent" disabled={disabled} defaultChecked /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
))}
```

### Label and description
Click either the label or the control. Descriptions are linked with aria-describedby. Desktop supports both label positions; Phone keeps the label on the left. Use defaultChecked for an initial value and name for form submission.
```tsx
// Desktop
<Switch color="accent" label="Notifications" labelPosition="start" name="notifications" defaultChecked />
<Switch color="accent" label="Weekly summary" description="Sent on Mondays." labelPosition="start" name="summary" />

// Phone: Field associates the external label and description with the switch.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Notifications"><Switch color="accent" name="notifications" defaultChecked /></Field>
<Field row label="Weekly summary" description="Sent on Mondays."><Switch color="accent" name="summary" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Controlled state
Change checked above or toggle the setting. Both update the same state. Use this pattern when your application owns the value.
```tsx
const [checked, setChecked] = useState(false)

// Desktop
<Switch color="accent" label="Airplane mode" checked={checked} onCheckedChange={setChecked} />

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Airplane mode"><Switch color="accent" checked={checked} onCheckedChange={setChecked} /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Grouped settings
Group related settings with FieldGroup. Use a row description to explain a locked setting and a footer for help that applies to the group. Phone shows the same groups in a full Page with navigation.
```tsx
// Place these groups inside Page.Content on Phone.
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
<FieldGroup title="Notifications">
  <Field row label="Push notifications"><Switch color="accent" defaultChecked /></Field>
  <Field row label="Product updates" description="A few emails a month."><Switch color="accent" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
<FieldGroup title="Privacy" footer="You can change your data sharing preference at any time.">
  <Field row label="Share usage data"><Switch color="accent" /></Field>
  <Field row label="Security alerts" description="Required for your account."><Switch color="accent" defaultChecked disabled /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
</div>
```

## Tab Bar
"The tab bar of a phone screen: two to five sections at the bottom in a floating glass capsule, an optional search or prominent tab, minimizing while the content scrolls. Desktop layouts navigate with a Sidebar or Tabs, so a tab bar never renders from 768px up."
Import: import { TabBar } from "@plexui/ui/components/TabBar"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/tab-bar
Props:
  - value (string) — Controlled value of the selected tab
  - defaultValue (string) — Selected tab (uncontrolled)
  - onValueChange ((value: string) => void) — Called with the value of the tab a person selects
  - search ({ value: string; label?: string }) — A search tab in a glass circle of its own at the trailing end; label defaults to Search
  - prominent ({ value: string; label: string; icon: ReactNode }) — A prominent tab in a glass circle of its own at the trailing end, in place of the search circle; search then joins the capsule
  - minimizeBehavior ("never" | "onScrollDown") default: "never" — Minimize to the selected tab while the Page content scrolls down
  - minimized (boolean) — Controlled minimized state
  - defaultMinimized (boolean) default: false — Minimized state (uncontrolled)
  - onMinimizedChange ((minimized: boolean) => void) — Called when the bar minimizes or expands
  - background ("soft" | "hard" | "glass" | "solid") default: "soft" — How the bar meets the content scrolled under it, see Background
  - aria-label (string) default: "Tabs" — Name of the navigation
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the bar
  TabBar.Item:
    - value (string) — Value of the tab
    - label (string) — Label under the symbol and the name of the tab
    - icon (ReactNode) — The symbol, a PlexUI icon
    - href (string) — Makes the tab a link
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — The tab cannot be selected
    - onClick ((event: MouseEvent) => void) — Called when the tab is pressed, before it is selected
    - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the tab

### Overview
Put the bar last in a Page: it reserves its height there. Up to three tabs sit in the middle, 94px apart; four and five share the width. The selected tab sits on a pill in the primary text, the others in a lighter gray, as Sidebar items are.
```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState('home')

<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Title>Home</Toolbar.Title>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
<TabBar value={tab} onValueChange={setTab}>
  <TabBar.Item value="home" label="Home" icon={<Home />} />
  <TabBar.Item value="calendar" label="Calendar" icon={<Calendar />} />
  <TabBar.Item value="photos" label="Photos" icon={<Images />} />
  <TabBar.Item value="settings" label="Settings" icon={<SettingsCog />} />
</TabBar>
</Page>
```

### Search tab
With search the search tab takes a glass circle of its own at the trailing end, as the iOS 26 search tab does. The capsule of the other tabs keeps to the leading end at their width, as in the kit and in Photos: with two tabs it ends well before the circle, with three it reaches 8px from it. It is a tab like the others: show the search screen when its value is selected.
```tsx
<TabBar value={tab} onValueChange={setTab} search={{ value: 'search' }}>
<TabBar.Item value="home" label="Home" icon={<Home />} />
<TabBar.Item value="calendar" label="Calendar" icon={<Calendar />} />
<TabBar.Item value="photos" label="Photos" icon={<Images />} />
</TabBar>
```

### Prominent tab
With prominent one destination leaves the capsule for a glass circle of its own at the trailing end, as the prominent tab of iOS 27 and its kit: one key destination, such as a cart or a library. It is still a tab, not an action: it shows a screen of its own when selected. A bar has one such circle, so prominent takes the place of the search circle; with both, search becomes the last tab of the capsule. The circle shows the symbol only, and label names the tab.
```tsx
<TabBar
value={tab}
onValueChange={setTab}
prominent={{ value: 'bag', label: 'Bag', icon: <ShoppingBag /> }}
>
<TabBar.Item value="home" label="Home" icon={<Home />} />
<TabBar.Item value="calendar" label="Calendar" icon={<Calendar />} />
<TabBar.Item value="photos" label="Photos" icon={<Images />} />
</TabBar>
```

### Minimize on scroll
With minimizeBehavior="onScrollDown" the bar shrinks to the selected tab while the content scrolls down and comes back when it scrolls up, as in iOS 26. Minimized, the circles keep 28px from the sides and at least 28px from the bottom, as in the iOS 27 kit. Tap the minimized tab to bring the others back.
```tsx
<TabBar value={tab} onValueChange={setTab} search={{ value: 'search' }} minimizeBehavior="onScrollDown">
...
</TabBar>
```

### Background
background sets how the bar meets the content scrolled under it, as a Toolbar does: soft (the default) leaves the content clear under and around the capsule, as native iOS 26 does, glass is a translucent, blurred band with a hairline, hard is an opaque band with a line on top, and solid an opaque band with no line. Glass and hard show themselves while the content continues under the bar.
```tsx
<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar background="hard">...</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
<TabBar value={tab} onValueChange={setTab} background="hard">
  ...
</TabBar>
</Page>
```

## Table
Styled table primitives for structured data, with header, body, footer, row, cell and caption parts on native table elements.
Import: import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell } from "@plexui/ui/components/Table"
Import: import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/table
  Table Primitives:
    - Table (table) — Root table container with horizontal scroll wrapper
    - TableHeader (thead) — Table header group
    - TableBody (tbody) — Table body group
    - TableFooter (tfoot) — Table footer group
    - TableRow (tr) — Table row
    - TableHead (th) — Table header cell
    - TableCell (td) — Table data cell
    - TableCaption (caption) — Table caption
  DataTable:
    - columns (ColumnDef<TData>[]) — Column definitions following TanStack Table v8 API (required)
    - data (TData[]) — Data array to display (required)
    - variant ("default" | "bordered") default: "default" — Visual variant: bordered adds a rounded border and tinted header
    - pageSize (number) default: 10 — Rows per page. Set 0 or Infinity to disable pagination. The rows-per-page select offers 10, 20, 50, 100 and this size
    - initialSorting (SortingState) — Initial column sorting state
    - globalFilter (string) — Controlled search/filter string
    - onGlobalFilterChange ((value: string) => void) — Callback when filter changes
    - onRowClick ((row: TData) => void) — Click handler for rows. Makes rows interactive: they take Tab and call it on Enter or Space
    - columnVisibility (VisibilityState) — Controlled column visibility state
    - onColumnVisibilityChange ((visibility: VisibilityState) => void) — Callback when visibility changes
    - enableRowSelection (boolean) default: false — Adds a first column (id select) with a checkbox per row and a header checkbox that selects every row on all pages, mixed when some are selected. A click on a checkbox is not a row click
    - rowSelection (RowSelectionState) — Controlled row selection state
    - onRowSelectionChange ((selection: RowSelectionState) => void) — Callback when selection changes
    - getRowId ((row: TData) => string) — Custom row ID accessor; selection keys use it
    - emptyMessage (ReactNode) default: "No results." — Shown when no rows
    - showPagination (boolean) default: true — Whether to show pagination controls. They hide on their own when every row fits on one page
    - className (string) — Class applied to outermost wrapper
  DataTableColumnHeader:
    - column (Column<TData, TValue>) — TanStack Table column object (required)
    - title (string) — Display text for the header (required)
    - className (string) — Class applied to the header button (or text when the column cannot sort)
  Column helpers:
    - idCell(accessor) (CellComponent) — Monospace ID with copy-on-click tooltip
    - dateTimeCell(accessor, options?) (CellComponent) — Formatted datetime with Intl.DateTimeFormat
    - statusCell(accessor, colorMap?) (CellComponent) — Badge cell with automatic status-to-color mapping
    - tooltipHeader(label, description) (HeaderComponent) — Header with dashed underline and info tooltip

### Overview
A complete table with header, body, footer, and caption showing invoice data.
```tsx
const invoices = [
{ invoice: "INV001", status: "Paid", method: "Credit Card", amount: "$250.00" },
{ invoice: "INV002", status: "Pending", method: "PayPal", amount: "$150.00" },
{ invoice: "INV003", status: "Unpaid", method: "Bank Transfer", amount: "$350.00" },
{ invoice: "INV004", status: "Paid", method: "Credit Card", amount: "$450.00" },
{ invoice: "INV005", status: "Paid", method: "PayPal", amount: "$550.00" },
]

return (
<Table>
  <TableCaption>A list of your recent invoices.</TableCaption>
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Invoice</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Status</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Method</TableHead>
      <TableHead className="text-right">Amount</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    {invoices.map((invoice) => (
      <TableRow key={invoice.invoice}>
        <TableCell className="font-medium">{invoice.invoice}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{invoice.status}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{invoice.method}</TableCell>
        <TableCell className="text-right">{invoice.amount}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    ))}
  </TableBody>
  <TableFooter>
    <TableRow>
      <TableCell colSpan={3}>Total</TableCell>
      <TableCell className="text-right">$1,750.00</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableFooter>
</Table>
)
```
