```tsx
    <TableHead className="text-right">Price</TableHead>
    <TableHead className="text-right">Total</TableHead>
  </TableRow>
</TableHeader>
<TableBody>
  <TableRow>
    <TableCell className="font-medium">Pro Plan</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">3</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$29.00</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$87.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
  <TableRow>
    <TableCell className="font-medium">Storage Add-on</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">1</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$9.00</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$9.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
</TableBody>
<TableFooter>
  <TableRow>
    <TableCell colSpan={3}>Subtotal</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right font-semibold">$96.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
</TableFooter>
</Table>
```

### Minimal
A simple table without caption or footer, showing a list of people.
```tsx
const people = [
{ name: "Lindsay Walton", title: "Front-end Developer", email: "lindsay@example.com" },
{ name: "Courtney Henry", title: "Designer", email: "courtney@example.com" },
{ name: "Tom Cook", title: "Director of Product", email: "tom@example.com" },
]

return (
<Table>
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Name</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Title</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Email</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    {people.map((person) => (
      <TableRow key={person.email}>
        <TableCell className="font-medium">{person.name}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{person.title}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{person.email}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    ))}
  </TableBody>
</Table>
)
```

### Variant
Use variant="bordered" for a card-like table with a rounded border and tinted header background. Toggle empty to supply no rows without resetting sorting or changing columns. emptyMessage selects the default message, custom text, or rich content. Filtering and its no-results state are shown separately.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, statusCell, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
{ accessorKey: "department", header: "Department" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
]

const previewUsers = users.slice(0, 6)
const emptyUsers: User[] = []
const emptyMessages = {
default: undefined,
text: "No users found.",
rich: <strong>No users found.</strong>,
}

export function UsersTable() {
const [empty, setEmpty] = useState(false)
const [emptyMessage, setEmptyMessage] = useState<keyof typeof emptyMessages>("text")

return <DataTable columns={columns} data={empty ? emptyUsers : previewUsers}
  variant="bordered" pageSize={Infinity} emptyMessage={emptyMessages[emptyMessage]} />
}
```

### Sorting
Click column headers to toggle sort direction. Columns use DataTableColumnHeader for sort controls.
```tsx
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{
  accessorKey: "role",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Role" />,
},
{
  accessorKey: "status",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Status" />,
},
]

export function UsersTable() {
return (
  <DataTable
    columns={columns}
    data={users}
    pageSize={5}
    initialSorting={[{ id: "name", desc: false }]}
  />
)
}
```

### Pagination
Automatic pagination with rows-per-page selector and navigation controls. Set pageSize to control the initial page size; the select offers 10, 20, 50 and 100 plus that size. The controls hide when every row fits on one page.
```tsx
import { DataTable, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{ accessorKey: "id", header: "ID" },
{ accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
{ accessorKey: "department", header: "Department" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
]

export function UsersTable() {
return <DataTable columns={columns} data={users} pageSize={5} />
}
```

### Row click
Pass onRowClick to make rows clickable. Clickable rows also take Tab and call it on Enter or Space.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "email", header: "Email" },
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
]

export function UsersTable() {
const [selectedUser, setSelectedUser] = useState<User | null>(null)

return (
  <>
    <DataTable columns={columns} data={users.slice(0, 8)} pageSize={4} onRowClick={setSelectedUser} />
    <p className="mt-3 text-sm text-secondary">
      {selectedUser
        ? "Clicked: " + selectedUser.name + " (" + selectedUser.id + ") - " + selectedUser.department
        : "Click a row to see selected user details."}
    </p>
  </>
)
}
```

### Row selection
Set enableRowSelection to add a first column of checkboxes. The header checkbox selects every row on all pages and shows a mixed state when only some are selected. Bind rowSelection and onRowSelectionChange to read the selection; getRowId keys it by your own ids.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import {
DataTable,
DataTableColumnHeader,
statusCell,
type ColumnDef,
type RowSelectionState,
} from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
]

export function UsersTable() {
const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({})

return (
  <>
    <DataTable
      columns={columns}
      data={users}
      pageSize={5}
      enableRowSelection
      rowSelection={rowSelection}
      onRowSelectionChange={setRowSelection}
      getRowId={(user) => user.id}
    />
    <p className="mt-3 text-sm text-secondary">
      {Object.keys(rowSelection).length} of {users.length} rows selected
    </p>
  </>
)
}
```

### Cell variants
Column helpers render common cells: idCell (monospace ID with copy-on-click), statusCell (status badge), dateTimeCell (formatted date) and tooltipHeader (header with an info tooltip). Other formats, like the salary below, are plain cell renderers; meta.align aligns a column.
```tsx
import { DataTable, dateTimeCell, idCell, statusCell, tooltipHeader, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0 })

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{ accessorKey: "id", header: "ID", cell: idCell<User>((row) => row.id) },
{ accessorKey: "name", header: "Name", cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span> },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
{ accessorKey: "joined", header: "Joined", cell: dateTimeCell<User>((row) => row.joined) },
{
  accessorKey: "salary",
  header: tooltipHeader("Salary", "Annual base salary in USD."),
  meta: { align: "right" },
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{money.format(row.original.salary)}</span>,
},
]

export function UsersTable() {
return <DataTable columns={columns} data={users} pageSize={6} />
}
```

### Filtering
Control search with globalFilter and onGlobalFilterChange. The filter searches across all columns.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Input } from "@plexui/ui/components/Input"
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, statusCell, type ColumnDef } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
{ accessorKey: "department", header: "Department" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
]

export function UsersTable() {
const [globalFilter, setGlobalFilter] = useState("")

return (
  <>
    <Input
      value={globalFilter}
      onChange={(event) => setGlobalFilter(event.target.value)}
      placeholder="Search name, role, department..."
    />
    <DataTable
      columns={columns}
      data={users}
      globalFilter={globalFilter}
      onGlobalFilterChange={setGlobalFilter}
      pageSize={5}
    />
  </>
)
}
```

### Column visibility
Toggle column visibility with the columnVisibility and onColumnVisibilityChange props.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader, statusCell, type ColumnDef, type VisibilityState } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
import { users, type User } from "./data"

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0 })

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
{
  accessorKey: "name",
  header: ({ column }) => <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="Name" />,
  cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium">{row.original.name}</span>,
},
{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role" },
{ accessorKey: "department", header: "Department" },
{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: statusCell<User>((row) => row.status) },
{
  accessorKey: "salary",
  header: "Salary",
  meta: { align: "right" },
  cell: ({ row }) => <span>{money.format(row.original.salary)}</span>,
},
]

export function UsersTable() {
const [columnVisibility, setColumnVisibility] = useState<VisibilityState>({
  role: true,
  department: true,
  status: true,
  salary: true,
})

return (
  <DataTable
    columns={columns}
    data={users}
    pageSize={5}
    columnVisibility={columnVisibility}
    onColumnVisibilityChange={setColumnVisibility}
  />
)
}
```

## Tabs
Switch between grouped views with segmented or underline tabs, icon-only triggers, and badge counts on each tab.
Import: import { Tabs } from "@plexui/ui/components/Tabs"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/tabs
Props:
  - value (string) — Selected tab value (controlled, required)
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called when selection changes
  - onClick (() => void) — Called on any click in the group, even when the selection does not change
  - variant ("segmented" | "underline") default: "segmented" — Visual style: segmented (background highlight) or underline (line indicator)
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Layout direction of the tab group
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Control height (3xs through 3xl)
  - gutterSize ("2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Horizontal padding of tabs
  - pill (boolean) default: true — Fully rounded control (segmented variant only)
  - flush (boolean) default: false — Text-width indicator, no border, gap spacing (underline variant only)
  - block (boolean) default: false — Full-width control with equal-width tabs
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable all tabs
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible name (required)
  - overflow ("scroll" | "menu") default: "scroll" — Tabs that do not fit: scroll sideways, or move into a menu at the end (horizontal, not block)
  - overflowLabel (string) default: "More" — Text of the menu button with overflow="menu"
  - className (string) — Extra classes on the group element
  - children (ReactNode) — Tabs.Tab children
  Tabs.Tab:
    - value (string) — Tab value (required)
    - disabled (boolean) — Disable this tab
    - icon (ReactNode) — Icon element (sized automatically)
    - badge (ReactNode | { content: ReactNode; color?: "secondary" | "success" | "danger" | "warning" | "info" | "discovery" | "caution"; variant?: "soft" | "solid"; pill?: boolean; loading?: boolean }) — Badge content (for example a count) or a badge config
    - aria-label (string) — Accessible name (required for icon-only tabs)
    - children (ReactNode) — Tab label

### Overview
Tabs provides two visual variants: segmented (default) with a sliding background highlight, and underline with an animated line indicator. Both support horizontal and vertical orientations. disabled affects the whole group, which on a phone shows at half opacity when horizontal, as a disabled iOS segmented control does; reportsDisabled disables only Reports. Arrow-key navigation skips disabled tabs without resetting the selected value. On a phone horizontal tabs of either variant are the iOS segmented control on glass, as toolbar buttons are: segments of one width in a 44px capsule, the selection a darker pill inside it with the primary label and the other labels secondary, filling the row of a phone screen; vertical tabs are an inset grouped list. So the phone view has no variant, flush, block, size and pill controls.
```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState("overview")
const [disabled, setDisabled] = useState(false)
const [reportsDisabled, setReportsDisabled] = useState(false)

return (
<Tabs value={tab} onChange={setTab} disabled={disabled} aria-label="Demo tabs">
  <Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="reports" disabled={reportsDisabled}>Reports</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
)
```

### Segmented with icons
Icons work with the segmented variant. Use the icon prop on individual tabs. Icons are automatically sized to match the current size.
```tsx
<Tabs size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Navigation">
<Tabs.Tab value="home" icon={<Home />}>Home</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings" icon={<SettingsCog />}>Settings</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications" icon={<Bell />}>Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Icon only
Omit the text children and pass only the icon prop for compact icon-only tabs. Always provide an aria-label on each tab for accessibility.
```tsx
<Tabs value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Navigation">
<Tabs.Tab value="home" icon={<Home />} aria-label="Home" />
<Tabs.Tab value="settings" icon={<SettingsCog />} aria-label="Settings" />
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications" icon={<Bell />} aria-label="Notifications" />
</Tabs>
```

### Segmented with badge
Pass a number or an object with content, color, variant, and pill to the badge prop. Badges render inline after the tab label inside the segmented container.
```tsx
<Tabs size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Filter">
<Tabs.Tab value="all" badge={{ content: 128, pill: true }}>All</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="unread" badge={{ content: 12, color: "info", pill: true }}>Unread</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="flagged" badge={{ content: 3, color: "danger", pill: true }}>Flagged</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline
Set variant="underline" for a minimal tab style with an animated line indicator under the active tab. No background container is rendered. iOS has no underline tabs: on a phone they are the segmented control of Overview, so this example has no Phone preview.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Sections">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline flush
Add flush with variant="underline" for minimal tabs where the indicator matches the text width exactly. No container border is rendered, and spacing between tabs uses gap instead of padding. On a phone these tabs are the segmented control of Overview, so this example has no Phone preview.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" flush value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Sections">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline block
Use block with the underline variant for full-width tabs that stretch evenly across the container. On a phone these tabs are the segmented control of Overview, so this example has no Phone preview.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" block value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Sections">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline with icons
Icons work with the underline variant the same way as with segmented. Use the icon prop on individual tabs. On a phone these tabs are the segmented control of Segmented with icons, so this example has no Phone preview.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Navigation">
<Tabs.Tab value="home" icon={<Home />}>Home</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings" icon={<SettingsCog />}>Settings</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications" icon={<Bell />}>Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Underline with badge
Badges are supported with the underline variant. Pass a simple value or an object with content, color, variant, and pill. On a phone these tabs are the segmented control of Segmented with badge, so this example has no Phone preview.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Filter">
<Tabs.Tab value="all" badge={{ content: 128, pill: true }}>All</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="unread" badge={{ content: 12, color: "info", pill: true }}>Unread</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="flagged" badge={{ content: 3, color: "danger", pill: true }}>Flagged</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Vertical segmented
Set orientation="vertical" to stack tabs vertically. The sliding thumb animates up and down. On a phone vertical tabs are an inset grouped list, as iOS lists a choice: 52px rows with the 17px label and a checkmark on the selected row instead of the thumb.
```tsx
<Tabs orientation="vertical" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Settings">
<Tabs.Tab value="account">Account</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="password">Password</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications">Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="display">Display</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Vertical underline
Combine variant="underline" with orientation="vertical" for a sidebar-style navigation pattern. The line indicator appears on the left side. On a phone both vertical variants are the list of Vertical segmented, so this example has no Phone preview.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" orientation="vertical" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Settings">
<Tabs.Tab value="account">Account</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="password">Password</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications">Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="display">Display</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Vertical underline with icons
Vertical underline tabs with icons provide a rich navigation experience commonly used in settings or admin panels.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" orientation="vertical" size="lg" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Navigation">
<Tabs.Tab value="home" icon={<Home />}>Home</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="settings" icon={<SettingsCog />}>Settings</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="notifications" icon={<Bell />}>Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Sizing
Both variants support the full 9-step size scale. The size prop controls the height, font size, icon size, and spacing of tabs. On a phone with touch.css horizontal tabs of either variant are the 44px glass segmented control of iOS, and vertical tabs are 52px list rows with the 17px label, at every size. The phone view shows each example at its default size, without the size and pill controls.
```tsx
<Tabs variant="underline" size="md" value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Demo tabs">
<Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="analytics">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
<Tabs.Tab value="reports">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Scrollable
When tabs overflow their container, they automatically become horizontally scrollable. The active tab scrolls into view smoothly. No extra prop is needed: just constrain the container width. A phone scrolls them the same way inside the glass capsule, as Safari's tab groups and Telegram's chat folders do, and each segment then takes the width of its label.
```tsx
<div className="flex w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Tabs value={tab} onChange={setTab} aria-label="Scrollable tabs">
  <Tabs.Tab value="1">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="2">Analytics</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="3">Reports</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="4">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="5">Members</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="6">Billing</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="7">Security</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="8">Integrations</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
</div>
```

### Overflow menu
With overflow="menu", the tabs that do not fit stay out of the row and move into a menu at its end, instead of a sideways scroll. When the active tab is a hidden one, the menu button shows its name and carries the selection. A tab's badge moves into the menu with it. overflowLabel sets the button's text (default "More"). Works for horizontal tabs without block.
```tsx
<div className="flex min-w-0 max-w-full w-[360px]">
<Tabs value={tab} onChange={setTab} variant="underline" overflow="menu" aria-label="Repository">
  <Tabs.Tab value="code">Code</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="issues" badge={12}>Issues</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="pulls" badge={3}>Pull requests</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="actions">Actions</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="projects">Projects</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="insights">Insights</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
</div>
```

## Tag Input
Input for entering multiple unique values as chip-style tokens, with suggestions and keyboard editing.
Import: import { TagInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/TagInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/tag-input
Props:
  - value (Tag[]) — Controlled value
  - defaultValue (Tag[]) — Uncontrolled initial tags
  - onChange ((tags: Tag[]) => void) — Change handler
  - id (string) — Id of the text input, so a label can target it with htmlFor
  - placeholder (string) — Input placeholder
  - validator ((value: string) => boolean) — Validates each tag when it is created; invalid tags shown in red
  - maxTags (number) — Maximum number of tags. At the limit the text input hides and a count shows below; the container then takes the tab stop, so arrow keys and Backspace still select and remove tags
  - rows (number) default: 1 — Min rows
  - size ('sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl') default: xl — Control height when rows=1; matches Input height of the same size
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully-rounded container and chips; matches Input/SelectControl pill
  - delimiters (string[]) default: [",", " "] — Characters that commit the current text as a tag
  - disabled (boolean) — Disables the input: tags cannot be added or removed, and pending text stays as typed
  - autoFocus (boolean) default: false — Focus on mount

### Overview
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[480px]">
<TagInput placeholder="Add a tag..." size="md" rows={1} pill={false} />
</div>

// Phone: the tags are the value of a row, under its label.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Tags">
  <TagInput variant="ghost" placeholder="Add a tag..." rows={1} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Inline filter row
When rows=1, TagInput matches the height of an Input or SelectControl of the same size, so it composes cleanly into horizontal filter rows. Toggle pill on both controls to keep the pair visually consistent.
```tsx
const FIELD_OPTIONS = [
{ value: "email", label: "Email" },
{ value: "name", label: "Name" },
{ value: "role", label: "Role" },
{ value: "team", label: "Team" },
{ value: "country", label: "Country" },
]

const [field, setField] = useState("email")
const [tags, setTags] = useState<Tag[]>([
{ value: "ada@plexui.com", valid: true },
{ value: "grace@plexui.com", valid: true },
])
const fieldLabel = FIELD_OPTIONS.find((option) => option.value === field)?.label ?? ""

// Desktop
return (
<div className="flex w-full max-w-2xl items-start gap-2">
  <Field label="Where" className="w-[160px] shrink-0">
    <Menu>
      <Menu.Trigger>
        <SelectControl size="md" pill={false} selected={!!field} className="w-full">
          {fieldLabel}
        </SelectControl>
      </Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content minWidth={160} onCloseAutoFocus={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
        {FIELD_OPTIONS.map((option) => (
          <Menu.CheckboxItem
            key={option.value}
            checked={field === option.value}
            onCheckedChange={() => setField(option.value)}
            indicatorVariant="ghost"
          >
            {option.label}
          </Menu.CheckboxItem>
        ))}
      </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  </Field>
  <Field label="Is in" className="flex-1">
    <TagInput size="md" pill={false} value={tags} onChange={setTags} placeholder="Add value, press Enter…" />
  </Field>
</div>
)

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row label="Where">
  {(control) => (
    <Menu>
      <Menu.Trigger>
        <SelectControl {...control} selected={!!field}>{fieldLabel}</SelectControl>
      </Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content minWidth={160} align="end">
        {FIELD_OPTIONS.map((option) => (
          <Menu.CheckboxItem
            key={option.value}
            checked={field === option.value}
            onCheckedChange={() => setField(option.value)}
            indicatorPosition="start"
            indicatorVariant="ghost"
          >
            {option.label}
          </Menu.CheckboxItem>
        ))}
      </Menu.Content>
    </Menu>
  )}
</Field>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Is in">
  <TagInput variant="ghost" value={tags} onChange={setTags} placeholder="Add a value" />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Suggestions
Combine TagInput with clickable buttons to let users add tags by clicking suggestions or typing manually. Suggestions disappear once selected.
```tsx
const SUGGESTIONS = ['React', 'TypeScript', 'Next.js', 'Tailwind CSS', 'Node.js', 'GraphQL', 'PostgreSQL', 'Redis', 'Docker', 'AWS'];

const [tags, setTags] = useState([
{ value: 'React', valid: true },
{ value: 'TypeScript', valid: true },
]);

const selectedValues = new Set(tags.map((t) => t.value));
const available = SUGGESTIONS.filter((s) => !selectedValues.has(s));

// Desktop
return (
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <TagInput value={tags} onChange={setTags} placeholder="Add a skill..." size="md" />
  {available.length > 0 && (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5">
      {available.map((s) => (
        <Button key={s} size="xs" color="secondary" variant="soft" pill={false}
          onClick={() => setTags([...tags, { value: s, valid: true }])}>
          {s}
        </Button>
      ))}
    </div>
  )}
</div>
);

// Phone: the suggestions follow the group.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Skills">
  <TagInput variant="ghost" value={tags} onChange={setTags} placeholder="Add a skill..." />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
{available.length > 0 && (
<FieldGroup title="Suggestions">
  {available.map((s) => (
    <Field row key={s} label={s}>
      <Button color="primary" variant="ghost" aria-label={`Add ${s}`} onClick={() => setTags([...tags, { value: s, valid: true }])}>
        Add
      </Button>
    </Field>
  ))}
</FieldGroup>
)}
```

## Text Link
Text link for inline internal and external links with router integration, color inheritance, underline control, and weight options.
Import: import { TextLink } from "@plexui/ui/components/TextLink"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/text-link
Props:
  - children (ReactNode) — Link content
  - href (string) — URL. An http:// or https:// URL is external
  - to (string | object) — Router link destination (internal); its type comes from the link component
  - primary (boolean) default: false — Primary color, no default underline
  - underline (boolean) default: true — Underline (default true unless primary)
  - forceExternal (boolean) — Force external link behavior
  - as (Component) — Link component (e.g. Next Link)
  - target (string) — Where to open the link. External links default to _blank
  - className (string) — Extra classes on the link

### Overview
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-4">
<TextLink href="#">Read more</TextLink>
<TextLink href="#" primary>External link <ArrowUpRight /></TextLink>
</div>
```

### Inline usage
```tsx
<p>
You can use the <TextLink href="#">responses endpoint</TextLink> to generate text. You can
either use the API directly from an HTTP client of your choice, or use one of the{" "}
<TextLink href="#">official SDKs</TextLink> for your preferred language.
</p>
```

### Default inheritance
By default, TextLink uses currentcolor inheritance and text-decoration: underline to create subtle visual differentiation from surrounding text. The hover effect is a dynamic deemphasis of the currentcolor, with some special cases for text-secondary and text-tertiary contexts.You can see this behavior by changing the text color context of the paragraph the links are in below:
```tsx
<p className="text-secondary">
You can use the <TextLink href="#">responses endpoint</TextLink> to generate text. You can
either use the API directly from an HTTP client of your choice, or use one of the{" "}
<TextLink href="#">official SDKs</TextLink> for your preferred language.
</p>
```

### Primary color
You can create a colorful link style with the primary prop, which uses color for visual differentiation.Primary links also remove the default underline treatment: pass underline to re-apply that style.
```tsx
<p>
Sample text with a <TextLink href="#" primary>primary link</TextLink>
</p>
```

### Underline
Links have an underlined aesthetic by default.Pass {'underline={false}'} to remove the underline from the link.
```tsx
<p className="text-secondary">
Sample text with a <TextLink href="#" underline={false}>subtle link</TextLink>
</p>
```

### External links
When external paths are provided, {''} will be used with {'target="_blank"'} and {'rel="noopener noreferrer"'} included by default. You can also compose icons along with the text to add visual indication.
```tsx
<TextLink href="#" primary underline>
External link <ArrowUpRight />
</TextLink>
```

### Font weight
Use the className prop to customize font weight.
```tsx
<TextLink href="#" className="font-semibold" underline={false}>
Contact support <ArrowRight />
</TextLink>
```

## Textarea
Multi-line text input that can grow with its content, with a size scale, autofill extension control, and invalid state styling.
Import: import { Textarea } from "@plexui/ui/components/Textarea"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/textarea
Props:
  - value (string | number) — Controlled value; uncontrolled when omitted
  - defaultValue (string | number) — Initial value when uncontrolled
  - onChange ((event: ChangeEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => void) — Called on every input
  - variant ("outline" | "soft" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Visual style of the textarea; ghost has no border and no fill, for a row or a container that frames it
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Control height for single-line equivalent
  - gutterSize ("2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Horizontal padding; defaults from size
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the textarea
  - readOnly (boolean) default: false — Make the textarea read-only
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark as invalid
  - allowAutofillExtensions (boolean) default: !!name — Allow autofill extensions
  - autoSelect (boolean) default: false — Select all contents when mounted
  - rows (number) default: 3 — Initial row count
  - autoResize (boolean) default: false — Grow/shrink with content
  - maxRows (number) — Max rows when autoResize; defaults to the larger of rows and 10
  - onAutofill (() => void) — Called when the browser autofills the textarea
  - className (string) — Applied to the container <div>
  - ref (Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>) — Ref to the <textarea>

### Overview
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Textarea placeholder="Enter text..." autoResize rows={3} />
</div>

// Phone: the textarea is the value of a row, under its label.
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Notes">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" placeholder="Add a note" autoResize rows={2} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Variants
Use variant to stylize the textarea. ghost has no border and no fill, for a field its container already frames. On Phone the row is the frame, so the textarea is ghost under the row's label.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6 w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Textarea placeholder="Enter text..." variant="outline" rows={3} />
<Textarea placeholder="Enter text..." variant="soft" rows={3} />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Note for the courier">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" placeholder="Gate code, floor, a safe place to leave it" autoResize rows={2} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Auto resize
Enable autoResize to automatically grow/shrink the textarea as the user types. Control the bounds with rows (initial height) and maxRows. On Phone the row grows with it.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("Line 1\nLine 2\nLine 3")

// Desktop
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Textarea value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)} placeholder="Type to grow..." autoResize rows={3} maxRows={8} />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Notes">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)} placeholder="Type to grow..." autoResize rows={3} maxRows={8} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Sizing
Sizing of the textarea is controlled with size and gutterSize props. size sets the textarea to a specific control height for single-line equivalent, and gutterSize sets the horizontal padding.Each size provides default values for gutterSize, as well as font-size and border-radius. Each of these values can be overridden independently.On Phone the row sets the type and insets, so a textarea in a row takes no size or gutterSize; rows sets its height. This example is desktop only, as Input's Sizing is.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Textarea placeholder="Write a message..." size="lg" gutterSize="md" />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Message">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" placeholder="Write a message..." rows={4} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Disabled
Use the disabled prop to disable the textarea, greying it out and preventing user interactions.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Textarea disabled defaultValue="Jane Doe" aria-label="Name" />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Notes">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" disabled defaultValue="Leave it at the front desk." autoResize rows={2} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Invalid
Use the invalid prop to mark the textarea as invalid. You decide how this state is removed, whether that's through onFocus, onChange, an onSubmit handler, etc.Default visual styles will be applied, based on the variant. Additionally, [data-invalid] is applied to the container for custom styling.On Phone the row is the frame, so the error is the errorMessage line under the row.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Textarea invalid placeholder="Invalid textarea" />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Reference" errorMessage={invalid ? "Keep it under 140 characters." : undefined}>
  <Textarea variant="ghost" defaultValue={reference} invalid={invalid} autoResize rows={2} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Auto select text
Pass autoSelect to select all text in the textarea, useful when pairing with other copy actions. This prop behaves like an imperative action when toggled and allows selection to change.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Textarea defaultValue="Toggle to auto select" autoSelect={false} aria-label="Notes" />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Notes">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" defaultValue="Toggle to auto select" autoSelect={false} autoResize rows={2} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

### Autofill extensions
By default, autofill extensions are prevented by Textarea. For the occasions where you want browser extensions to be present, pass allowAutofillExtensions to remove the disabling.When name is passed this value will default to true. Browser autofill extensions are a desktop matter: on iOS autofill comes from the system above the keyboard, so this example is desktop only.
```tsx
// Desktop
<div className="w-full min-w-0 max-w-[400px]">
<Textarea name="email" placeholder="Allowed" allowAutofillExtensions />
</div>

// Phone
<FieldGroup>
<Field row orientation="vertical" label="Address">
  <Textarea variant="ghost" name="address" autoComplete="street-address" placeholder="Allowed" allowAutofillExtensions autoResize rows={2} />
</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

## Tip
A short message that points out a feature people might miss, inside the page or anchored to a control, as TipKit tips do.
Import: import { Tip } from "@plexui/ui/components/Tip"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/tip
Props:
  - title (ReactNode) — The tip's title: what the feature is
  - description (ReactNode) — One or two sentences on how to use it
  - icon (ReactNode) — A symbol or image that leads the message
  - actions (ReactNode) — Buttons for the tip's actions, side by side below the message
  - mobileActions ("rows" | "buttons") default: "rows" — How the actions show at 767px and below: rows of text under a separator, or the buttons as given, each a full-width capsule
  - onClose (() => void) — Shows the Close button; called when it is clicked
  - arrowEdge ("top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right") — Draws an arrow at this edge, pointing at what the tip explains
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the tip
  - ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>) — Ref applied to the tip
  Tip.Popover:
    - open (boolean) — Shows the tip (controlled)
    - defaultOpen (boolean) default: false — Shows the tip at first (uncontrolled)
    - onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void) — Called when the tip opens or closes
    - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — The side of the control the tip shows on, turned when it does not fit
    - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — The alignment against the control
    - sideOffset (number) default: 4 — The distance from the control to the arrow's point, in pixels
    - closeButton (boolean) default: true — Shows the Close button
    - className (string) — CSS classes applied to the popover around the tip and its arrow

### Overview
An inline tip takes its place in the layout. A symbol leads the message in the secondary color; onClose shows Close in the trailing corner. On a phone the tip is the opaque card of a grouped list, so place it on a grouped background.
```tsx
const [shown, setShown] = useState(true)

{shown && (
<Tip
  icon={<Bookmark />}
  title="Save it for later"
  description="Bookmarked articles wait in your reading list, ready offline on every device."
  onClose={() => setShown(false)}
/>
)}
```

### Actions
Actions sit side by side below the message, each as wide as the others. Use small pill buttons, as the kit does. On a phone each action is a row of text in its color under a separator, one under another, starting under the text, as iOS cards show them.
```tsx
<Tip
icon={<Bell />}
title="Turn on notifications"
description="Get a message when someone replies to your post or mentions you."
actions={
  <>
    <Button color="primary" variant="soft" size="sm" pill>Not now</Button>
    <Button color="primary" size="sm" pill>Turn on</Button>
  </>
}
/>
```

### Buttons on a phone
With mobileActions="buttons" the actions keep their buttons on a phone: each is a capsule as wide as the tip under the message, 48px tall with a 17px label, in its own color and variant, as the iOS card in Settings that opens the Support app shows. Use it for a card that asks for a permission, with one soft primary button.
```tsx
<Tip
icon={<Bell />}
title="Get alerts"
description="Hear about severe weather where you are, even when the app is closed."
mobileActions="buttons"
actions={<Button color="primary" variant="soft" size="sm" pill>Turn on</Button>}
/>
```

### Arrow
With arrowEdge an inline tip points at what it explains with the kit's arrow, centered on that edge. The tip leaves room for the arrow on that side.
```tsx
<Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Filter">
<Filter />
</Button>
<Tip
arrowEdge="top"
title="Filter the list"
description="Show only the items from the last week, month or year."
/>
```

### Popover
A popover tip floats next to its control with an arrow that points at it. The control stays usable and keeps the focus. Close, Escape or a press outside the tip and its control closes it, through onOpenChange. Show it when the control appears; here the button shows it.
```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

<Tip.Popover
open={open}
onOpenChange={setOpen}
title="Filter the list"
description="Show only the items from the last week, month or year."
>
<Button color="secondary" variant="soft" onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
  <Filter />
  Filter
</Button>
</Tip.Popover>
```

## Toast
Toast notifications for transient feedback, with semantic variants, descriptions, action buttons, promise integration, and persistent toasts.
Import: import { Toaster, toast } from "@plexui/ui/components/Toast"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/toast
  Toaster:
    - position ("top-left" | "top-center" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-center" | "bottom-right") default: "top-center" — Where toasts anchor on the viewport
    - duration (number) default: 3000 — Default auto-dismiss duration in ms
    - offset (string | number | { top?; right?; bottom?; left? }) default: 32px — Distance from the viewport edge. Without a top or bottom edge here, the page's --toast-offset-top or --toast-offset-bottom sets it.
    - mobileOffset (string | number | { top?; right?; bottom?; left? }) default: 16px top and bottom, 14px at the sides, past the safe area — Gutter under 600px, where a toast fills the width between the side gutters. Explicit edges override their defaults; omitted edges keep them, and the page's --toast-mobile-offset-top or --toast-mobile-offset-bottom sets the top or bottom one.
    - gap (number) — Gap between stacked toasts in px

### Overview
On a phone a toast takes the corners, padding and text of an iOS notification banner, the system's own message at the top of the screen: 24px corners and 15pt text, with its buttons drawn as a medium phone Button, a 34px capsule in a 44px target. Under 600px it fills the width between 14px gutters past the safe area, as notifications do on an iOS phone; a compact toast keeps its own width. It stays a message of the page, with an opaque surface.
```tsx
toast("Inquiry ID copied")
```

### Variants
Semantic variants map to PlexUI's success / danger / warning / info tokens. No richColors is passed, so variants retheme automatically with data-theme.
```tsx
toast("Changes saved")
toast.success("Inquiry ID copied")
toast.error("Failed to assign owner")
toast.warning("Session expires in 2 minutes")
toast.info("New version available")
```

### Description
```tsx
toast("Changes saved", {
description: "Your profile is live for everyone on the team.",
})
```

### Action
```tsx
toast("Message sent", {
description: "Delivered to #design channel.",
action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => toast.success("Message recalled") },
})
```

### Promise
Use toast.promise to tie a single toast to an async operation. The toast shows a loading state, then swaps to success or error. Here saveProfile() resolves with {"{ name: \"Profile\" }"} after 1.5 seconds.
```tsx
toast.promise(saveProfile(), {
loading: "Saving…",
success: (data) => `${data.name} saved`,
error: "Save failed",
})
```

### Long content
```tsx
toast("Your deployment is still running", {
description:
  "This is a long message to show how the toast handles multi-line content without clipping or awkward wrapping. The title and description should both wrap cleanly.",
})
```

### Compact
Spread compact into any toast(...) options for a centered-text layout. On a desktop a toast shrinks to its content anyway; on a phone, where a toast fills the width, a compact one keeps the width of its content. Both center its text.
```tsx
import { toast, compact } from "@plexui/ui/components/Toast"

toast.success("Inquiry ID copied", compact)
```

### Persistent
Pass duration: Infinity for toasts that stay open until the user acts on them. There are no close (×) affordances, so put a labelled action on the toast so dismissal is intentional and keyboard-accessible. An error that waits like this is an alert (see Screen readers).
```tsx
const id = toast("Backup scheduled for 2:00 AM UTC", {
description: "This stays open until you dismiss it.",
duration: Infinity,
action: { label: "Dismiss", onClick: () => toast.dismiss(id) },
})
```

## Toolbar
"The top and bottom bars of a phone screen: navigation, a title, a search field and actions over the content. Desktop layouts have their own composition, so a toolbar never renders from 768px up."
Import: import { Toolbar } from "@plexui/ui/components/Toolbar"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/toolbar
Props:
  - placement ("top" | "bottom") default: "top" — Top bar with 44px targets, or bottom bar with 48px targets
  - titleStyle ("inline" | "large" | "compact-large" | "compact-medium") default: "inline" — Size and place of Toolbar.Title in a top bar
  - titleAlign ("center" | "start") default: "center" — Alignment of an inline title. Large and compact titles always start at the leading edge
  - background ("soft" | "hard" | "glass" | "solid") default: "glass" at the top, "soft" at the bottom — How the bar meets the content scrolled under it, see Background. "edge" is the earlier name of "soft"
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the bar
  Toolbar.Title:
    - subtitle (ReactNode) default: — — Second, smaller line below the title
    - as ("h1" | "h2" | "h3") default: "h1" — Heading level of the title

### Overview
Leading and trailing items take 44px targets; the title is centered across the whole width. Scroll the content: the canvas color fades out over the rows under the bar, and the glass starts to cast a shadow.
```tsx
<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <NavigationButton action="back" />
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Title>Orders</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <NavigationButton action="close" />
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
</Page>
```

### Titles
titleStyle sets the size and place of the title: inline in the row of controls, large on a row of its own below them (on a page it scrolls up with the content under the controls, which then show it inline), and compact-large or compact-medium at the leading edge of the row. subtitle adds a second line. titleAlign="start" puts an inline title after the leading items.
```tsx
<Toolbar titleStyle="large">
<Toolbar.Leading>
  <NavigationButton action="back" />
</Toolbar.Leading>
<Toolbar.Title subtitle="24 orders">Orders</Toolbar.Title>
<Toolbar.Trailing>
  <NavigationButton action="confirm" />
</Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Group
Toolbar.Group puts related actions in one capsule. A single action keeps a capsule of its own. A ButtonGroup in a toolbar is the same capsule. Name each icon button with aria-label.
```tsx
<Toolbar>
<Toolbar.Leading>
  <NavigationButton action="close" />
</Toolbar.Leading>
<Toolbar.Trailing>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Details"><InfoCircle /></Button>
  <Toolbar.Group aria-label="Order actions">
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Translate"><Translate /></Button>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
  </Toolbar.Group>
</Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Search
Toolbar.Content fill stretches a search field between the leading and trailing items. The field takes the row height and the material of the bar buttons.
```tsx
<Toolbar>
<Toolbar.Content fill>
  <Input variant="soft" pill placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search orders" startAdornment={<SearchSm />} />
</Toolbar.Content>
<Toolbar.Trailing>
  <NavigationButton action="close" aria-label="Close search" />
</Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
```

### Bottom
placement="bottom" sets the bar at the bottom of the page with 48px targets and the device's bottom safe area. Toolbar.Content centers a main action; with fill a search field or a single action takes the whole row. The 48px items stand 28px from the sides and above the home indicator, 12px apart, and a bottom bar draws no band: the content runs under and around its glass, as in iOS 26 Mail and Contacts. A search field holds SearchSm, set in Regular; a plus next to it takes iconSize="sm", as Contacts draws it smaller than the other symbols. The page content scrolls under both bars.
```tsx
<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Title>Orders</Toolbar.Title>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
<Toolbar placement="bottom">
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Filter"><Filter /></Button>
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Content>
    <Button color="primary" pill>New order</Button>
  </Toolbar.Content>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Search"><Search /></Button>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
</Page>

<Toolbar placement="bottom">
<Toolbar.Content fill>
  <Input variant="soft" pill placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search orders" startAdornment={<SearchSm />} />
</Toolbar.Content>
<Toolbar.Trailing>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill iconSize="sm" aria-label="New order"><PlusLg /></Button>
</Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>

<Toolbar placement="bottom">
<Toolbar.Content fill>
  <Button color="primary" pill block><Plus /> New order</Button>
</Toolbar.Content>
</Toolbar>
```

### Background
background sets how a bar meets the content scrolled under it. glass, the default of a top bar, is a translucent, blurred bar with a hairline. soft, the default of a bottom bar, is the scroll edge effect of iOS 26 and draws no line: a top bar with a title covers the content under its controls with the canvas color and fades it out past them over a light blur, while a top bar of controls alone on a page covers only the status bar, and a bottom bar on a page leaves the content clear under and around its controls, as native iOS 26 does (Contacts, Notes, Mail); each glass control stands out by itself. A Sheet's bottom bar fades its content into the panel. hard is an opaque bar of the canvas color with a line. solid is an opaque bar with no line. Glass and hard show themselves once content is under the bar: under the top bar after the content has scrolled, over the bottom bar while it continues below. Page.Header, Page.Footer, the bars of a Sheet and TabBar take the same values.
```tsx
<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar background="hard">
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <NavigationButton action="back" />
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Title>Orders</Toolbar.Title>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
<Toolbar placement="bottom" background="hard">
  <Toolbar.Content>
    <Button color="primary" pill>New order</Button>
  </Toolbar.Content>
</Toolbar>
</Page>
```

### Disabled
A disabled bar button keeps its glass capsule and draws its symbol or label in the tertiary label color, as the iOS 26 bar buttons do. Inside Toolbar.Group the capsule belongs to the group, so the enabled actions next to it keep their look. A prominent action, NavigationButton action="confirm" or a solid primary Button, drops its color for a gray capsule, with a white label in light and a dim one in dark. Cancel and More stay enabled.
```tsx
<Page surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" pill>Cancel</Button>
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Title>New order</Toolbar.Title>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <NavigationButton action="confirm" disabled />
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
<Page.Content>...</Page.Content>
<Toolbar placement="bottom">
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Filter" disabled><Filter /></Button>
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Content>
    <Button color="primary" pill disabled>Place order</Button>
  </Toolbar.Content>
  <Toolbar.Trailing>
    <Toolbar.Group aria-label="Order actions">
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="Translate" disabled><Translate /></Button>
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform pill aria-label="More"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
    </Toolbar.Group>
  </Toolbar.Trailing>
</Toolbar>
</Page>
```

### Sheet
In a Sheet the toolbar sits below the grabber and takes the place of the Sheet's own bar and Close button on a phone. Keep Dialog.Header with Dialog.Title: it still names the dialog for assistive technology, and it is the header from 768px up.
```tsx
<Dialog.Content mobileVariant="sheet" surface="grouped">
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Leading>
    <Dialog.Close>
      <NavigationButton action="close" />
    </Dialog.Close>
  </Toolbar.Leading>
  <Toolbar.Title>Orders</Toolbar.Title>
</Toolbar>
<Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Title>Orders</Dialog.Title>
</Dialog.Header>
<Dialog.Body>...</Dialog.Body>
</Dialog.Content>
```

## Tooltip
Brief informative text shown on hover or focus, for any trigger element, with conditional enabling and a compact variant.
Import: import { Tooltip } from "@plexui/ui/components/Tooltip"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/tooltip
Props:
  - children (ReactElement) — The trigger: a single element. Wrap plain text in Tooltip.TriggerDecorator
  - content (ReactNode) — Tooltip content (null = no tooltip)
  - compact (boolean) default: false — Short 1-3 word tooltips, inverse styling
  - interactive (boolean) default: false — Content is interactive, stays open when hovered
  - maxWidth (number | "none") default: 300 — Max width of tooltip
  - openDelay (number) default: 150 — Delay before showing (ms)
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "top" — Preferred side
  - sideOffset (number) default: 5 — Distance from trigger
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Alignment
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 — Alignment offset
  - gutterSize ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Content padding
  - contentClassName (string) — Class for tooltip content
  - forceOpen (boolean) — Force open or closed
  - preventUnintentionalClickToClose (true) — Keeps the tooltip open when the trigger is clicked right after it opened

### Overview
```tsx
<Tooltip content="This is additional context that appears when the trigger is hovered or focused">
<Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>Simple text with tooltip</Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>
</Tooltip>
```

### Different triggers
Tooltip provides an optional component, Tooltip.TriggerDecorator, to help create accessible tooltip triggers. However, any component can be used as a trigger.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
<Tooltip content="Tooltip on button">
  <Button color="primary" size="lg">Sample button</Button>
</Tooltip>
<Tooltip content="Tooltip on span">
  <span>Inaccessible trigger</span>
</Tooltip>
</div>
```

### Conditionally enabled
Sometimes a tooltip should only be disabled under certain conditions, such as when a component is disabled, providing more context as to why that is. Below is an example of how to do this by conditionally passing in null content.
```tsx
<Tooltip
content={disabled ? "This action is disabled for reasons" : null}
>
<Button color="primary" size="lg" disabled={disabled}>
  Sample button
</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

### Compact tooltips
Compact tooltips are designed for short, 1-3 word tooltips with inverted styling. They feature minimal padding, a dark background with white text, and no box shadows. Use {'compact={true}'} for brief status messages.
```tsx
<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard" compact>
<Button color="secondary" variant="ghost" size="md" aria-label="Copy to clipboard"><Copy /></Button>
</Tooltip>
```
